sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the eye, 0.1 cun medial to the inner canthus of the eye, in the depression between the superomedial parts of the inner canthus of the eye and the medial wall of the orbit. It is in the depression superomedial to the lachrymal duct.

2. Jingming is on the face, in the depression between the superomedial parts of the inner canthus of the eye and the medial wall of the orbit.
Note: When the eye is closed, BL1 is located in the depression 0.1 B-cun superior and medial to the inner canthus of the eye. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Crossing point with Governor vessel, Yin heel vessel, Yang heel vessel, BL, ST and SI meridian. Entry point. Exit point(yin heel vessel).

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Red and sore eyes, acute and chronic conjunctivitis, optic neuritis, inflammation of the ora serrata, astigmatism, myopia, hypermetropia, atrophy of the optic nerve, night blindness, color blindness, early stages of cataracts, glaucoma, keratoleukoma, pterygium, excessive tearing on exposure to wind, opacity of cornea.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the nape of the neck at the same level as the superior border of the spinous process of the 2nd cervical vertebra in the depression at the lateral border of the trapezius muscle. It is 1.5 cun lateral to GV15. Another measurement says it is 0.5 cun superior to the posterior hairline, and 1.3 cun lateral to the posterior median line(GV15). Same horizontal position as GV15 and BL10.

2. Tianzhu is in the posterior region of the neck, at the same level as the superior border of the spinous process of the second cervical vertebra (C2), in the depression lateral to the trapezius muscle. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Windows of Heaven points(celestial pillar).

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Hysteria, seizures, infantile convulsions, dizzy and painful head, occipital headache, eye diseases, nasal congestion, swelling of the larynx, pharyngitis, pain and stiffness and soreness in back of neck, strengthens the lower back.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the upper back at the same level as the inferior border of the spinous process of the 1st thoracic vertebra, 1.5 cun lateral to the posterior median line. It is at the midpoint between GV13 and SI14, 1.5 cun lateral to GV13. Same horizontal position as GV13, BL11 and SI14.

2. Dazhu is in the upper back region, at the same level as the inferior border of the spinous process of the first thoracic vertebra (T1), 1.5 B-cun lateral to the posterior median line. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Eight Meeting points(bones). Meeting point with SI, TB, GB and BL meridian. Points of the Four Seas(sea of blood).

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Tidal fevers, common cold, headache and chills, fullness in the chest, throat blockage, bronchitis, pleurisy, pneumonia, opens the channel, infantile convulsions, benefits the bones and joints, neck and back pain, stiffness along the spine, low back pain, pain and inability to bend the knee, numbness in the limbs, arthritis, tuberculosis of the bones.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the upper back at the same level as the inferior border of the spinous process of the 2nd thoracic vertebra, 1.5 cun lateral to the posterior median line, and 1.5 cun medial to BL41. Same horizontal position as BL12 and BL41.

2. Fengmen is in the upper back region, at the same level as the inferior border of the spinous process of the second thoracic vertebra (T2), 1.5 B-cun lateral to the posterior median line. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Crossing point with Governor vessel and BL meridian.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Asthma, bronchitis, pleurisy, pneumonia, common cold, cough due to cold, headache, benefits the nose, congested nose, stiff neck, shoulder strain, pain in the chest and back, opens the channel, vomiting, belching, urticaria.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the upper back at the same level as the inferior border of the spinous process of the 3rd thoracic vertebra, 1.5 cun lateral to the posterior median line, and 1.5 cun lateral to GV12. Same horizontal position as GV12, BL13 and BL42.

2. Feishu is in the upper back region, at the same level as the inferior border of the spinous process of the third thoracic vertebra (T3), 1.5 B-cun lateral to the posterior median line. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Transport point(lung).

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Asthma, wheezing, cough, throat blockage, bronchitis, fullness in chest and difficult breathing, pleurisy, pulmonary TB, pneumonia, spontaneous sweating, night sweats, afternoon fever, spitting blood, goiter, opens the channel, insanity, convulsions, steaming bones syndrome.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the upper back at the same level as the inferior border of the spinous process of the 4th thoracic vertebra, 1.5 cun lateral to the posterior median line, and 1.5 cun medial to BL43. Same horizontal position as BL14 and BL43.

2. Jueyinshu is in the upper back region, at the same level as the inferior border of the spinous process of the fourth thoracic vertebra (T4), 1.5 B-cun lateral to the posterior median line. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Transport point(pericardium).

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Vomiting, intercostal neuralgia, rheumatic heart disease, palpitation, stuffy chest.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the upper back at the same level as the inferior border of the spinous process of the 5th thoracic vertebra, 1.5 cun lateral to the posterior median line, and 1.5 cun lateral to GV11. Same horizontal position as GV11, BL15 and BL44. Another measurement says it is the same horizontal position as SI11, but that is currently being disputed.

2. Xinshu is in the upper back region, at the same level as the inferior border of the spinous process of the fifth thoracic vertebra (T5), 1.5 B-cun lateral to the posterior median line. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Transport point(heart).

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Atrial fibrillation, tachycardia, irritability and depressed feeling in the chest and heart, rheumatic heart disease, unbinds the chest and removes blood stasis, chest pain, intercostal neuralgia, coughing blood, vomiting without eating, hysteria, psychosis, mania, epilepsy, seizures, neurasthenia, spermatorrhea, chills and fever, tidal fevers, night sweats, hot palms and soles of feet.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the upper back at the same level as the inferior border of the spinous process of the 6th thoracic vertebra, 1.5 cun lateral to the posterior median line, and 1.5 cun lateral to GV10. Same horizontal position as GV10, BL16 and BL45.

2. Dushu is in the upper back region, level with the inferior border of the spinous process of the sixth thoracic vertebra (T6), 1.5 B-cun lateral to the posterior median line. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Spasms of the diaphragm, hiccup, hot or cold chest pain, endocarditis and pericarditis, mastitis, abdominal pain, intestinal noises, alopecia, pruritis, psoriasis(heat lodged in GV).

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the upper back at the same level as the inferior border of the spinous process of the 7th thoracic vertebra, 1.5 cun lateral to the posterior median line, and 1.5 cun lateral to GV9. Same horizontal position as GV9, BL17 and BL46.

2. Geshu is in the upper back region, at the same level as the inferior border of the spinous process of the seventh thoracic vertebra (T7), 1.5 B-cun lateral to the posterior median line.
Note: The inferior angle of the scapula is at the same level as the spinous process of the seventh thoracic vertebra (T7). [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Eight Meeting points(blood). Transport point(diaphragm).

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Cools blood-heat, stops bleeding, removes blood stasis, nourishes and harmonises blood, anemia, chronic hemorrhagic disorders, coughing or spitting blood, TB of lymph glands, belching, urticaria, hot sensation in the bones, chills and fever, night sweats, hypersomnia, afternoon fever, measles, lassitude, regulates the diaphragm, spasms of the diaphragm, nervous vomiting, constriction of the esophagus, difficulty swallowing, abdominal distension or lumps, stomach cancer.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the upper back at the same level as the inferior border of the spinous process of the 9th thoracic vertebra, 1.5 cun lateral to the posterior median line, and 1.5 cun lateral to GV8. Same horizontal position as GV8, BL18 and BL47.

2. Ganshu is in the upper back region, at the same level as the inferior border of the spinous process of the ninth thoracic vertebra (T9), 1.5 B-cun lateral to the posterior median line. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Transport point(liver).

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Neurasthenia, jaundice, chronic and acute hepatitis, cholecystitis, intercostal neuralgia, pain of lumps in the chest and abdomen, stomach diseases, nosebleed, spitting blood, irregular menstruation, night blindness, any eye diseasesmental disorders, epilepsy, backache, epistaxis.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the upper back at the same level as the inferior border of the spinous process of the 10th thoracic vertebra, 1.5 cun lateral to the posterior median line, and 1.5 cun lateral to GV7. Same horizontal position as GV7, BL19 and BL48.

2. Danshu is in the upper back region, at the same level as the inferior border of the spinous process of the tenth thoracic vertebra (T10), 1.5 B-cun lateral to the posterior median line. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Transport point(gall bladder).

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Soreness in the chest and ribs, pain in the flanks, abdominal distension, gastritis, bitter taste in the mouth, dry or bilious vomiting, yellowish eyes, jaundice, hepatitis, cholecystitis, roundworm in the bile duct, chills, headache, sore throat, sciatica(main), swelling of axillary lymph glands, TB of the lymph glands, hot sensation in the bones and fever(deficient yin), sperm in the urine.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the eyebrow in the depression at the medial end of the eyebrow on the supraorbital notch. It is 0.5 cun lateral to EX-HN1.

2. Cuanzhu is on the head, in the depression at the medial end of the eyebrow.
Note: A depression, the frontal notch, can often be palpated on the medial end of the eyebrow directly superior to BL1. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Dizziness, headache, acute conjunctivitis, eyes swollen and sore, excessive lacrimation, keratoleukoma, myopia, expels external pathogenic factors such as wind, clears heat, facial paralysis, spasms of the eyelid, infantile convulsions, insanity.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the upper back at the same level as the inferior border of the spinous process of the 11th thoracic vertebra, 1.5 cun lateral to the posterior median line, and 1.5 cun lateral to GV6. Same horizontal position as GV6, BL20 and BL49.

2. Pishu is in the upper back region, at the same level as the inferior border of the spinous process of the eleventh thoracic vertebra (T11), 1.5 B-cun lateral to the posterior median line. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Transport point(spleen).

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Jaundice, hepatitis, gastritis, enteritis, constriction of the esophagus inhibiting swallowing, nervous vomiting, indigestion, abdominal distension, prolapsed stomach, lumps in the chest and abdomen, enlargement of the liver and spleen, diarrhea, dysentery, chronic urticaria, nourishes blood, anemia, chronic hemorrhagic diseases, transforms dampness, edema, prolapsed uterus, weakness or heaviness in the limbs.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the upper back at the same level as the inferior border of the spinous process of the 12th thoracic vertebra, 1.5 cun lateral to the posterior median line, and 1.5 cun medial to BL50. Same horizontal position as BL21 and BL50.

2. Weishu is in the upper back region, at the same level as the inferior border of the spinous process of the twelfth thoracic vertebra (T12), 1.5 B-cun lateral to the posterior median line. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Transport point(stomach).

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Loss of appetite, difficulty swallowing, regurgitant vomiting, infant vomiting milk, hepatitis, gastritis, stomachache, abdominal pain from cold in stomach, prolapsed stomach, gastric distension, pancreatitis, ulcer, enteritis, diarrhea, anorexia, borborygmus, nausea, edema, insomnia, pain along the spine.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the lower back at the same level as the inferior border of the spinous process of the 1st lumbar vertebra, 1.5 cun lateral to the posterior median line, and 1.5 cun lateral to GV5. Same horizontal position as GV5, BL22 and BL51.

2. Sanjiaoshu is in the lumbar region, at the same level as the inferior border of the spinous process of the first lumbar vertebra (L1), 1.5 B-cun lateral to the posterior median line. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Transport point(triple energizer).

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Neurasthenia, dizziness and headache, vomiting, indigestion, abdominal distension and intestinal noises, borborygmus, gastritis, enteritis, jaundice, diarrhea, ascites, urinary retention, nephritis, enuresis, edema, low back pain.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the lower back at the same level as the inferior border of the spinous process of the 2nd lumbar vertebra, 1.5 cun lateral to the posterior median line, and 1.5 cun lateral to GV4. Same horizontal position as GV4, BL23 and BL52.

2. Shenshu is in the lumbar region, at the same level as the inferior border of the spinous process of the second lumbar vertebra (L2), 1.5 B-cun lateral to the posterior median line. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Transport point(kidneys).

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Anemia, tidal fevers, seizures, infantile paralysis(polio), alopecia, deafness, tinnitus, blurring of vision, dizziness, bronchial asthma, emaciation and thirst, renal colic, deficient kidneys, nephroptosis, nephritis, blood in urine, edema, impotence, spermatorrhea, loss of sperm, irregular menstruation, injury to soft tissues of lower back, low back pain and cold knees, weakness of the knee, diarrhea.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the lower back at the same level as the inferior border of the spinous process of the 3rd lumbar vertebra, 1.5 cun lateral to the posterior median line.

2. Qihaishu is in the lumbar region, at the same level as the inferior border of the spinous process of the third lumbar vertebra (L3), 1.5 B-cun lateral to the posterior median line. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Functional uterine bleeding, hemorrhoids, asthma, dysmenorrhea, irregular menstruation, low back pain, pain in the lumbar vertebrae, paralysis of lower limbs.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the lower back at the same level as the inferior border of the spinous process of the 4th lumbar vertebra, 1.5 cun lateral to the posterior median line, and 1.5 cun lateral to GV3. Same horizontal position as GV3 and BL25.

2. Dachangshu is in the lumbar region, at the same level as the inferior border of the spinous process of the fourth lumbar vertebra (L4), 1.5 B-cun lateral to the posterior median line. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Transport point(large intestine).

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Abdominal distension and intestinal noises, enteritis, difficult or painful urination or defecation, constipation, diarrhea, dysentery, muscular atrophy, low back pain or sprain, pain in sacroiliac joint.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the lower back at the same level as the inferior border of the spinous process of the 5th lumbar vertebra, 1.5 cun lateral to the posterior median line.

2. Guanyuanshu is in the lumbar region, at the same level as the inferior border of the spinous process of the fifth lumbar vertebra (L5), 1.5 B-cun lateral to the posterior median line. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Anemia, emaciation and thirst, diabetes, chronic peritonitis, chronic enteritis, cystitis, frequent or painful urination, diarrhea, enuresis, sciatica, low back pain.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the sacral region at the same level as the 1st posterior sacral foramen, 1.5 cun lateral to the median sacral crest. Same horizontal position as BL31 and BL27.

 2. Xiaochangshu is in the sacral region, at the same level as the first posterior sacral foramen, and 1.5 B-cun lateral to the median sacral crest.
		Note: At the same level as BL31. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Transport point(small intestine).

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Thirst, dry mouth, peritonitis, enteritis, colic, constipation, blood in urine, dark or red urine, dysentery, nocturnal emission, enuresis, morbid leukorrhea, incontinence, vaginal discharge, sermatorrhea, low back pain, pain in the sacroiliac joints and diseases of the sacroiliac joints.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the sacral region at the same level as the 2nd posterior sacral foramen, 1.5 cun lateral to the median sacral crest. Same horizontal position as BL32, BL28, and BL53.

2. Pangguangshu is in the sacral region, at the same level as the second posterior sacral foramen, and 1.5 B-cun lateral to the median sacral crest.
Note: At the same level as BL32. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Transport point(bladder).

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Diabetes, constipation, diarrhea, enuresis, frequent urination, diseases of the urogenital system, dark and rough-flowing urine, incontinence, swelling and pain in the genitals, loss of sperm, pain in the lumbosacral region, sciatica.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the sacral region at the same level as the 3rd posterior sacral foramen, 1.5 cun lateral to the median sacral crest. Same horizontal position as BL33 and BL29.
2. Zhonglushu is in the sacral region, at the same level as the third posterior sacral foramen, and 1.5 B-cun lateral to the median sacral crest.
Note: At the same level as BL33. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Enteritis, lumbosacral pain, sciatica, dysentery, hernia, stiffness and pain of the lower back.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the front of the head, one third of GV24 when connecting GB15(0.5 cun superior to the anterior hairline in the vertical line from the center of the pupil) to GV24 and dividing it into three. Same horizontal position as GV24, BL3, BL4, GB15, GB13 and ST8.

2. Meichong is on the head, superior to the frontal notch, 0.5 B-cun superior to the anterior hairline.
Note: Midway between GV24 and BL4. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Seizures, headache, vertigo, nasal obstruction, occluded nose, giddiness.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the sacral region at the same level as the 4th posterior sacral foramen, 1.5 cun lateral to the median sacral crest. Same horizontal position as GV2, BL34, BL30 and BL54.

2. Baihuanshu is in the sacral region, at the same level as the fourth posterior sacral foramen, and 1.5 B-cun lateral to the median sacral crest.
Note: 1.5 B-cun lateral to the sacral hiatus, at the same level as BL34. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Painful defecation or urination, colic, prolapse of the rectum, anal diseases, excessive uterine bleeding, loss of sperm, morbid leukorrhea, irregular menstruation, vaginal discharge, endometritis, cold sensation and pain of the lower back, pain in the lumbosacral region, sciatica, debility of the leg and knee, sequelae of infantile paralysis, tenesmus.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the sacral region at the 1st posterior sacral foramen. Same horizontal position as BL31 and BL27.

2. Shangliao is in the sacral region, in the first posterior sacral foramen.
Note: The first posterior sacral foramen is palpated in the depression, moving superiorly from BL32. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Crossing point with GB and BL meridian.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Paralysis of lower limbs, sequelae of infantile paralysis, diseases of the lumbosacral joint, sciatica, peritonitis, dysuria, constipation, orchitis, irregular menstruation, leukorrhea, prolapse of the uterus, inducing labor.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the sacral region at the 2nd posterior sacral foramen. Same horizontal position as BL32, BL28 and BL53.

2. Ciliao is in the sacral region, in the second posterior sacral foramen.
Note: The second posterior sacral foramen is located in the depression, midway between the posterior superior iliac spine and the spinous process of the second sacral vertebra. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Diseases of the lumbosacral joint, sciatica, paralysis of lower limbs, muscular atrophy and pain, sequelae of infantile paralysis, peritonitis, hernia, enuresis, dysuria, nocturnal emission, orchitis, impotence, irregular menstruation, leukorrhea, dysmenorrhea, inducing labor.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the sacral region at the 3rd posterior sacral foramen. Same horizontal position as BL33 and BL29.

2. Zhongliao is in the sacral region, in the third posterior sacral foramen.
Note: The third posterior sacral foramen is located in the first depression, moving downward from BL32. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Crossing point with GB, LR and BL meridian.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Paralysis of lower limbs, sequelae of infantile paralysis, diseases of the lumbosacral joint, sciatica, peritonitis, dysuria, constipation, diarrhea, orchitis, irregular menstruation, leukorrhea, prolapse of the uterus, inducing labor.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the sacral region at the 4th posterior sacral foramen. Same horizontal position as GV2, BL34, BL30 and BL54.

2. Xialiao is in the sacral region, in the fourth posterior sacral foramen.
Note: The fourth posterior sacral foramen is located in the second depression, moving downward from BL32, at the same level as the sacral hiatus. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Crossing point with GB, LR and BL meridian.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Paralysis of lower limbs, sequelae of infantile paralysis, diseases of the lumbosacral joint, sciatica, peritonitis, lower abdominal pain, constipation, dysuria, orchitis, irregular menstruation, leukorrhea, inducing labor.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the coccyx region of the buttocks at the end of the coccyx on both sides, 0.5 cun lateral to the extremity of the coccyx. In prone position or in knee-chest position, it is in the depression at the lateral end of the coccyx.

2. Huiyang is in the buttock region, 0.5 B-cun lateral to the extremity of the coccyx.
Note: The subject may be in prone position or knee-chest position. BL35 is located at the soft depression lateral to the extremity of the coccyx. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Dysentery, bloody stools, diarrhea, hemorrhoids, impotence, morbid leukorrhea, pain in lower back during menstruation.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the buttock region at the midpiont of the gluteal crease.

2. Chengfu is in the buttock region, at the midpoint of the gluteal fold. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Low back pain, sciatica, pain in the lower back and leg, paralysis of lower extremity, swelling of the coccyx, retention of urine, difficulty in urination, constipation, hemorrhoids, pain in the genitals.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the posterior aspect of the thigh, 6 cun inferior to the gluteal fold, between the biceps femoris muscle and the semitendinosus muscle, and 6 cun inferior to the midpoint of the line connecting BL36 and BL40.

2. Yinmen is on the posterior aspect of the thigh, between the biceps femoris and the semitendinosus muscles, 6 B-cun inferior to the gluteal fold.
Note 1: In the prone position, the semitendinosus and the biceps femoris muscles are more distinct when the knee is flexed against resistance. In addition, it is easier to find the two muscles with internal and external rotation of the hip.
Note 2: 1 B-cun superior to the midpoint of the line connecting BL36 with BL40. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Occipital headache, paralysis, hemiplegia, herniated disc, low back pain that inhibits flexion and extension, sciatica, distension on the lateral side of thigh, paralysis of lower limb.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the posterolateral aspect of the knee, 1 cun superior to the popliteal crease, at the medial aspect to the biceps femoris tendon.

2. Fuxi is on the posterior aspect of the knee, just medial to the biceps femoris tendon, 1 B-cun proximal to the popliteal crease.
Note: With the knee in slight flexion, BL38 is located medial to the biceps femoris tendon, 1 B-cun proximal to BL39. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Numbness of the gluteal and femoral regions, paralysis along the lateral aspect of lower extremities, acute gastroenteritis, cystitis, constipation.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the posterolateral aspect of the knee at the popliteal crease, medial border of the biceps femoris tendon, and 1 cun lateral to the BL40.

2. Weiyang is on the posterolateral aspect of the knee, just medial to the biceps femoris tendon in the popliteal crease.
Note: The biceps femoris tendon is more prominent when the knee is slightly flexed. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Lower Sea points of the Six Bowels(triple energizer).

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Low back pain extending to the abdomen, fullness in the chest or abdomen, spasm of gastrocnemius muscle, cystitis, nephritis, loss or retention of urine, chyluria(milky urine), dysuria, constipation, edema, cramp of the leg and foot.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the front of the head, 0.5 cun superior to the anterior hairline, and 1.5 cun lateral to the anterior median line. It is one third of GV24 when connecting GV24 to ST8 by 4.5 cun as an arching shape and dividing it into three. It is 1.5 cun lateral to the GV24, and 3 cun medial to the ST8. Same horizontal position as GV24, BL3, BL4, GB15, GB13 and ST8.

2. Qucha is on the head, 0.5 B-cun superior to the anterior hairline, 1.5 B-cun lateral to the anterior median line.
Note: At the junction of the medial one third and lateral two thirds of the line connecting GV24 with ST8. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Headache, occluded nose, nosebleed, epistaxis, blurring and failing of vision.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the posterior aspect of the knee at the midpoint of the popliteal crease, between the biceps femoris tendon and the semitendinosus tendon.

2. Weizhong is on the posterior aspect of the knee, at the midpoint of the popliteal crease. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Sea point. Earth point. Lower Sea points of the Six Bowels(bladder). Ma Dan-Yang Twelve Heavenly Star points. Four Command points(lumbar region). Six Command points(lumbar region).

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Tidal fevers, seizures, coma due to stroke, hemiplegia, heat exhaustion, vomiting, acute gastroenteritis, twisting pain in the chest and abdomen, diarrhea, stiffness and pain of the lumbar spine, low back pain, sciatica, arthritis of the knee, paralysis of lower limb, spasm of gastrocnemius muscle, leprosy, erysipelas, carbuncles.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the upper back at the same level as the inferior border of the spinous process of the 2nd thoracic vertebra, 3 cun lateral to the posterior median line, and 1.5 cun lateral BL12. Same horizontal position as BL12 and BL41.

2. Fufen is in the upper back region, at the same level as the inferior border of the spinous process of the second thoracic vertebra (T2), 3 B-cun lateral to the posterior median line.
Note: BL41 and BL12 are located at the same level as the inferior border of the spinous process of the second thoracic vertebra (T2). [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Crossing point with SI and BL meridian.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Soreness and pain of the shoulder, neck, and back regions, numbness in the elbow and arm.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the upper back at the same level as the inferior border of the spinous process of the 3rd thoracic vertebra, 3 cun lateral to the posterior median line, and 3 cun lateral GV12. Same horizontal position as GV12, BL13 and BL42.

2. Pohu is in the upper back region, at the same level as the inferior border of the spinous process of the third thoracic vertebra (T3), 3 B-cun lateral to the posterior median line.
Note: BL42, BL13 and GV12 are located at the same level as the inferior border of the third thoracic vertebra (T3). [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Asthma, bronchitis, pleurisy, atelectasis, pulmonary tuberculosis, neck rigidity, pain in the shoulder and back.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the upper back at the same level as the inferior border of the spinous process of the 4th thoracic vertebra, 3 cun lateral to the posterior median line, and 1.5 cun lateral BL14. Same horizontal position as BL14 and BL43.

2. Gaohuang is in the upper back region, at the same level as the inferior border of the spinous process of the fourth thoracic vertebra (T4), 3 B-cun lateral to the posterior median line.
Note: BL43 and BL14 are located at the same level as the inferior border of the spinous process of the fourth thoracic vertebra (T4). [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Consumptive deficient diseases, general weakness caused by prolonged illness, neurasthenia, hiccup, asthma, bronchitis, pleurisy, pulmonary tuberculosis, coughing blood, night sweating, poor memory, deficient spleen and stomach, nocturnal emission, pain along the spine.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the upper back at the same level as the inferior border of the spinous process of the 5th thoracic vertebra, 3 cun lateral to the posterior median line, and 3 cun lateral GV11. Same horizontal position as GV11, BL15 and BL44.

2. Shentang is in the upper back region, at the same level as the inferior border of the spinous process of the fifth thoracic vertebra (T5), 3 B-cun lateral to the posterior median line.
Note: BL44, BL15 and GV11 are located at the same level as the inferior border of the spinous process of the fifth thoracic vertebra (T5). [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Asthma, cough, bronchitis, cardiac pain, heart disease, palpitation, stuffy chest, intercostal neuralgia, stiffness and pain of the back.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the upper back at the same level as the inferior border of the spinous process of the 6th thoracic vertebra, 3 cun lateral to the posterior median line, and 3 cun lateral GV10. Same horizontal position as GV10, BL16 and BL45.

2. Yixi is in the upper back region, at the same level as the inferior border of the spinous process of the sixth thoracic vertebra (T6), 3 B-cun lateral to the posterior median line.
Note: BL45, BL16 and GV10 are located at the same level as the inferior border of the spinous process of the sixth thoracic vertebra (T6). [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Malaria, hiccup, asthma, pericarditis, intercostal neuralgia, pain of the shoulder and back.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. 1.5 cun lateral to the BL17. 3 cun lateral to the GV9, at the level of the lower border of the spinous process of the 7th thoracic vertebra, the same level as the inferior angle of scapula in the position of standing up. Same level as GV9, BL17 and BL46.
2. Geguan is in the upper back region, at the same level as the inferior border of the spinous process of the seventh thoracic vertebra (T7), 3 B-cun lateral to the posterior median line.
 Note: BL46, BL17 and GV9 are located at the same level as the inferior border of the spinous process of the seventh thoracic vertebra (T7). [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Dysphagia, hiccup, vomiting, belching, intercostal neuralgia, spasms of esophagus, gastric hemorrhage, pain and stiffness of the back.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the upper back at the same level as the inferior border of the spinous process of the 9th thoracic vertebra, 3 cun lateral to the posterior median line, 3 cun lateral GV8. Same horizontal position as GV8, BL18 and BL47.

2. Hunmen is in the upper back region, at the same level as the inferior border of the spinous process of the ninth thoracic vertebra (T9), 3 B-cun lateral to the posterior median line.
Note: BL47, BL18 and GV8 are located at the same level as the inferior border of the spinous process of the ninth thoracic vertebra (T9). [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Pain in the chest and hypochondriac region, back pain, neurasthenia, pleurisy, vomiting, stomachache, diseases of the liver and gall bladder, diarrhea.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the upper back at the same level as the inferior border of the spinous process of the 10th thoracic vertebra, 3 cun lateral to the posterior median line, and 3 cun lateral GV7. Same horizontal position as GV7, BL19 and BL48.

2. Yanggang is in the upper back region, at the same level as the inferior border of the spinous process of the tenth thoracic vertebra (T10), 3 B-cun lateral to the posterior median line.
Note: BL48, BL19 and GV7 are located at the same level as the inferior border of the spinous process of the tenth thoracic vertebra (T10). [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Hepatitis, jaundice, cholecystitis, gastritis, borborygmus, abdominal pain, diarrhea, pain in the hypochondriac region.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the upper back at the same level as the inferior border of the spinous process of the 11th thoracic vertebra, 3 cun lateral to the posterior median line, and 3 cun lateral GV6. Same horizontal position as GV6, BL20 and BL49.

2. Yishe is in the upper back region, at the same level as the inferior border of the spinous process of the eleventh thoracic vertebra (T11), 3 B-cun lateral to the posterior median line.
Note: BL49, BL20 and GV6 are located at the same level as the inferior border of the spinous process of the eleventh thoracic vertebra (T11). [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Vomiting, difficulty in swallowing, hepatitis, cholecystitis, gastritis, abdominal distension, borborygmus, diarrhea.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. OLocated on the front of the head, 1 cun superior to the anterior hairline, 1.5 cun lateral to the anterior median line(GV23), and 0.5 cun posterior to BL4. Same horizontal position as GV23 and BL5.

2. Wuchu is on the head, 1 B-cun superior to the anterior hairline, 1.5 B-cun lateral to the anterior median line.
Note: 0.5 B-cun superior to BL4, at the same level as GV23. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Headache, vertigo, seizures, blurring of vision, epilepsy, convulsion, rhinitis.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the upper back at the same level as the inferior border of the spinous process of the 12th thoracic vertebra, 3 cun lateral to the posterior median line, and 1.5 cun lateral BL21. Same horizontal position as BL21 and BL50.

2. Weicang is in the upper back region, at the same level as the inferior border of the spinous process of the twelfth thoracic vertebra (T12), 3 B-cun lateral to the posterior median line.
Note: BL50 and BL21 are located at the same level as the inferior border of the spinous process of the twelfth thoracic vertebra (T12). [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Abdominal pain, stomachache, infantile indigestion, gastritis, back pain.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the lower back at the same level as the inferior border of the spinous process of the 1st lumbar vertebra, 3 cun lateral to the posterior median line, and 3 cun lateral to GV5. Same horizontal position as GV5, BL22 and BL51.

2. Huangmen is in the lumbar region, at the same level as the inferior border of the spinous process of the first lumbar vertebra (L1), 3 B-cun lateral to the posterior median line.
Note: BL51, BL22 and GV5 are located at the same level as the inferior border of the spinous process of the first lumbar vertebra (L1). [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Abdominal pain, abdominal mass, pain in upper abdomen, mastitis, low back pain, paralysis of lower limb, constipation.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the lower back at the same level as the inferior border of the spinous process of the 2nd lumbar vertebra, 3 cun lateral to the posterior median line, and 3 cun lateral to GV4. Same horizontal position as GV4, BL23 and BL52.

2. Zhishi is in the lumbar region, at the same level as the inferior border of the spinous process of the second lumbar vertebra (L2), 3 B-cun lateral to the posterior median line.
Note: BL52, BL23 and GV4 are located at the same level as the inferior border of the spinous process of the second lumbar vertebra (L2). [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Vomiting, indigestion, enuresis, frequency of urination, nephritis, incontinence, painful urination, swelling and pain in the genitals, edema, impotence, nocturnal emissions, spermatorrhea, prostatitis, eczema of the scrotum, irregular menstruation, low back pain, paralysis of lower limb.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the buttock region at the same level as the 2nd posterior sacral foramen, 3 cun lateral to the median sacral crest. Same horizontal position as BL32, BL28 and BL53.

2. Baohuang is in the buttock region, at the same level as the second posterior sacral foramen, 3 B-cun lateral to the median sacral crest.
Note: BL53, BL28 and BL32 are located at the same level as the second posterior sacral foramen. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Borborygmus, abdominal distension, pain in the lower back, anuria, retention of urine, low back pain, sciatica.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the buttock region at the same level as the 4th posterior sacral foramen, 3 cun lateral to the median sacral crest. Same horizontal position as GV2, BL34, BL30 and BL54.

2. Zhibian is in the buttock region, at the same level as the fourth posterior sacral foramen, 3 B-cun lateral to the median sacral crest.
Note: 3 B-cun lateral to the sacral hiatus, at the same level as BL 30. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Dysuria, diseases of reproductive organs and anus, hemorrhoids, constipation, difficult defecation, swelling around external genitalia, genital pain, pain in lumbosacral region, strained muscles of the buttocks, sciatica, paralysis of lower limbs.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the posterior aspect of the lower leg, 2 cun inferior to the popliteal crease in the depression between the two branches of the gastrocnemius muscle. It is 2 cun inferior to BL40.

2. Heyang is on the posterior aspect of the leg, between the lateral head and medial head of the gastrocnemius muscle, 2 B-cun distal to the popliteal crease.
Note: 2 B-cun distal to BL40, on the line connecting BL40 with BL57. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Low back pain, soreness from lower back to knee, abnormal uterine bleeding.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the posterior aspect of the lower leg, 5 cun inferior to the popliteal crease in the depression between the two branches of the gastrocnemius muscle at the midpoint of the line connecting BL55 and BL57.

2. Chengjin is on the posterior aspect of the leg, between the two muscle bellies of the gastrocnemius muscle, 5 B-cun distal to the popliteal crease.
Note: Midway between BL55 and BL57. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Spasm of the gastrocnemius, acute lower back pain, pain in calf, paralysis of lower limb, headache, hemorrhoids.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the posterior aspect of the lower leg at the connecting point of the two branches of the gastrocnemius muscle with the calcaneal tendon. It is at the lateral belly of the gastrocnemius muscle which makes a lambda shape.

2. Chengshan is on the posterior aspect of the leg, at the connecting point of the calcaneal tendon with the two muscle bellies of the gastrocnemius muscle.
Note: With the leg stretched (plantar flexion) or the heel up, BL57 is located at the sharp angled depression inferior to the muscle belly of the gastrocnemius muscle.
The two heads of the gastrocnemius muscle are separated to make a lambda shape (λ). [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Ma Dan-Yang Twelve Heavenly Star points.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Sore throat, vomiting and diarrhea, prolapsed anus, hemorrhoids, constipation, pain of lumbar spine, sciatica, pain of lower back and leg, twisted calf muscles, spasm of the gastrocnemius, beriberi, paralysis of lower limb.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the posterolateral of the lower leg, 7 cun superior to BL60 between the inferior border of the lateral branch of the gastrocnemius muscle and the calcaneal tendon. It is 1 cun inferiorlateral to BL57. Same horizontal position as BL58, LR6, ST39, GB36 and GB35.

2. Feiyang is on the posterolateral aspect of the leg, between the inferior border of the lateral head of the gastrocnemius muscle and the calcaneal tendon, at the same level as 7 B-cun proximal to BL60.
Note: BL58 is located 1 B-cun lateral and distal to BL57, proximal to BL60. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Connecting point.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Headache, insanity, seizures, vertigo, blurring of vision, nasal obstruction, nasal congestion, nephritis, cystitis, hemorrhoids, pain of lower back and leg, pain in the calf, beriberi, progressive painful joints, rheumatoid arthritis.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the posterolateral of the lower leg, 3 cun superior to the BL60 between the fibula and the calcaneal tendon.

2. Fuyang is on the posterolateral aspect of the leg, between the fibula and the calcaneal tendon, at the same level as 3 B-cun proximal to BL60. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Cleft point(yang heel vessel).

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Heavy sensation of the head, headache, benefits the lower back, low back pain, paralysis of lower limb(caused by damp), inflammation of ankle joint, redness and swelling of the external malleolus.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the front of the head, 2.5 cun superior to the anterior hairline, 1.5 cun lateral to the anterior median line, and 1.5 cun posterior to BL5. Same horizontal position as BL6 and GB17.

2. Chengguang is on the head, 2.5 B-cun superior to the anterior hairline, 1.5 B-cun lateral to the anterior median line.
Note: 1.5 B-cun superior to BL5. 2 B-cun superior to BL4. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Common cold, vertigo, headaches, pannus, rhinitis.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the posterolateral of the ankle at the midpoint between the prominence of the lateral malleolus and the posterior border of the calcaneal tendon. Same horizontal position as KI3 and BL60.

2. Kunlun is on the posterolateral aspect of the ankle, in the depression between the prominence of the lateral malleolus and the calcaneal tendon. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: River point. Fire point. Ma Dan-Yang Twelve Heavenly Star points.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Tidal fevers, headache, stiff neck, low back pain, sciatica(important point), paralysis of lower limb, diseases of the ankle joint and soft tissues, redness and swelling of the external malleolus, difficult delivery, retained placenta, infantile fright, difficult labour, epilepsy.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the lateral aspect of the foot, 1.5 cun inferior to the BL60, lateral to the calcaneus in the depression at the border between the red and white skin.

2. Pucan (Pushen) is on the lateral aspect of the foot, distal to BL60, lateral to the calcaneus, at the border between the red and white flesh. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Crossing point with Yang heel vessel and BL meridian.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Beriberi, relaxes the tendons, low back pain, paralysis of lower limb, pain in ankle and foot.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the lateral aspect of the ankle, 0.5 cun inferior to the prominence of the lateral malleolus in the depression between the lateral malleolus and the calcaneus bone. Same horizontal position as KI6 and BL62.

2. Shenmai is on the lateral aspect of the foot, directly inferior to the prominence of the lateral malleolus, in the depression between the inferior border of the lateral malleolus and the calcaneus.
Note: BL62 is located in the depression distal to the inferior border of the lateral malleolus. The corresponding medial acupuncture point to BL62 is KI6. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Opening (master) point(yang heel vessel). Thirteen Ghost point. Confluence points of the eight vessels(yang heel vessel).

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Insanity, psychosis, mania, dizziness, seizures, epilepsy, hemiplegia, loss of speech due to stroke, headache(good point), lateral and midline headache, meningitis, mouth and eyes awry, ringing in the ears, Meniere's disease, palpitations, pain of the lower back and leg, arthritis of the ankle.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the midpoint of the BL62 and BL64, proximal to the tuberosity of the 5th metatarsal bone in the depression lateral to the cuboid bone.

2. Jinmen is on the dorsum of the foot, distal to the anterior border of the lateral malleolus, posterior to the tuberosity of the fifth metatarsal bone, in the depression inferior to the cuboid bone. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Opening (master) point(yang link vessel). Cleft point. Crossing point with Yang link vessel.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Mania, epilepsy, infantile convulsions, seizures, opens the channel, alleviates pain and eliminates stagnation(cleft point), pain in the lower back and legs, pain at the bottom of the foot.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the lateral aspect of the foot in the depression inferior to the tuberosity of the 5th metatarsal bone at the red and white skin. On the foot, inferior border of the 5th metatarsal bone in the depression between the red and white skin.

2. Jinggu is on the lateral aspect of the foot, distal to the tuberosity of the fifth metatarsal bone, at the border between the red and white flesh.
Note: The tuberosity of the fifth metatarsal bone is located approximately midway between the heel and the fifth metatarsophalangeal joint. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Source point.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Tidal fevers, headache, heaviness in the head, neck rigidity, seizures, insanity, meningitis, membrane over the eye, palpitations, myocarditis(specific point), pain of lower back and leg, cold in the legs.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the lateral aspect of the foot in the depression proximal to the 5th metatarsophalangeal joint at the border between the red and white skin.

2. Shugu is on the lateral aspect of the foot, in the depression proximal to the fifth metatarsophalangeal joint, at the border between the red and white flesh. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Stream point. Wood point. Sedation point.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Mania, mental illness, seizures, headache, neck rigidity, malaria, blurring of vision, pannus, backache, pain in the lower extrernities.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the lateral aspect of the 5th toe in the depression distal to the 5th metatarsophalangeal joint at the border between the red and white skin.

2. Zutonggu is on the little toe, in the depression distal and lateral to the fifth metatarsophalangeal joint, at the border between the red and white flesh. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Brook point. Water point. Ben point(five phases).

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Headache, vertigo, mental illness, neck rigidity, blurring of vision, asthma, nosebleed.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the lateral aspect of the 5th toe in the depression, 0.1 cun posterior(into the body) to the lateral corner of the little toenail at the intersection of the vertical line of the lateral border and the horizontal line of the base of the 5th toenail.

2. Zhiyin is on the little toe, lateral to the distal phalanx, 0.1 F-cun proximal to the lateral corner of the toenail, at the intersection of the vertical line of the lateral side of the nail and the horizontal line of the base of the toenail. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Well point. Metal point. Tonification point. Exit point.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Malposition of fetus, difficult labour, detention of after birth, failure to discharge placenta, infantile convulsions, stroke, headache, occipital headache, nasal obstruction, nosebleed, itching over the entire body.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the top of the head, 4 cun superior to the anterior hairline, 1.5 cun lateral to the anterior median line, and 1.5 cun posterior to BL6. Same horizontal position as BL7 and GB18.

2. Tongtian is on the head, 4 B-cun superior to the anterior hairline, 1.5 B-cun lateral to the anterior median line.
Note: Midway between BL6 and BL8. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Hemiplegia, headache, pain and heaviness at the vertex, dizziness, loss of sense of smell, rhinorrhea, rhinitis, mouth awry.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the top of the head, 5.5 cun superior to the anterior hairline, 1.5 cun lateral to the posterior median line, 0.5 cun posterior and 1.5 cun lateral to GV20, and 1.5 cun posterior to the BL7.

2. Luoque is on the head, 5.5 B-cun superior to the anterior hairline, 1.5 B-cun lateral to the anterior median line.
Note: 0.5 B-cun posterior and 1.5 B-cun lateral to GV20. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Subdues wind, facial paralysis, vertigo, opens the orifices, rhinitis, transforms phlegm, goiter, vomiting.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the back of the head. It is at the same level as the superior border of the external occipital protuberance, 1.3 cun lateral to the posterior median line. Another measurement says 1.3 cun or 1.5 cun lateral to the posterior median line(GV17), and 2.5 cun superior to the posterior hairline. Same horizontal position as GV17, BL9, GB19 and TE20.

2. Yuzhen is on the head, at the same level as the superior border of the external occipital protuberance, and 1.3 B-cun lateral to the posterior median line.
Note: BL9 is located at the intersection of two imaginary lines: the vertical line of the lateral border of the trapezius muscle and the horizontal line of the superior border of the external occipital protuberance. At the same level as GV17. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Headache, vertigo, neck pain, ophthalmalgia, myopia.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the perineal region. In males, the midpoint between the anus and the posterior border of the scrotum. In females, the midpoint between the anus and the posterior commissure of labium majoris.

2. In the perineal region, at the midpoint of the line connecting the anus with the posterior border of the scrotum in males and the posterior commissure of labium majoris in females.
Note: CV1 is located midway between the anus and the genital organ, with the subject lying on the side or in knee-chest position. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Crossing point with Governor vessel, Thoroughfare vessel and Conception vessel. Thirteen Ghost point. Entry point.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Retention of urine hemorrhoids, nocturnal emission, revive from drowning, urethritis, prostatitis, vaginitis, irregular menstruation.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:

2. On the upper abdomen, 2 B-cun superior to the centre of the umbilicus, on the anterior median line. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Crossing point with SP, ST and CV meridian.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Epigastric pain, food stagnation, indigestion, stomachache, prolapsed stomach, diarrhea.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:

2. On the upper abdomen, 3 B-cun superior to the centre of the umbilicus, on the anterior median line. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Stomachache, vomiting, angina, ascites, abdominal pain, acute and chronic gastritis, intestinal noises, anorexia.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:

2. On the upper abdomen, 4 B-cun superior to the centre of the umbilicus, on the anterior median line.
Note: CV12 is located at the midpoint of the line connecting the xiphisternal junction and the centre of umbilicus. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Alarm point(stomach). Crossing point with SI, TE, ST and CV meridian. Eight Meeting points(bowel). Nine points for Recovery Yang.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Insomnia, hypertension, neurasthenia, spitting blood related to consumptive illness, mental diseases, madness, lack of appetite, indigestion, vomiting, vomiting food long after digestion, sour taste upon swallowing, abdominal pain, abdominal distension, stomachache, pain in the stomach cavity, prolapsed stomach, acute or chronic gastritis, gastric ulcers, acute intestinal obstruction, jaundice, constipation, diarrhea, dysentery.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the upper abdomen at the anterior median line, 5 cun superior to the umbilicus. Same horizontal position as CV13, KI20 and ST20.

2. On the upper abdomen, 5 B-cun superior to the centre of the umbilicus, on the anterior median line. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Crossing point with ST, SI and CV meridian.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Chest pain, irritable and feverish heart, cardiac spasms, excessive salivation, epilepsy, insomnia, distension of the abdomen, acute and chronic gastritis, dilated stomach, stomach spasms, jaundice.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the upper abdomen at the anterior median line, 6 cun superior to the umbilicus. Same horizontal position as CV14, KI21, ST19 and LR14.

2. On the upper abdomen, 6 B-cun superior to the centre of the umbilicus, on the anterior median line. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Alarm point(heart).

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Stomachache, mental diseases, seizures, hiccup, cough, palpitations, chest pain, angina pectoris, vomiting, vomiting long after ingestion of food, chronic hepatitis, round worms in the bile duct, insomnia.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the upper abdomen at the anterior median line, 1 cun inferior to the xiphisternal junction where the sternum and the xiphoid process meet.

2. On the upper abdomen, 1 B-cun inferior to the xiphisternal junction, on the anterior median line. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Connecting point(Conception vessel).

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Pain in the cardiac region and the chest, nausea, mental illness, seizures, hiccup, asthma, angina pectoris.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the chest at the anterior median line on the xiphisternal junction where the sternum and the xiphoid process meet. Same horizontal position as CV16, KI22, ST18 and SP17.

2. In the anterior thoracic region, at the midpoint of the xiphisternal junction, on the anterior median line. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Distension and fullness in the chest and intercostal region, nausea, anorexia, vomiting, food stuck in throat, hiccup, asthma.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the chest at the anterior median line, same level as the 4th intercostal space between the 4th rib and 5th rib at the midpoint of the both nipples. Same horizontal position as CV17, KI23, ST17, PC1, SP18, GB23 and GB22.

2. In the anterior thoracic region, at the same level as the fourth intercostal space, on the anterior median line. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Alarm point(pericardium). Crossing point with SP, KI, SI, TE and CV meridian. Eight Meeting points(qi). Points of the Four Seas(sea of qi).

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Palpitation, difficulty or inability to swallow food, spitting and coughing blood, tumors on the neck, bronchial asthma, wheezing, panting, bronchitis, chest pain, lung abscess, intercostal neuralgia, insufficient lactation, mastitis.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the chest at the anterior median line, same level as the 3rd intercostal space between the 3rd rib and 4th rib. Same horizontal position as CV18, KI24, ST16 and SP19.

2. In the anterior thoracic region, at the same level as the third intercostal space, on the anterior median line. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Cough, vomiting, asthma, bronchitis, emphysema, intercostal neuralgia.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the chest at the anterior median line, same level as the 2nd intercostal space between the 2nd rib and 3rd rib. Same horizontal position as CV19, KI25, ST15 and SP20.

2. In the anterior thoracic region, at the same level as the second intercostal space, on the anterior median line. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Pain in the chest, asthma, bronchiectasis, pulmonary tuberculosis.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the pubic region. At the intersection of the anterior median line and the superior border of the pubic symphysis. Same horizontal position as CV2, KI11, ST30, LR12 and SP12.

2. On the lower abdomen, superior to the pubic symphysis, on the anterior median line. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Crossing point with LR and CV meridian.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Enuresis, nocturnal emission, impotence, morbid leukorrhea, cystitis, orchitis, irregular menstruation, prolapsed uterus, dysmenorrhea, hernia.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the chest at the anterior median line, same level as the 1st intercostal space between the 1st rib and 2nd rib. Same horizontal position as CV20, KI26, ST14 and LU1.

2. In the anterior thoracic region, at the same level as the first intercostal space, on the anterior median line. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Pain and fullness in the chest and intercostal region, asthma, bronchitis, pharyngitis, intercostal neuralgia.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the chest at the anterior median line, 1 cun inferior to the suprasternal fossa. Same horizontal position as CV21, KI27, ST13 and LU2.

2. In the anterior thoracic region, 1 B-cun inferior to the suprasternal fossa, on the anterior median line.
Note: CV21 is located 1 B-cun inferior to CV22. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Three Substances points(human).

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Swollen pharynx, spasms of the esophagus, cough, throat blockage, laryngeal stridor in children, bronchial asthma, chronic bronchitis, fullness & pain in the chest and ribs, cardiac spasm.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the neck at the intersection of the anterior median line and the suprasternal fossa. Same horizontal position as CV22, ST11 and ST12.

2. In the anterior region of the neck, in the centre of the suprasternal fossa, on the anterior median line.
Note: CV22 is located in the depression midway between the medial ends of each clavicle. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Crossing point with Yin link vessel and CV meridian. Windows of Heaven points(celestial chimney).

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Asthma, heavy wheezing, cough, sore throat, hiccup, pharyngitis, nervous vomiting, spasms of the esophagus, coughing blood and pus in the sputum, bronchitis, diseases of the vocal cords, hoarse voice, early stages of tumors or nodular growths on the neck, goiter.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the neck in the depression at the intersection of the anterior median line and the superior border of the hyoid bone which is superior to the thyroid cartilage.

2. In the anterior region of the neck, superior to superior border to thyroid cartilage, in the depression superior to the hyoid bone, on the anterior median line.
Note: With the head slightly extended, the hyoid tubercle can be palpated between the mandible and the thyroid cartilage. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Crossing point with Yin link vessel and CV meridian.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Swelling and pain of the subglossal region, salivation with glossoplegia, paralysis of hypoglossus muscle, loss of voice, tonsillitis, pharyngitis, bronchitis.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the chin in the depression at the intersection of the anterior median line of the face and the mentolabial sulcus.

2. On the face, in the depression in the centre of the mentolabial sulcus. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Crossing point with Governor vessel, ST, LI and CV meridian. Thirteen Ghost point. Exit point.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Facial puffiness, swelling of the gums, toothache, salivation, hemiplegia, facial paralysis, facial edema, mouth and eyes awry, ulcers in the mouth.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the lower abdomen at the anterior median line, 4 cun inferior to the umbilicus. Same horizontal position as CV3, KI12 and ST29.

2. On the lower abdomen, 4 B-cun inferior to the centre of the umbilicus, on the anterior median line. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Alarm point(bladder). Crossing point with LR, KI, SP and CV meridian.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Edema, excessive bleeding, pelveoperitonitis, sciatica, nephritis, urethritis, frequent urination, lack of urine, retention of urine, uterine bleeding, enuresis, impotence, spontaneous loss of sperm, premature ejaculation, spermatorrhea, female sterility, vaginal pain, vaginal discharge containing blood, dysmenorrhea, irregular menstruation, lack of menses, itching in the vagina, vaginitis, leukorrhea.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the lower abdomen at the anterior median line, 3 cun inferior to the umbilicus. Same horizontal position as CV4, KI13 and ST28.

2. On the lower abdomen, 3 B-cun inferior to the centre of the umbilicus, on the anterior median line. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Alarm point(small intestine). Crossing point with LR, KI, SP and CV meridian.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: General weakness, tidal fever, emaciation and constant thirst, abdominal pain, stroke, twisting pain below the navel, hernia, pelveoperitonitis, nephritis, blood in the urine, urinary tract infection, enuresis, cold diarrhea, blood in the stool, dysentery, impotence, loss of sperm, spermatorrhea, irregular menstruation, lack of menstruation, dysmenorrhea, prolapsed uterus, functional uterine bleeding, leukorrhea, infertility, vaginal discharge.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the lower abdomen at the anterior median line, 2 cun inferior to the umbilicus. Same horizontal position as CV5, KI14 and ST27.

2. On the lower abdomen, 2 B-cun inferior to the centre of the umbilicus, on the anterior median line. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Alarm point(triple energizer).

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Abdominal pain, diarrhea, edema, retention of urine, amenorrhea,morbid leukorrhea, uterine bleeding, mastitis, abnormal uterine bleeding.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the lower abdomen at the anterior median line, 1.5 cun inferior to the umbilicus.

2. On the lower abdomen, 1.5 B-cun inferior to the centre of the umbilicus, on the anterior median line. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: The important tonification point for mental and physical exhaustion.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Abdominal pain, abdominal distension, intestinal paralysis, colic, neurasthenia, excessive bleeding, heat stroke or exhaustion, polyuria, urinary retention, incontinence among children, impotence, spermatorrhea, dysmenorrhea, irregular menstruation, infertility.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the lower abdomen at the anterior median line, 1 cun inferior to the umbilicus. Same horizontal position as CV7, KI15 and ST26.

2. On the lower abdomen, 1 B-cun inferior to the centre of the umbilicus, on the anterior median line. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Crossing point with Thoroughfare vessel and KI, CV meridian.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Abdominal distention, pruritus vulvae, postpartum hemorrhage, edema, pain of hernia, irregular menstruation, leukorrhea, abnormal uterine bleeding, prolapsed uterus.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the center of the umbilicus. Same horizontal position as CV8, KI16, ST25, SP15 and GB26.

2. On the upper abdomen, in the centre of the umbilicus. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Abdominal pain, loss of consciousness, heat stroke or exhaustion, apoplexy, simultaneous vomiting and diarrhea, intestinal noises and pain, intestinal tuberculosis, shock resulting from intestinal adhesions, acute and chronic enteritis, prolapsed anus, chronic diarrhea, continuous diarrhea, edema.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the upper abdomen, at the anterior median line, 1 cun superior to the umbilicus. Same level as CV9 and ST24.

2. On the upper abdomen, 1 B-cun superior to the centre of the umbilicus, on the anterior median line. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Abdominal pain, borborygmus, vomiting, diarrhea, edema, retention of urine, ascites, nephritis.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the lateral aspect of the eye, 0.5 cun lateral to the outer canthus of the eye, at the end of the eye wrinkle.

2. On the head, in the depression, 0.5 B-cun lateral to the outer canthus of the eye. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Crossing point with SI, GB and TE meridian. Entry point.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Headache, failing of vision, lacrimation, atrophy of the optic nerve, ametropia, keratitis, night blindness, membranes over the eye, glaucoma, excessive tearing, sore throat.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the temporal region of the head. It is one third of GB9 when connecting GB9, GB10, GB11 and GB12 as an arching shape and dividing it into three. It is at the point posterosupeorior to the mastoid process.

2. On the head, posterosuperior to the mastoid process, at the junction of the upper one third and lower two thirds of the curved line from GB9 to GB12.
Note: Posterior to the auricular apex, 1 B-cun superior to the hairline. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Crossing point with BL and GB meridian.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Headache, deafness, tinnitus, toothache, bronchitis.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the posterolatral aspect of the head. It is two thirds of GB9 when connecting GB9, GB10, GB11 and GB12 as an arching shape and dividing it into three. It is at the point of the  posterosupeorior to the mastoid process.

2. On the head, posterior and superior to the mastoid process, at the junction of the upper two thirds and lower one third of the curved line from GB 9 to GB12. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Crossing point with BL, SI, TE and GB meridian.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Headache, ear ache, deafness, tinnitus, bronchitis, stiff neck.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1.Located on the posterolatral aspect of the head in the depression posteroinferior to the mastoid process.

2. In the anterior region of the neck, in the depression posteroinferior to the mastoid process. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Crossing point with BL, TE and GB meridian.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Insomnia, seizures, headache, facial paralysis, facial swelling, swelling of the cheek, retroauricular pain, toothache, parotitis.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the front of the head, 0.5 cun superior to the anterior hairline, and 3 cun lateral to the anterior median line. It is two thirds of GV24 when connecting GV24 to ST8 by 4.5 cun as an arching shape and dividing it into three. Same horizontal position as GV24, BL3, BL4, GB15, GB13 and ST8.

2. On the head, 0.5 B-cun superior to the anterior hairline, 3 B-cun lateral to the anterior median line.
Note: GB13 is at the junction of the medial two thirds and lateral one third of the curved line from GV24 to ST8. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Crossing point with Yang link vessel and GB meridian.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Insomnia, headache, vertigo, seizures, hemiplegia, stiff neck, costalgia.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the forehead at the vertical line of the center of the pupil, 1 cun superior to the superior border of the eye brow when the superior border of the eye brow and the anterior hairline are connected by 3 cun.

2. On the head, 1 B-cun superior to the eyebrow, directly superior to the centre of the pupil. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Crossing point with Yang link vessel, TE, LI, ST and GB meridian.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Chills, vertigo, headache, facial paralysis, eyelid tic, itching eyelids, supraorbital neuralgia, ptosis, eye diseases, sore eyes, night blindness, stiff neck, vomiting.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the front of the head at the vertical line of the center of the pupil, 0.5 cun superior to the anterior hairline. It is at the midpoint when connecting GV24 to ST8 by 4.5 cun as an arching shape. Same horizontal position as GV24, BL3, BL4, GB15, GB13 and ST8.

2. On the head, 0.5 B-cun within the anterior hairline, directly superior to the centre of the pupil.
Note: When looking straight ahead, GB15 is superior to the centre of the pupil, at the midpoint of the curved line from the GV24 to ST8. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Crossing point with Yang link vessel, BL and GB meridian.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Seizures, apoplectic coma, malaria, vertigo, acute and chronic conjunctivitis, lacrimation, pannus, pain in outer canthus, occluded nose.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Directly superior to the center of the pupil or the midline between the GV24 and ST8, 1.5 cun superior to the anterior hairline. 1 cun superior to the GB15.
2. On the head, 1.5 B-cun within the anterior hairline, directly superior to the centre of the pupil.
 Note: GB16 is 1 B-cun superior to GB15. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Crossing point with Yang link vessel and GB meridian.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Apoplectic coma, headache, vertigo, facial edema, conjunctivitis, toothache.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the front of the head at the vertical line of the center of the pupil, 2.5 cun superior to the anterior hairline. It is 1 cun posterior to GB16. Same horizontal level as BL6 and GB17.

2. On the head, 2.5 B-cun within the anterior hairline, directly superior to the centre of the pupil.
Note: GB17 is 2 B-cun superior to GB15. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Crossing point with Yang link vessel and GB meridian.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Migraine, headache, vertigo, toothache, vomiting, stiff neck.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the top of the head at the vertical line of the center of the pupil, 4 cun superior to the anterior hairline. It is 1.5 cun posterior to GB17. Same horizontal position as BL7 and GB18.

2. On the head, 4 B-cun within the anterior hairline, directly superior to the centre of the pupil.
Note: GB18 is 1.5 B-cun posterior to GB17, at the same level as BL7. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Crossing point with Yang link vessel and GB meridian.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Headache, vertigo, epistaxis, common cold, eye diseases, occluded nose, nosebleed, rhinorrhea, bronchitis.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the back of the head. At the same level as the superior border of the external occipital protuberance. It is two fifths of GV17 when connect GV17 to TE20 and dividing it into five. Located at the vertical line of GB20. Same horizontal position as GV17, BL9, GB19 and TE20.

2. On the head, at the same level as the superior border of the external occipital protuberance, directly superior to GB20.
Note: GB19 is at the same level as GV17 and BL9. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Crossing point with Yang link vessel and GB meridian.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Epilepsy, seizures, mental illness, common cold, headache, tinnitus, asthma, palpitations.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the ear at the anterior to the intertragic notch and anteroinferior to the triages in the depression between anterior to the tragus and posterior border of the condyloid process of the mandible, when the mouth is opened. It is over the superficial temporal artery. TE21, SI19 and GB2 is placed in order on the same vertical line.

Between anterior and inferior to the intertragic notch of the tragus and posterior border of the condyloid process of the mandible, when the mouth is opened. TE21, SI19 and GB2 is placed in order on same vertical line.

2. On the face, in the depression between the intertragic notch and the condylar process of the mandible.
Note: When the mouth is opened, GB2 is located in the depression anterior to the intertragic notch. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Madly running away, seizures in which the body is alternately tense and limp, hemiplegia, facial paralysis, deafness, tinnitus, otitis media, deaf-mutism, mouth and eyes awry, dislocation of the jaw, toothache, swelling of the parotid glands.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the nape of the neck at the inferior border of the occipital bone in the depression between the origins of the sternocleidomastoid and trapezius. Same horizontal position as GV16 and GB20.

2. In the anterior region of the neck, inferior to the occipital bone, in the depression between the origins of sternocleidomastoid and the trapezius muscles.
Note: GB20 is at the same level as GV16. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text:
Exit point(yang heel vessel). Meeting point with TE, Yang link vessel, Yang heel vessel and GB meridian.
Other name : 热府[针灸学-南京].

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Hypertension, common cold, tidal fevers, hemiplegia, seizures, brain disease, insomnia, headache, lateral and midline headaches, vertigo, eye diseases, eyes red and sore, glaucoma nasal obstruction, rhinitis, sinusitis, deafness, tinnitus, swellings or tumors on the neck, stiff neck.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the nape of the neck at the midpoint between the spinous process of the 7th cervical vertebra and the acromion, midpoint between the GV14 and LI15. When the elbow is fixed on the side flank and then folding the arm to the opposite shoulder, the point where the tip of the middle finger touches.

2. In the posterior region of the neck, at the midpoint of the line connecting the spinous process of the seventh cervical vertebra (C7) with the lateral end of the acromion. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Crossing point with Yang link vessel, TE, ST and GB meridian. Seven points for CVA.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Common cold, hemiplegia due to stroke, vertigo, blurred vision, nasal obstruction, aphasia due to apoplexy, cough from rebellious qi, stiff neck, pain in the back of the shoulder, infantile convulsion, mastitis, breast abscess, functional uterine breeding, difficult labor, scrofula.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the flank bBetween the 4th rib and 5th rib in the 4th intercostal space at the midaxillary line. It is 3 cun inferior to the HT1. Same horizontal position as CV17, KI23, ST17, PC1, SP18, GB23 and GB22.

2. In the lateral thoracic region, in the fourth intercostal space, on the midaxillary line. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Axillary lymphadenitis, intercostal neuralgia, pleurisy, pain of shoulders and arm.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the flank between the 4th rib and 5th rib in the 4th intercostal space, 1 cun anterior to the midaxillary line. Same horizontal position as CV17, KI23, ST17, PC1, SP18, GB23 and GB22.

2. In the lateral thoracic region, in the fourth intercostal space, 1 B-cun anterior to the midaxillary line. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Crossing point with BL and GB meridian.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Vomiting, asthma, fullness of the chest, acidic belching, pleurisy.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the chest etween the 7th rib and 8th rib, in the 7th intercostal space, 4 cun lateral to the anterior median line. It is 0.5 cun inferior to LR14.

2. In the anterior thoracic region, in the seventh intercostal space, 4 B-cun lateral to the anterior median line.
Note 1: GB24 is inferior to the centre of the nipple, one rib inferior to LR14.
Note 2: In females, GB24 can be found at the intersection of the midclavicular line and the seventh intercostal space. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Alarm point(gall bladder). Crossing point with SP, Yang link vessel and GB meridian.

sections.name: Indications
