sections.text: Vomiting, hiccups, intercostal neuralgia, acute and chronic hepatitis, jaundice, cholecystitis, peptic ulcer, acid regurgitation.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. On the lateral side of the abdomen, just inferior to the end of the 12th rib.
2. On the lateral abdomen, inferior to the free extremity of the 12th rib.
 Note: GB25 can be located while the subject is lying on the side with the shoulder flexed. The free extremity of the 12th rib can be palpated below the inferior border of the costal arch posterior to the posterior axillary line. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Alarm point(kidneys).

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Intercostal neuralgia, abdominal distention, borborygmus, diarrhea, pain of intestinal hernia, nephritis, lumbago.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the flank at the intersection of the vertical line of the free extremity of the 11th rib and the horizontal line of the umbilicus. Inferior to LR13. It is at the same level as the umbilicus. Same horizontal position as CV8, KI16, ST25, SP15 and GB26.

2. On the lateral abdomen, inferior to the free extremity of the 11th rib, at the same level as the centre of umbilicus.
Note 1: GB26 can be located by first locating the tenth rib, then searching for the free extremity of the 11th rib that is situated immediately below the inferior border of the costal arch.
Note 2: GB26 is inferior to LR13, at the same level as CV8. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Entry point(belt vessel). Crossing point with Belt vessel and GB meridian.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Convulsions, paraplegia due to trauma, abdominal pain, hernia, intestinal colic, diarrhea, cystitis, irregular menstruation, endometritis, profuse blood and leukorrhea, amenorrhea.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the groin region, 3 cun inferior to the umbilicus, just medial(inside) to the ASIS(anterior superior iliac spine). It is 3 cun inferior to GB26.

2. On the lower abdomen, 3 B-cun inferior to the centre of umbilicus, medial to the anterior superior iliac spine.
Note: GB27 is 3 B-cun inferior to GB26, at the same level as CV4. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Crossing point with Belt vessel and GB meridian.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Lower abdominal pain, hernia, colic, constipation, orchitis, endometritis, leukorrhea, vaginal discharge containing blood, low back pain, infantile convulsions.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the groin region, 0.5 cun medial(inside) and inferior to the ASIS(anterior superior iliac spine). It is 0.5 cun medial(inside) and inferior to GB27.

2. On the lower abdomen, 0.5 B-cun medioinferior to the anterior superior iliac spine.
Note: GB28 is 0.5 B-cun medioinferior to GB27. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Crossing point with Belt vessel and GB meridian.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Pain of intestinal hernia, chronic constipation, prolapsed uterus, endometritis, leukorrhea, adnexitis.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the lateral aspect of the buttock region at the midpoint between the ASIS(anterior superior iliac spine) and the prominence of the greater trochanter.

2. In the buttock region, midpoint of the line connecting the anterior superior iliac spine and the prominence of the greater trochanter. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Crossing point with Belt vessel, Yang heel vessel and GB meridian.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Stomachache, cystitis, diarrhea, orchitis, endometritis, low back pain and associated pain in lower abdomen, lower abdominal pain, pain and numbness in the thigh and lumbar region, diseases of the hip joint and surrounding soft tissues, pain in the leg, paralysis or atrophy of leg.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the lateral side of the face in the depression at the midpoint of superior border of the zygomatic arch, superior to the ST7.

2. On the head, in the depression superior to the midpoint of the zygomatic arch.
Note: In the depression superior to the zygomatic arch, superior to ST7. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Crossing point with TE, ST and GB meridian.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Facial paralysis, deviation of the eye and mouth, toothache, otitis media, tinnitus, deafness, diplacusis, “locked” jaw.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the buttock region. It is one third of the prominence of the greater trochanter when connecting the prominence of the greater trochanter and the sacral hiatus and dividing it into three.

2. In the buttock region, at the junction of the lateral one third and medial two thirds of the line connecting the prominence of the greater trochanter with the sacral hiatus.
Note: GB30 is easier to locate when the subject is lying on the side with the thigh flexed.
Remarks: Alternative location for GB30 -in the buttock region, at the junction of the lateral one third and medial two thirds of the distance between the prominence of the greater trochanter and the anterior superior iliac spine. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Crossing point with BL and GB meridian. Nine points for Recovery Yang. Ma Dan-Yang Twelve Heavenly Star points.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Hemiplegia, wind rash, edema, pain in the groin, diseases of the hip joint and surrounding soft tissues, sciatica, pain in the lower back and leg, numbness and paralysis of the lower extremity.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the lateral aspect of the thigh where the tip of the middle finger touches while standing with hands at the sides. It is at the posterior border of the iliotibial band, 10 cun superior to the popliteal crease when the popliteal crease and the prominence of the greater trochanter are connected by 19 cun. Another measurement says it is 7 cun superior to the popliteal crease.

2. On the lateral aspect of the thigh, in the depression posterior to the iliotibial band where the tip of the middle finger rests, when standing up with the arms hanging alongside the thigh.
Note: GB31 is located by first finding the iliotibial band when the knee is slightly flexed and the hip is abducted against resistance. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Seven points for CVA. Eight points for Beriberi.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Hemiplegia, headache, eyes red & swollen, itching on one side of the body, neuritis of the lateral cutaneous nerve of the thigh and a muscle branch of the femoral nerve, soreness and pain in the lower back and leg, pain in lower back and leg, paralysis of lower limb, numbness and stiffness of the lower leg and foot.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the lateral aspect of the thigh at the posterior border of the iliotibial band, 7 cun superior to the popliteal crease, when the popliteal crease and the prominence of the greater trochanter are connected by 19 cun. It is 3 cun inferior to GB31. Another measurement says it is 5 cun superior to the popliteal crease.

2. On the lateral aspect of the thigh, posterior to the iliotibial band, 7 B-cun superior to the popliteal crease. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Hemiplegia, sciatica, beriberi, paralysis of lower limb.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the lateral aspect of the thigh in the depression posterior border of the lateral epicondyle of the femur between the biceps femoris tendon and the iliotibial band, 5 cun superior to GB34, and 3 cun superior to the popliteal crease when the popliteal crease and the prominence of the greater trochanter are connected by 19 cun. Another measurement says it is 2 cun superior to the popliteal crease.

2. On the lateral aspect of the knee, in the depression between the biceps femoris tendon and the iliotibial band, posterior and proximal to the lateral epicondyle of the femur. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Inability to flex or extend the knee, diseases of the knee and surrounding soft tissues, progressive swelling and pain of the knee, paralysis of lower limb.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the lateral aspect of the lower leg in the depression anteroinferior to the head of the fibula. Same horizontal position as GB34 and SP9.

2. On the fibular aspect of the leg, in the depression anterior and distal to the head of the fibula. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Sea point. Earth point. Eight Meeting points(tendons). Lower Sea points of the Six Bowels(gall bladder). Ma Dan-Yang Twelve Heavenly Star points.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Hemiplegia, weakness, hypertension, distension of the mouth, tongue, throat, face, and head, perifocal, inflammation of the shoulder, fullness of the chest and ribs, intercostal neuralgia, hepatitis, distension of the gall bladder, round worm in the bile duct, cholecystitis, loss of urine, habitual constipation, pain in the knee, paralysis and numbness of lower limb, infantile convulsion.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the lateral aspect of the lower leg at the posterior border of the fibula, 7 cun superior to the prominence of the lateral malleolus when the popliteal crease and the prominence of the lateral malleolus are connected by 16 cun. GB36 is at the anterior border of the fibula. Same horizontal position as GB35, BL58, LR6, ST39 and GB36.

2. On the fibular aspect of the leg, posterior to the fibula, 7 B-cun proximal to the prominence of the lateral malleolus.
Note: GB35 is located 1 B-cun distal to the midpoint of the line connecting the prominence of the lateral malleolus and the lateral end of the popliteal crease, posterior to GB36. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Cleft point(yang link vessel). Crossing point with Yang link vessel and GB meridian.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Fullness of the chest and hypochondriac region, asthma, sciatica, pain on lateral aspect of leg.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the lateral aspect of the lower leg at the anterior border of the fibula, 7 cun superior to the prominence of the lateral malleolus when the popliteal crease and the prominence of the lateral malleolus are connected by 16 cun. GB35 is at the posterior border of the fibula. Same horizontal position as GB36, GB35, BL58, LR6 and ST39.

2. On the fibular aspect of the leg, anterior to the fibula, 7 B-cun proximal to the prominence of the lateral malleolus.
Note: GB36 is located 1 B-cun distal to the midpoint of the line connecting the prominence of the lateral malleolus and the lateral end of the popliteal crease, anterior to GB35. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Cleft point.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Pain in the neck, headache, rabies, hepatitis, paralysis of lower limb.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the lateral aspect of the lower leg at the anterior border of the fibula, 5 cun superior to the prominence of the lateral malleolus when the popliteal crease and the prominence of the lateral malleolus are connected by 16 cun.

2. On the fibular aspect of the leg, anterior to the fibula, 5 B-cun proximal to the prominence of the lateral malleolus. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Connecting point.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Muscular atrophy, chills and fever without sweating, seizures, migraine headache, atrophy of optic nerve, pain and itching of the eye, cataract, night blindness, pain in the knee, pain along lateral aspect of calf, blockage and numbness of the leg, soreness of the leg & knee.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the lateral aspect of the lower leg at the anterior border of the fibula, 4 cun superior to the prominence of the lateral malleolus when the popliteal crease and the prominence of the lateral malleolus are connected by 16 cun.

2. On the fibular aspect of the leg, anterior to the fibula, 4 B-cun proximal to the prominence of the lateral malleolus. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: River point. Fire point. Sedation point.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Malaria, hemiplegia, migraine headache, scrofula, arthritis of knee, paralysis of lower limb.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the lateral aspect of the lower leg at the anterior border of the fibula, 3 cun superior to the prominence of the lateral malleolus when the popliteal crease and the prominence of the lateral malleolus are connected by 16 cun. Same horizontal position as GB39 and SP6.

2. On the fibular aspect of the leg, anterior to the fibula, 3 B-cun proximal to the prominence of the lateral malleolus. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Eight Meeting points(marrow). Seven points for CVA. Eight points for Beriberi.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Apoplexy, hemiplegia, migraine headache, nosebleed, coughing, throat blockage, stiff neck, scrofula, fullness in the chest and abdomen, sciatica, beriberi, diseases of the knee and ankle joints and surrounding soft tissues.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. In the hairline of the temporal side, at the junction of the upper one fourth and lower three fourths of the line between the ST8 to GB7. ST8, GB4, GB5, GB6 is same line in order.
2. On the head, at the junction of the upper one fourth and lower three fourths of the curved line from ST8 to GB7. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Crossing point with TE, ST, LI and GB meridian.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Vertigo, seizures, convulsions, migraine headache, tinnitus, rhinitis.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the lateral aspect of the ankle. It is Inferior to the anterior border of the lateral malleolus at the intersection of the vertical line of the anterior border of the lateral malleolus and the horizontal line of the inferior border of the lateral malleolus. Lateral border of the extensor digitorum longus tendon.

2. On the anterolateral aspect of the ankle, in the depression lateral to the extensor digitorum longus tendon, anterior and distal to the lateral malleolus.
Note: GB40 is easier to locate by finding the extensor digitorum longus tendon when the second to fifth toes are extended against resistance. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Source point.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Tidal fevers, axillary lymphadenitis, pain in the chest and ribs, vomiting, acid regurgitation, distension on the lower abdomen, cholecystitis, colic, sciatica, soreness of the leg due to twisted muscles, diseases of the ankle and surrounding soft tissues.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the back of the foot, lateral to the 5th tendon of the extensor digitorum longus at the junction on the 4th and the 5th metatarsal bones.

2. On the dorsum of the foot, distal to the junction of the bases of the fourth and fifth metatarsal bones, in the depression lateral to the fifth extensor digitorum longus tendon. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Stream point. Wood point. Confluence points of the eight vessels(belt vessel). Ben point(five phases).

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Headache, vertigo, conjunctivitis, scrofula, rib pain, mastitis, abscessed breast, irregular menstruation, dampness and swelling of the foot.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the back of the foot in the depression proximal to the the 4th metatarsophalangeal joint between the 4th and 5th metatarsal bones, medial to the 5th tendon of the extensor digitorum longus. It is 0.5 cun distal(toe) to GB41.

2. On the dorsum of the foot, between the fourth and fifth metatarsal bones, in the depression proximal to the fourth metatarsophalangeal joint. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Pain of the canthus, tinnitis, mastitis, low back pain, inflammation of the dorsum of the foot.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the lateral aspect of the 4th toe in the depression distal to the 4th metatarsophalangeal joint at the web margin between the 4th and 5th toe at the border between the red and white skin.

2. On the dorsum of the foot, between the fourth and fifth toes, proximal to the web margin, at the border between the red and white flesh. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Brook point. Water point. Tonification point.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Headache, dizziness and vertigo, hypertension, migraine headache, tinnitis, intercostal neuralgia, febrile diseases.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the lateral aspect of the 4th toe in the depression, 0.1 cun posterior(into the body) to the lateral corner of the 4th toenail. It is at the intersection of the vertical line of the lateral border and the horizontal line of the base of the 4th toenail.

2. On the fourth toe, lateral to the distal phalanx, 0.1 F-cun proximal to the lateral corner of the toenail, at the intersection of the vertical line of the lateral side of the nail and the horizontal line of the base of the fourth toenail. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Well point. Metal point. Exit point.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Hypertension, migraine, headache, deafness, conjunctivitis, asthma, pleurisy, intercostal neuralgia.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the temporal region of the head. It is one half of ST8 when connecting ST8, GB4, GB5, GB6 and GB7 as an arching shape and dividing it into four.

2. On the head, at the midpoint of the curved line from ST8 to GB7. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Crossing point with TE, LI and GB meridian.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Neurasthenia, migraine headache, facial swelling, toothache.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. In the hairline of the temporal side, at the junction of the upper three fourths and lower one fourth of the line between the ST8 to GB7. ST8, GB4, GB5, GB6 is same line in order.
2. On the head, at the junction of the upper three fourths and lower one fourth of the curved line from ST8 to GB7. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Crossing point with TE, ST, LI and GB meridian.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Frequent sneezing, neurasthenia, migraine headache, facial swelling, toothache.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the temporal region of the head at the intersection of the vertical line of the auricular apex and the horizontal line of the posterior border of the temporal hairline.

2. On the head, at the junction of the vertical line of the posterior border of the temporal hairline and the horizontal line of the apex of the auricle. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Crossing point with BL and GB meridian. Seven points for CVA.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Headache, migraine headache, spasms of the temporalis muscle, swelling of the cheek, trismus, trigeminal neuralgia.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the temporal region of the head in the vertical line of the auricular apex, 1.5 cun superior to the temporal hairline. It is easily found with masticatory muscle activity.

2. On the head, directly superior to the auricular apex, 1.5 B-cun superior to the temporal hairline.
Note: Superior to the TE20, 1.5 B-cun within the hairline, it is easier to palpate the point while the subject is chewing. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Crossing point with BL and GB meridian.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Vertigo, vomiting, migraine headaches, eye diseases.It is easily facilitated in authoring activities.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the temporal region of the head in the vertical line of the posterior border of the auricular root, 2 cun superior to the temporal hairline. It is 0.5 cun posteroinferior to GB8.

2. On the head, directly superior to the posterior border of the auricular root, 2 B-cun superior to the hairline.
Note: GB9 is 0.5 B-cun posterior to the GB8. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Crossing point with BL and GB meridian.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Epilepsy, convulsion, seizures, headache, gingivitis, swelling and pain of the gums, goiter.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the coccyx region of the buttocks at the midpoint between the end of the coccyx and the anus, inferior to the coccyx.

2. In the perineal region, inferior to the coccyx, midway between the tip of the coccyx and the anus.
Note: The subject may be in prone position or knee-chest position. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Connecting point. Crossing point with Governor vessel, GB and KI meridian.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Diarrhea, bloody stools, hemorrhoids, prolapse of the rectum, prolapsed anus, cloudy and turbid urine, psychosis, madness, infantile convulsions, impotence, eczema of the scrotum, loss of sperm, inducing labor.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the upper back at the posterior median line in the depression inferior to the spinous process of the 6th thoracic vertebra. Same horizontal position as GV10, BL16 and BL45.

2. In the upper back region, in the depression inferior to the spinous process of the sixth thoracic vertebra (T6), on the posterior median line. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Cough, hot or cold common cold, malaria, stiffness in the neck and soreness along the spine, asthma, bronchitis, hot condition in the spleen, round worm in the bile duct, stomachache, carbuncles.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the upper back at the posterior median line in the depression inferior to the spinous process of the 5th thoracic vertebra. Same horizontal position as GV11, BL15 and BL44.

2. In the upper back region, in the depression inferior to the spinous process of the fifth thoracic vertebra (T5), on the posterior median line. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Fever, malaria, seizures, heart disease, intercostal neuralgia.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the upper back at the posterior median line in the depression inferior to the spinous process of the 3rd thoracic vertebra. Same horizontal position as GV12, BL13 and BL42.

2. In the upper back region, in the depression inferior to the spinous process of the third thoracic vertebra (T3), on the posterior median line.
Note: The depression inferior to the spinous process of the third thoracic vertebra (T3) which is at the intersection of two imaginary lines: the posterior median line and the horizontal line of the medial end of the spine of the scapula. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Mental diseases, hysteria, seizures, infantile convulsions, aphasia due to apoplexy, wheezing cough associated with a consumptive condition, asthma, bronchitis, pulmonary tuberculosis, pneumonia, heat in the chest, chest & back pain, stiffness & pain in the lumbar region.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the upper back at the posterior median line, in the depression inferior to the spinous process of the 1st thoracic vertebra. Same horizontal position as GV13, BL11 and SI14.

2. In the upper back region, in the depression inferior to the spinous process of the first thoracic vertebra (T1), on the posterior median line. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Crossing point with BL and GV meridian.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Stiffness of the back, fever, tidal fevers, fever & chills, malaria, absence of sweating, psychosis, seizures, infantile convulsions, headache, heaviness in the head & dizziness, head & neck muscle spasms, pulmonary tuberculosis.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the nape of the neck at the posterior median line in the depression inferior to the spinous process of the 7th cervical vertebra. The most prominent bones when bow the head are the spinous process of the 7th cervical vertebra, which moves when turn head to the left and right. Same horizontal position as GV14 and SI15.

2. In the posterior region of the neck, in the depression inferior to the spinous process of the seventh cervical vertebra (C7), on the posterior median line.
Note 1: When the head is in a neutral position while the subject is seated, the most prominent site on the posterior aspect of the neck is the spinous process of the seventh cervical vertebra (C7). Forward flexion of the neck may facilitate palpation of the C7 spinous process.
Note 2: Slight rotation of C7 can be palpated by rotating the head with the neck slightly flexed. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Crossing point with Three Yang meridians of the hand(SI, LI, TE), Three Yang meridians of the foot(ST, GB, BL) and Governor vessel. Points of the Four Seas(sea of qi).

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Neck pain and rigidity, pain in the back of the shoulder, malaria, febrile diseases, tidal fevers, fever and chills, hot sensation in bones with recurrent fever, cold-induced diseases, blood diseases, heatstroke, hemiplegia, psychosis, seizures, cough, congested throat, asthma, bronchitis, emphysema, pulmonary tuberculosis, constricted feeling in chest and soreness in ribs, hepatitis.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the nape of the neck at the posterior median line in the depression inferior to the spinous process of the 2nd cervical vertebra. It is 0.5 cun superior to the posterior hairline, in the posterior median line. Same horizontal position as GV15 and BL10.

2. In the posterior region of the neck, in the depression superior to the spinous process of the second cervical vertebra (C2), on the posterior median line.
Note: After locating GV16, GV15 is located 0.5 B-cun inferior to GV16. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Crossing point with Yang link vessel and GV meridian. Points of the Four Seas(sea of qi). Nine points for Recovery Yang.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Apoplexy, cerebral palsy, incomplete maturation of the brain, seizures, convulsions, hysteria, headache, occipital headache, deaf-mutism, nosebleed, stiff tongue inhibiting speech, stiff neck.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the nape of the neck at the posterior median line, between both trapezius muscles, inferior to the external occipital protuberance, and 1 cun superior to the posterior hairline. Same horizontal position as GV16 and GB20.

2. In the posterior region of the neck, directly inferior to the external occipital protuberance, in the depression between the trapezius muscles.
Note: With the head slightly extended in the seated position, loosen the trapezius muscle, then move superiorly from the midpoint of the posterior hairline to the occipital bone, GV16 will be found. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Crossing point with Yang link vessel, Yang heel vessel, BL and GV meridian. Points of the Four Seas(sea of marrow). Windows of Heaven points(wind warehouse). Thirteen Ghost point.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Headache, neck rigidity, common cold, stroke, mental illness, numbness of the limbs.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the back of the head at the posterior median line of the head in the depression superior to the external occipital protuberance. Same horizontal position as GV17, BL9, GB19 and TE20.

2. On the head, in the depression superior to the external occipital protuberance.
Note: GV17 is located in the depression at the intersection of two imaginary lines: the vertical line of the posterior median line and the horizontal line of the superior border of the external occipital protuberance, at the same level as BL9. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Crossing point with BL and GV meridian.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Epilepsy, dizziness, insomnia, seizures, headache, stiff neck.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the back of the head at the posterior median line of the head, 4 cun superior to the posterior hairline. It is 1.5 cun superior to the GV17.

2. On the head, 4 B-cun superior to the posterior hairline, on the posterior median line.
Note: GV18 is located in the depression 1.5 B-cun superior to GV17. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Mania, insomnia, seizures, headache, stiff neck.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the back of the head at the posterior median line of the head, 5.5 cun superior to the posterior hairline. It is 1.5 cun posterior to the GV20.

2. On the head, 5.5 B-cun superior to the posterior hairline, on the posterior median line.
Note: GV19 is located 1.5 B-cun posterior to GV20. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Headache, vertigo, mania, common cold, insomnia, seizures, migraine headache.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the sacral region at the posterior median line, inferior to the 4th sacrum, in the sacral hiatus. Same horizontal position as GV2, BL34, BL30 and BL54.

2. In the sacral region, at the sacral hiatus, on the posterior median line.
Note: The sacral hiatus is a small depression immediately above the anal cleft. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Epilepsy, seizures, incontinence, enuresis, hemorrhoids, irregular menstruation, low back pain, paralysis of lower limb.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the top of the head at the anterior median line of the head, 5 cun superior to the anterior hairline, and 1 cun anterior to the midpoint of the line connecting the anterior hairline and the posterior hairline. It is at the midpoint of the line connecting both the auricular apex, when folding both ears.

2. On the head, 5 B-cun superior to the anterior hairline, on the anterior median line.
Note 1: GV20 is located in the depression 1 B-cun anterior to the midpoint of the line from the anterior hairline to the posterior hairline.
Note 2: When the ears are folded, GV20 is located at the midpoint of the connecting line between the auricular apices. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Crossing point with Three Yang meridians of the hand(SI, LI, TE), Three Yang meridians of the foot(ST, GB, BL), Governor vessel and LR meridian. Points of the Four Seas(sea of marrow). Seven points for CVA. Three Substances points(heaven).

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Headache, vertigo, hypertension, shock, insomnia, stroke, madness, hemiplegia, seizures, pain at the vertex, dizziness, deafness, tinnitus, nasal congestion, “locked” jaw, prolapsed anus, hemorrhoids, prolapsed uterus.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the top of the head at the anterior median line of the head, 3.5 cun superior to the anterior hairline.

2. On the head, 3.5 B-cun superior to the anterior hairline, on the anterior median line.
Note: GV21 is located at the midpoint of the line connecting GV20 and GV22. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Epilepsy, dizziness, infantile convulsions, headache, vertigo, rhinitis, rhinopolypus.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the front of the head at the anterior median line of the head, 2 cun superior to the anterior hairline.

2. On the head, 2 B-cun superior to the anterior hairline, on the anterior median line.[WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Headache, blurring of vision, infantile convulsions, vertigo, rhinitis, rhinopolypus.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the front of the head at the anterior median line of the head, 1 cun superior to the anterior hairline. Same horizontal position as GV23 and BL5.

2. On the head, 1 B-cun superior to the anterior hairline, on the anterior median line. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Thirteen Ghost point.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Febrile diseases in which there is no sweating, seizures, headache, dizziness, facial edema, ophthalmalgia, myopia, sore eyes, keratitis, rhinitis, rhinopolypus, nosebleed, sinus problems, mental disorders.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the front of the head at the anterior median line of the head, 0.5 cun superior to the anterior hairline, and 3.5 cun superior to the midpoint of the line connect both the medial ends of the eyebrows. Same horizontal position as GV24, BL3, BL4, GB15, GB13 and ST8.

2. On the head, 0.5 B-cun superior to the anterior hairline, on the anterior median line.
Note: When the anterior hairline is unclear or changed, GV 24 is located 3.5 B-cun superior to the midpoint between the medial ends of the eyebrows. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Crossing point with BL, ST and GV meridian.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Epilepsy, anxiety, palpitation, insomnia, seizures, headache, vertigo, rhinitis, rhinopolypus, stomatitis.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the nose at the anterior median line of the nose on the center of the tip of the nose.

2. On the face, at the tip of the nose. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Loss of consciousness, low blood pressure, bradycardia, shock, infantile convulsion, brandy nose, nasal obstruction, extra tissue in the nose, epistaxis, rhinitis, rosacea.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the inferior to the nose at the midpoint of the philtrum. Another measurement says it is one third inferior to the superior border of the philtrum, in the philtrum midline.

2. On the face, at the midpoint of the philtrum midline.
Remarks: Alternative location for GV26 - At the junction of the upper one third and lower two thirds of the philtrum midline. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Crossing point with LI, ST and GV meridian. Thirteen Ghost point.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Mental disorders, shock, unconsciousness, coma, heat exhaustion, motion sickness, hysteria, insanity, seizures, convulsions, spasms of the muscles in the region of the mouth or eyes, mouth and eyes awry, lip tremor, apoplectic locked jaw, emaciation and thirst even after drinking, halitosis, nose diseases, twisting pain in the vicinity of the heart and abdomen, edema, facial edema, jaundice, acute lower back sprain.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the lip in the anterior median line of the face at the midpoint of the tubercle of the upper lip.

2. On the face, at the midpoint of the tubercle of the upper lip. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Mental disorders, seizures, lip twitching, lip stiffness, pain and swelling of the gums, occluded nose, rhinopolypus, vomiting, stomatitis.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located inside the mouth at the intersection of the frenulum of the upper lip and the upper gum.

2. On the face, at the junction of the frenulum of the upper lip with the upper gum.
Note: With the head extended in the seated posture and the upper lip lifted, GV28 is located at the junction of the frenulum of the upper lip with the upper gum. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Crossing point with Conception vessel, ST and GV meridian. Exit point.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Mental disorders, rhinorrhea, pain and bleeding around the teeth.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the lower back at the posterior median line in the depression inferior to the spinous process of the 4th lumbar vertebra. Same horizontal position as GV3 and BL25.

2. In the lumbar region, in the depression inferior to the spinous process of the fourth lumbar vertebra (L4), on the posterior median line.
Note: GV3 can be located by first palpating the highest points of the iliac crests and the spinous process of the fourth lumbar vertebra (L4) can then be found at the midpoint of the highest points of both iliac crest. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Continuous vomiting, lower abdominal distension, chronic enteritis, diarrhea, scrofula, impotence, spermatorrhea, vaginal discharge with blood, irregular menstruation, low back pain, paralysis of the lower limbs, numb & stiff lower limbs, pain in the knees.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the lower back at the posterior median line in the depression inferior to the spinous process of the 2nd lumbar vertebra. Same horizontal position as GV4, BL23 and BL52.

2. In the lumbar region, in the depression inferior to the spinous process of the second lumbar vertebra (L2), on the posterior median line. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Tidal fevers, headache, infantile convulsions, sequelae of infantile paralysis, peritonitis, pain of intestinal colic, prolapsed anus, nephritis, enuresis, nocturnal emission, impotence, spermatorrhea, irregular menstruation, vaginal discharge with blood, uterine bleeding, endometritis, leukorrhea, spinal myelitis, low back pain or sprain, sciatica, related pain in lower back and abdomen.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the lower back at the posterior median line in the depression inferior to the spinous process of the 1st lumbar vertebra. Same horizontal position as GV5, BL22 and BL51.

2. In the lumbar region, in the depression inferior to the spinous process of the first lumbar vertebra (L1), on the posterior median line. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Lumbago, stiffness and pain of lumbar vertebra, nocturnal emission, impotence, irregular menstruation, abdominal pain, prolapsed anus, diarrhea, dysentery.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the upper back at the posterior median line in the depression inferior to the spinous process of the 11th thoracic vertebra. Same horizontal position as GV6, BL20 and BL49.

2. In the upper back region, in the depression inferior to the spinous process of the 11th thoracic vertebra (T11), on the posterior median line. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Pain in the epigastric region, hepatitis, jaundice, diarrhea, epilepsy, seizures, low back pain, paralysis of lower limb.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the upper back at the posterior median line in the depression inferior to the spinous process of the 10th thoracic vertebra. Same horizontal position as GV7, BL19 and BL48.

2. In the upper back region, in the depression inferior to the spinous process of the tenth thoracic vertebra (T10), on the posterior median line. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Pain in the epigastric region, cholecystitis, stomachache, diminishing vision, low back pain.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the upper back at the posterior median line in the depression inferior to the spinous process of the 9th thoracic vertebra. Same horizontal position as GV8, BL18 and BL47.

2. In the upper back region, in the depression inferior to the spinous process of the ninth thoracic vertebra (T9), on the posterior median line. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Epilepsy, stiffness of the back, hysteria, seizures, pleurisy, intercostal neuralgia, gastric pain, hepatitis, cholecystitis.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the upper back at the posterior median line in the depression inferior to the spinous process of the 7th thoracic vertebra. In the standing position it is the same level as the inferior angle of the scapula. Same horizontal position as GV9, BL17 and BL46.

2. In the upper back region, in the depression inferior to the spinous process of the seventh thoracic vertebra (T7), on the posterior median line.
Note: The depression inferior to the spinous process of the seventh thoracic vertebra (T7) which is at the intersection of two imaginary lines: the posterior midline and the horizontal line of the inferior border of the inferior angle of the scapula. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Jaundice, cough, asthma, body curled up and lethargic, malaria, panting, pleurisy, fullness in the chest, chest and back pain, intercostal neuralgia, hepatitis, round worm in the bile duct, cholecystitis, stomachache, cold stomach, intestinal noises.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the armpit with the upper arm abducted in the axillary fossa over the axillary artery.

2. In the axilla in the centre of the axillary fossa over the axillary artery. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Entry point.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Angina pectoris, arthritis of the shoulder, chest pain, depression, inability to raise arm, intercostal neuralgia, jaundice, perifocal inflammation of the shoulder joint, dryness of the throat.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1.하완 전면 내측에 있다. 척측수근굴근건(flexor carpi ulnaris tendon) 요측으로 완횡문(palmar wrist crease)에서 위로 0.5寸 올라간 곳이다.
2. 掌後脈中, 去腕五分. [침구대성]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: 心經의 郄穴. 다른이름 - 少陰郄. 石宮.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: 鼻衄, 吐血, 洒淅畏寒, 厥逆氣驚, 心痛霍亂, 胸中滿.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the medial aspect of the upper arm, 3 cun superior to the cubital crease, on the medial aspect of the biceps brachii muscle. One third of HT3 when connecting HT1 to HT3 and dividing it into three.

2. On the medial aspect of the arm, just medial to the biceps brachii muscle, 3 B-cun superior to the cubital crease.Note: With the elbow flexed and the arm abducted, HT2 is located at the junction of the upper two thirds and lower one third of the line connecting HT1 with HT3. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Pain in the cardiac and hypochondriac regions, shoulder and arm, costalgia, icteric sclera.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the anteromedial aspect of the elbow, on the same level as the cubital fossa, right anterior to the medial epicondyle of the humerus. Same horizontal position as SI8, HT3, PC3, LU5 and LI11.

2. On the anteromedial aspect of the elbow, just anterior to the medial epicondyle of the humerus, at the same level as the cubital crease.Note: With the elbow is flexed, HT3 is located at the midpoint of the line connecting the medial end of the cubital crease and the medial epicondyle of the humerus. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Sea point. Water point.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Cardiac pain, absent mindedness, chest pain, debility of the limbs, diseases of the elbow, headache and dizziness, intercostal neuralgia, lymphadenitis, madness, neurasthenia, nodular growths in the neck, psychosis, stiff neck, toothache, ulnar nerve neuralgia, vomiting, spasmodic pain and numbness of the hand and arm, tremor of the hand, scrofula, pain in the axilla and hypochondriac region.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the anteromedial aspect of the forearm, 1.5 cun superior to the palmar wrist crease, lateral(radial) to the flexor carpi ulnaris tendon.

2. On the anteromedial aspect of the forearm, just radial to the flexor carpi ulnaris tendon, 1.5 B-cun proximal to the palmar wrist crease.
Note 1: 1.5 B-cun proximal to HT7, at the same level as the superior border of the head of the ulna.Note 2: 1.5 B-cun proximal to the radial side of the superior border of the pisiform bone. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: River point. Metal point.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Cardiac pain, spasmodic pain of the elbow and arm, sudden loss of voice.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the anteromedial aspect of the forearm, 1.5 cun superior to the palmar wrist crease, lateral(radial) to the flexor carpi ulnaris tendon. Same horizontal position as HT5 and LU8.

2. On the anteromedial aspect of the forearm, radial to the flexor carpi ulnaris tendon, 1 B-cun proximal to the palmar wrist crease.Note 1: 1 B-cun proximal to HT7. HT4 is located at the level with the root of the head of the ulna, HT5, the body of the head of the ulna and HT6, the base of the head of the ulna.Note 2: 1 B-cun proximal to the radial side of the proximal border of the pisiform bone. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Connecting point. Ma Dan-Yang Twelve Heavenly Star points.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Palpitation, dizziness, blurring of vision, sore throat, sudden loss of voice, aphasia with stiffness of the tongue, pain in the wrist and elbow, abnormal uterine bleeding, bradycardia, tachycardia, chest pain, cough and asthma, headache, incontinence, neurasthenia, psychosis.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the anteromedial aspect of the forearm, 0.5 cun superior to the palmar wrist crease, lateral(radial) to the flexor carpi ulnaris tendon.

2. On the anteromedial aspect of the forearm, radial to the flexor carpi ulnaris tendon, 0.5 B-cun proximal to the palmar wrist crease.Note 1: 0.5 B-cun proximal to HT7, at the same level as the distal border of the head of the ulna.Note 2: 0.5 B-cun proximal to the radial side of the proximal border of the pisiform bone. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Cleft point.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Cardiac pain, hysteria, night sweating, neurasthenia, palpitations, pulmonary tuberculosis, hemoptysis, epistaxis, sudden loss of voice.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the ulnar side of the wrist of the palm in the palmar wrist crease, lateral(radial) to the flexor carpi ulnaris tendon. Same horizontal position as HT7, PC7, LU9, LI5, TE4 and SI5.
2. On the anteromedial aspect of the wrist, radial to the flexor carpi ulnaris tendon, on the palmar wrist crease.Note: In the depression radial to the proximal border of the pisiform bone, on the palmar wrist crease. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Source point. Stream point. Earth point. Sedation point.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Cardiac pain, palpitations, irritability, hysteria, amnesia, insomnia, mania, epilepsy, dementia, pain in the hypochondriac region, feverish sensation in the palm, yellowish sclera, absent-mindedness, angina pectoris, excessive dreaming,heart disease, idiocy and seizures, jaundice, neurasthenia, pain in the ribs, panting, paralysis of the hypoglossal muscle, vomiting blood.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the palm, in the depression proximal to the 5th metacarpophalangeal joint between the 4th and 5th metacarpal bones. Same horizontal position as HT8 and PC8.

2. On the palm of the hand, in the depression between the fourth and fifth metacarpal bones, proximal to the fifth metacarpophalangeal joint.Note: Between the fourth and fifth metacarpal bones, where the tip of the little finger rests when a fist is made, at the same level as PC8. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Brook point. Fire point. Ben point(five phases).

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Palpitation, angina pectoris, cardiac arrhythmia, chest pain, difficult urination, dysuria, enuresis, hysteria, incontinence, itching of the groin, rheumatic heart disease, spasms of the little finger, feverish sensation in the palm, pruritus of the external genitalia.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the radial aspect of the 5th finger in the depression, 0.1 cun posterior(into the body) to the radial corner of the little fingernail. At the intersection of the vertical line of the radial border and the horizontal line of the base of the 5th nail.

2. On the little finger, radial to the distal phalanx, 0.1 F-cun proximal-lateral to the radial corner of the little fingernail, at the intersection of the vertical line of the radial border of the nail and horizontal line of the base of the little fingernail. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Well point. Wood point. Exit point. Tonification point. Eight Meeting points(pulse).

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Palpitation, cardiac pain, apoplectic coma, high fever, hysteria, infantile convulsions, pain in the chest and hypochondriac regions, mania, febrile diseases, loss of consciousness.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the sole of the foot, in the depression when the foot is in plantar flexion. It is one third of the web margin when connecting the web margin between 2nd toe and 3rd toe to the heel and dividing it into three.

2. On the sole of the foot, in the deepest depression of the sole when the toes are flexed.
Note: When the toes are flexed, KI1 is located approximately in the depression at the junction of the anterior one third and the posterior two thirds of the line connecting the heel with the web margin between the bases of the second and third toes. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Well point. Wood point. Sedation point. Entry point. Nine points for Recovery Yang. Three Substances points(earth).

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Loss of consciousness, heat exhaustion, hypertension, stroke, insomnia, vertigo, headache at the vertex, mental illness, insanity, psychosis, seizures, infantile convulsions, blurred vision, nosebleed, dry tongue, loss of voices, swollen throat, colic, diarrhea, difficult urination and defecation, edema, paralysis of the lower limbs, soles of feet, hot pain in tips of toes.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the posteromedial of the knee in the popliteal crease, between the semitendinosus tendon and the semimembranosus tendon, just lateral to the semitendinosus tendon.

2. On the posteromedial aspect of the knee, just lateral to the semitendinosus tendon, in the popliteal crease. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Sea point. Water point. Ben point(five phases). Crossing point with Yin link vessel, Thoroughfare vessel and KI meridian.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Mental disorders, diseases of urogenital system, dysuria, hernia, impotence, uterine bleeding, pain in the knee and popliteal fossa, arthritis of knee.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the pubic region, 5 cun inferior to the umbilicus, and 0.5 cun lateral to the anterior median line. Same horizontal position as CV2, KI11, ST30, LR12 and SP12.

2. On the lower abdomen, 5 B-cun inferior to the centre of the umbilicus, 0.5 B-cun lateral to the anterior median line. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Crossing point with Thoroughfare vessel and KI meridian.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Hernia Dysuria, enuresis, incontinence of urine, urethritis, pain of genitalia, nocturnal emission, impotence, spermatorrhea.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the lower abdomen, 4 cun inferior to the umbilicus, and 0.5 cun lateral to the anterior median line. Same horizontal position as CV3, KI12 and ST29.

2. On the lower abdomen, 4 B-cun inferiorto the centre of the umbilicus, 0.5 B-cun lateral to the anterior median line. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Crossing point with Thoroughfare vessel and KI meridian.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Nocturnal emission, impotence, neuralgia of spermatic cord, spermatorrhea, leukorrhea.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the lower abdomen, 3 cun inferior to the umbilicus, and 0.5 cun lateral to the anterior median line. Same horizontal position as CV4, KI13 and ST28.

2. On the lower abdomen, 3 B-cun inferior to the centre of the umbilicus, 0.5 B-cun lateral to the anterior median line. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Crossing point with Thoroughfare vessel and KI meridian.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Abdominal pain, dysuria, urinary tract infection, diarrhea, sterility, irregular menstruation, dysmenorrhea, leukorrhea.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the lower abdomen, 2 cun inferior to the umbilicus, and 0.5 cun lateral to the anterior median line. Same horizontal position as CV5, KI14 and ST27.

2. On the lower abdomen, 2 B-cun inferior to the centre of the umbilicus, 0.5 B-cun lateral to the anterior median line. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Crossing point with Thoroughfare vessel and KI meridian.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Abdominal pain, urinary tract infection, diarrhea, dysmenorrhea, sterility, irregular menstruation, leukorrhea.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the lower abdomen, 1 cun inferior to the umbilicus, and 0.5 cun lateral to the anterior median line. Same horizontal position as CV7, KI15 and ST26.

2. On the lower abdomen, 1 B-cun inferior to umbilicus, 0.5 B-cun lateral to the anterior median line. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Crossing point with Thoroughfare vessel and KI meridian.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Abdominal pain, constipation, low back pain, irregular menstruation.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the lateral to the umbilicus, 0.5 cun lateral to the anterior median line. Same horizontal position as CV8, KI16, ST25, SP15 and GB26.

2. On the upper abdomen, 0.5 B-cun lateral to the centre of the umbilicus. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Crossing point with Thoroughfare vessel and KI meridian.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Vomiting, hiccup, stomach spasms, abdominal pain and distension, enteritis, diarrhea, habitual constipation, pain of hernia.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the upper abdomen, 2 cun superior to the umbilicus, and 0.5 cun lateral to the anterior median line. Same horizontal position as CV10, KI17, ST23 and LR13.

2. On the upper abdomen, 2 B-cun superior to the centre of the umbilicus, 0.5 B-cun lateral to the anterior median line. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Crossing point with Thoroughfare vessel and KI meridian.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Abdominal pain, stomachache, peritonitis, diarrhea, constipation, colic.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the upper abdomen, 3 cun superior to the umbilicus, and 0.5 cun lateral to the anterior median line. Same horizontal position as CV11, KI18, ST22 and SP16.

2. On the upper abdomen, 3 B-cun superior to the centre of the umbilicus, 0.5 B-cun lateral to the anterior median line. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Crossing point with Thoroughfare vessel and KI meridian.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Vomiting, hiccup, spasms of esophagus, postpartum abdominal pain, stomachache, constipation, sterility.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the upper abdomen, 4 cun superior to the umbilicus, and 0.5 cun lateral to the anterior median line. Same horizontal position as CV12, KI19 and ST21.

2. On the upper abdomen, 4 B-cun superior to the centre of the umbilicus, 0.5 B-cun lateral to the anterior median line. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Crossing point with Thoroughfare vessel and KI meridian.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Malaria, vomiting, epigastric pain, pleurisy, emphysema, abdominal distention or pain, borborygmus, constipation.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Anterior and inferior to the medial malleolus, in the depression on the lower tuberosity of the navicular bone, at the border of the red and white skin.
2. On the medial aspect of the foot, inferior to the tuberosity of the navicular bone, at the border between the red and white flesh. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Brook point. Fire point. Opening (master) point(yin heel vessel). Crossing point with Yin heel vessel.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Tidal fevers, thirst and emaciation, diabetes, jaundice, tetanus(cramping), pharyngitis, congested throat, cystitis, diarrhea with intestinal pain and noises, itching in genital region, pruritus vulvae, prolapse of uterus, irregular menstruation, sterility, infantile omphalitis.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the upper abdomen, 5 cun superior to the umbilicus, and 0.5 cun lateral to the anterior median line. Same horizontal position as CV13, KI20 and ST20.

2. On the upper abdomen, 5 B-cun superior to the centre of the umbilicus, 0.5 B-cun lateral to the anterior median line. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Crossing point with Thoroughfare vessel and KI meridian.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Seizures, vomiting, stiff neck, palpitations, intercostal neuralgia, abdominal pain and distension, diarrhea.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the upper abdomen, 6 cun superior to the umbilicus, and 0.5 cun lateral to the anterior median line. Same horizontal position as CV14, KI21, ST19 and LR14.

2. On the upper abdomen, 6 B-cun superior to the centre of the umbilicus, 0.5 B-cun lateral to the anterior median line. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Crossing point with Thoroughfare vessel and KI meridian. Exit point(thoroughfare vessel).

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Intercostal neuralgia, abdominal pain, distended stomach, stomach spasms, chronic gastritis, nausea, morning sickness.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the chest between the 5th rib and 6th rib in the 5th intercostal space, 2 cun lateral to the anterior median line. Same horizontal position as CV16, KI22, ST18 and SP17.

2. In the anterior thoracic region, in the fifth intercostal space, 2 B-cun lateral to the anterior median line. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Exit point.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Cough, asthma, rhinitis, bronchitis, pleurisy, intercostal neuralgia, gastritis, anorexia.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the chest between the 4th rib and 5th rib in the 4th intercostal space, 2 cun lateral to the anterior median line. Same horizontal level as CV17, KI23, ST17, PC1, SP18, GB23 and GB22.

2. In the anterior thoracic region, in the fourth intercostal space, 2 B-cun lateral to the anterior median line. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Cough, asthma, bronchitis, pleurisy, intercostal neuralgia, mastitis.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the chest between the 3rd rib and 4th rib in the 3rd intercostal space, 2 cun lateral to the anterior median line. Same horizontal position as CV18, KI24, ST16 and SP19.

2. In the anterior thoracic region, in the third intercostal space, 2 B-cun lateral to the anterior median line. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Cough, asthma, vomiting, bronchitis, chest pain, intercostal neuralgia, mastitis.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the chest between the 2nd rib and 3rd rib in the 2nd intercostal space, 2 cun lateral to the anterior median line. Same horizontal position as CV19, KI25, ST15 and SP20.

2. In the anterior thoracic region, in the second intercostal space, 2 B-cun lateral to the anterior median line. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Cough, asthma, vomiting, bronchitis, chest distention, intercostal neuralgia, emphysema.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the chest between the 1st rib and 2nd rib in the 1st intercostal space, 2 cun lateral to the anterior median line. Same horizontal position as CV20, KI26, ST14 and LU1.

2. In the anterior thoracic region, in the first intercostal space, 2 B-cun lateral to the anterior median line. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Cough, asthma, vomiting, bronchitis, intercostal neuralgia, accumulation of phlegm.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the chest between the clavicle and the 1st rib, 2 cun lateral to the anterior median line. Same horizontal position as CV21, KI27, ST13 and LU2.

2. In the anterior thoracic region, just inferior to the clavicle, 2 B-cun lateral to the anterior median line. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Exit point.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Cough, asthma, vomiting, bronchitis, chest pain, abdominal distension.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the posteromedial of the ankle, 3 cun superior to the bottom of the foot, at the midpoint between the prominence of the medial malleolus and the calcaneal tendon. Same horizontal position as KI3 and BL60.

2. On the posteromedial aspect of the ankle, in the depression between the prominence of the medial malleolus and the calcaneal tendon. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Source point. Stream point. Earth point. Nine points for Recovery Yang.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Neurasthenia, thirst and emaciation, alopecia, toothache, sore throat, throat blockage, chronic laryngitis, tinnitus, emphysema, nephritis, cystitis, dark urine, enuresis, frequency of micturition, constipation, impotence, spermatorrhea, abcessed breast, irregular menstruation, low back pain, paralysis of lower limb, pain in sole of foot.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the posteromedial of the ankle in the depression, posteroinferior to the medial malleolus, at the attachment of the calcaneus tendon to the calcaneus bone. It is 0.5 cun inferior to KI3.

2. On the medial aspect of the foot, posteroinferior to the medial malleolus, superior to the calcaneus, in the depression anterior to the medial attachment of the calcaneal tendon. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Connecting point.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Spitting of blood, dementia, neurasthenia, hysteria, malaria, asthma, soreness in pharynx, retention of urine, pain in heel.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the posteromedial of the ankle in the depression, anterosuperior to the calcaneal tuberosity. It is 1 cun inferior to KI3.

2. On the medial aspect of the foot, 1 B-cun inferior to KI3, in the depression anterior to the calcaneal tuberosity. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Cleft point.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Myopia, dysuria, amenorrhea, irregular menstruation, dysmenorrhea, prolapsed uterus.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the medial aspect of the knee, 1 cun inferior to the prominence of the medial malleolus in the depression at the inferior border of the medial malleolus. Same horizontal position as KI6 and BL62.

2. On the medial aspect of the foot, 1 B-cun inferior to the prominence of the medial malleolus, in the depression inferior to the medial malleolus.
Note: The corresponding lateral point to KI6 is BL62. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Confluence points of the eight vessels(yin heel vessel). Opening (master) point(yin heel vessel).

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Epilepsy, seizures, hemiplegia, insomnia, neurasthenia, psychosis, eye pain, asthma, tonsillitis, pharyngitis, throat blockage, dry throat, sore throat, edema, frequency of micturition, retention of urine, constipation, pruritus vulvae, irregular menstruation, vaginal discharge, prolapsed uterus, difficult labor.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the posteromedial of the lower leg. When SP9 and KI3 are connected by 13 cun, 2 cun superior to KI3, at the anterior border of the calcaneal tendon, it is 0.5 cun posterior to KI8. Same horizontal position as KI7 and KI8.

2. On the posteromedial aspect of the leg, anterior to the calcaneal tendon, 2 B-cun superior to the prominence of the medial malleolus.
Note: At the same level and posterior to KI8. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: River point. Metal point. Tonification point.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Tidal fevers, absence of sweating, spontaneous sweating, night sweats, febrile diseases without sweating, edema, insanity, abdominal distension, nephritis, urinary dysfunction, urinary tract infection, diarrhea, borborygmus, pus and blood in the stool, orchitis, functional uterine bleeding, leukorrhea, pain of lumbar vertebrae, low back pain, muscular atrophy of the leg.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the medial aspect of the calf, 2 cun superior to the prominence of the medial malleolus at the posterior aspect of the medial border of the tibia. It is 0.5 cun anterior to KI7. Same horizontal position as KI7 and KI8.

2. On the medial aspect of the leg, in the depression posterior to the medial border of the tibial bone, 2 B-cun superior to the prominence of the medial malleolus.
Note: 0.5 B-cun anterior to KI7. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Cleft point(yin heel vessel).

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Retention of urine, diarrhea, constipation, pain and swelling of testis, irregular menstruation, abnormal uterine bleeding, pain on medial aspect of lower limb.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the posteromedial of the lower leg between the soleus muscle and the calcaneal tendon. When SP9 and KI3 are connected by 13 cun, it is 5 cun superior to KI3. Same horizontal position as LR5 and KI9.

2. On the posteromedial aspect of the leg, between the soleus muscle and the calcaneal tendon, 5 B-cun superior to the prominence of the medial malleolus.
Note 1: With the knee flexed and the leg stretched (plantar flexion) against resistance, the soleus muscle can be seen more clearly along the medial border of the tibia bone.
Note 2: At the same level as LR5, on the line connecting KI3 with KI10. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Cleft point(yin link vessel). Entry point(yin link vessel).

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Seizures, insanity, psychosis, colic, hernia, nephritis, cystitis, orchitis, pelvic inflammatory disease, pain along medial aspect of lower leg, spasm of gastrocnemius muscle.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the radial aspect of the 2nd finger in the depression, 0.1 cun posterior(into the body) to the radial corner of the index fingernail. At the intersection of the vertical line of the radial border and the horizontal line of the base of the 2nd nail.

2. Shangyang is on the index finger, radial to the distal phalanx, 0.1 F-cun proximal-lateral to the radial corner of the index fingernail, at the intersection of the vertical line of the radial border of the fingernail and the horizontal line of the base of the index fingernail. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Well point. Metal point. Sedation point. Entry point.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Apoplectic coma, deafness, finger numb, high fever, sore throat, toothache.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the posterolateral aspect of the forearm. When LI11 and LI5 are connected by 12 cun, 2 cun inferior to LI11.

2. Shousanli is on the posterolateral aspect of the forearm, on the line connecting LI5 with LI11, 2 B-cun inferior to the cubital crease. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Abdominal pain, diarrhea, hemiplegia, indigestion, loss of voice, pain in shoulder & arm, paralysis of upper limb(stroke), scrofula(lymph swellings), stomachache, swelling of mandible and cheek, toothache, ulcer, vomiting with diarrhea.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the lateral aspect of the elbow. Midpoint of the line connecting LU5 and the lateral epicondyle of the humerus. In the depression at the lateral end of the transverse cubital crease when the hand is on the chest. Same horizontal position as SI8, HT3, PC3, LU5 and LI11.

2. Quchi is on the lateral aspect of the elbow, at the midpoint of the line connecting LU5 with the lateral epicondyle of the humerus.
Note: When the elbow is fully flexed, LI11 is located in the depression on the lateral end of the cubital crease. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Sea point. Earth point. Tonification point. Thirteen Ghost point. Seven points for CVA. Ma Dan-Yang Twelve Heavenly Star points.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Allergies, skin diseases, dry & parched skin, eyes red & painful, anemia,  paralysis, hemiplegia, high fever, hives, hypertension, little menstrual flow, measles, goiter, nodular growths in the neck, throat blockage, toothache, wind rash, arthritic pain in upper limb.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the posterolateral aspect of the upper arm. 1.5 cun superolateral to LI11 on the lateral epicondyle of the humerus. When the elbow is fully flexed, it is in the depression beyond the ridged muscle of the posterior to LI11.

2. Zhouliao is on the posterolateral aspect of the elbow, superior to the lateral epicondyle of the humerus, anterior to the lateral supraepicondylar ridge. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Pain in the elbow and arm, inflammation lateral epicondyle of humerus, lassitude, spasm or numbness of arm.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the lateral aspect of the upper arm. On the line connecting LI11 with LI15, 3 cun superior to the LI11. When connecting the anterior axillary fold to LI11 by 9 cun and dividing it into three, it is one third of LI11.

2. Shouwuli is on the lateral aspect of the arm, on the line connecting LI11 with LI15, 3 B-cun superior to the cubital crease. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Contracture and pain of the elbow and arm, scrofula, coughing blood, peritonitis, pneumonia.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the lateral aspect of the upper arm. On the line connecting LI11 with LI15, 7 cun superior to the LI11. Superior to the lower border of the deltoid muscle.

2. Binao is on the lateral aspect of the arm, just anterior to the border of the deltoid muscle, 7 B-cun superior to LI11. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Any eye diseases, chills and fever, pain in shoulder and neck and arm, paralysis of upper limb, scrofula.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the anterior aspect of the shoulder in the depression between the anterolateral end of the acromion and greater tubercle of the humerus. When the arm is abducted, two depressions appear, anterior and posterior to the acromion. Anterior depression is LI15, posterior depression is TE14.

2. Jianyu is on the shoulder girdle, in the depression between the anterior end of lateral border of the acromion and the greater tubercle of the humerus.
Note: When the arm is abducted, two depressions appear, anterior and posterior to the acromion. LI15 is located in the deeper depression anterior to the acromion. TE14 is located in the posterior depression. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Crossing point with LI, SI and Yang heel vessel.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Excessive sweating, goiter, hemiplegia, hypertension, inflammation of shoulder joint, pain in shoulder joint, wind dampness in shoulder, wind rash, urticaria.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the shoulder in the depression between the acromial end of the clavicle and the spine of the scapula. Touch the upper border of the spine with the scapula outward and needle to where it stops at the end.

2. Jugu is on the shoulder girdle, in the depression between the acromial end of the clavicle and the spine of the scapula.
Note: In the depression between the two bones lateral to the suprascapular fossa. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Crossing point with LI and Yang heel vessel.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Diseases of the shoulder joint and soft tissues of the shoulder, nodular growths on the neck, pain in the arm & shoulder(frozen shoulder), scrofula, spitting blood.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the lateral aspect of the neck. It is the same level as the cricoid cartilage on the posterior border of the sternocleidomastoid muscle. 1 cun inferior to LI18. Same horizontal position as ST10 and LI7.
 
2. Tianding is on the anterior aspect of the neck, at the same level as the cricoid cartilage, just posterior to the border of the sternocleidomastoid muscle.
Note: Directly inferior to LI18, at the same level as ST10. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Sudden loss of voice, sore throat, scrofula, goiter, tonsillitis.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the lateral aspect of the neck. Same horizontal position as the superior border of the thyroid cartilage, and midpoint of anterior and posterior border of the sternocleidomastoid muscle. Same horizontal position as ST9, LI8 and SI16.

2. Futu is on the anterior aspect of the neck, at the same level as the superior border of the thyroid cartilage, between the anterior and posterior borders of the sternocleidomastoid muscle. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Windows of Heaven points(support the chimney).

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Coughing and wheezing, difficulty swallowing, distension and soreness in throat, excessive mucous, hoarse voice, thyroid surgery anesthesia.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the maxilla, inferior to nose, at the intersection of the vertical line of the lateral margin of the nostril and the horizontal line of the midpoint of the philtrum. 0.5 cun lateral to GV26.

2. Kouheliao is on the face, at the same level as the midpoint of the philtrum, inferior to the lateral margin of the nostril.
Note: 0.5 B-cun laterals to GV26.
Remarks: Alternative location for LI19 - On the face, at the same level as the junction of the upper one third and lower two thirds of the philtrum, inferior to the lateral margin of the nostril. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Polys in the nose, facial paralysis, nosebleed, rhinitis, ulceration of the nose.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the radial aspect of the 2nd finger in the depression distal to the 2nd metacarpophalangeal joint at the border between the red and white skin. The radial end of the biggest crease when hand is balled into a fist.

2. Erjian is on the index finger, in the depression distal to the radial side of the second metacarpophalangeal joint, at the border between the red and white flesh. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Spring point. Water point. Sedation point.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text:
Facial paralysis, fever, nosebleed, sore throat, toothache, trigeminal neuralgia.
It is the place where the biggest wrinkles occur when you bend your fingers.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the maxilla, lateral to nose, in the nasolabial sulcus at the same horizontal position as the midpoint of the lateral border of the ala of the nose. Another theory, in the nasolabial sulcus at the same position as the inferior border of the ala of the nose.

2. Yingxiang is on the face, in the nasolabial sulcus, at the same level as the midpoint of lateral border of the ala of the nose.
Remarks: Alternative location for LI20 - On the face, in the nasolabial sulcus, at the level of the inferior border of the ala of the nose. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Crossing point with LI and ST meridian. Exit point.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Facial paralysis, facial swelling and itching, inability to distinguish odors, mouth and eyes awry, nasosinusitis, nosebleed, rhinitis, round worm in the bile duct, tissue in nose.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. On the line between the LI5 and LI11, 2 cun inferior to the LI11(the cubital crease).
2. Shousanli is on the posterolateral aspect of the forearm, on the line connecting LI5 with LI11, 2 B-cun inferior to the cubital crease. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Abdominal pain, diarrhea, hemiplegia, indigestion, loss of voice, pain in shoulder & arm, paralysis of upper limb(stroke), scrofula(lymph swellings), stomachache, swelling of mandible and cheek, toothache, ulcer, vomiting with diarrhea.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1.  Located on the radial aspect of the dorsum of the hand in the depression proximal to the 2nd metacarpophalangeal joint at the border between the red and white skin with the hand balled into a fist.

2. Sanjian is on the dorsum of the hand, in the depression radial and proximal to the second metacarpophalangeal joint. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Stream point. Wood point.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Eyes painful, inflammation of dorsum of hand, malaria, sore throat, toothache, trigeminal neuralgia.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the dorsum of the hand between the 1st and the 2nd metacarpal bones, but a little bit on the radial side of the 2nd metacarpal bones.

2. Hegu is on the dorsum of the hand, radial to the midpoint of the second metacarpal bone. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Source point. Ma Dan-Yang Twelve Heavenly Star points. Entry point. Four Gate points(qi). Four Command points(face and mouse). Six Command points(face and mouse). Nine points for Recovery Yang. Two command points.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Aborting dead fetus, abortion, common cold, deafness, diseases of the sensory organs, facial edema, facial paralysis, headache, hemiplegia, locked jaw, membrane on the eye, neurasthenia, nosebleed, pain in the eyes, scabies, throat blockage, tidal fevers, toothache, wind rash.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the posterolateral(radial) aspect of the wrist in the depression between the radial styloid process and the scaphoid bone, and also between the extensor pollicis longus tendon and extensor pollicis brevis tendon in the depression anatomical snuffbox, when the thumb is abducted. Same horizontal position as LI5, TE4, SI5, HT7, PC7 and LU9.

2. Yangxi is on the posterolateral aspect of the wrist, at the radial side of the dorsal wrist crease, distal to the radial styloid process, in the depression of the anatomical snuffbox.
Note: The depression of the anatomical snuffbox is formed when the thumb is fully abducted and extended between the tendons of the extensor pollicis longus and the extensor pollicis brevis. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: River point. Fire point.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Deafness, diseases of the soft tissue of the wrist joint, eyes red & painful, headache, inability to flex arm at elbow, infantile digestion, throat blockage (sore throat), tinnitus, toothache.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the posterolateral aspect of the forearm. When LI11 and LI5 are connected by 12 cun, it is one fourth of LI5. 3 cun superior to LI5.

2. Pianli is on the posterolateral aspect of the forearm, on the line connecting LI5 with LI11, 3 B-cun superior to the dorsal wrist crease.
Note: LI6 is located at the junction of the upper three fourths and the lower one fourth of the line connecting LI5 with LI11. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Connecting point.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Facial paralysis, neuralgia of forearm, nose bleed, tonsillitis.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the posterolateral aspect of the forearm. When LI11 and LI5 are connected by 12 cun, it is 5 cun superior to LI5. In the depression on the ridge of long radial extensor of wrist and short radial extensor of wrist when hand is balled into a fist to allow dorsi flection.
