2. Wenliu is on the posterolateral aspect of the forearm, on the line connecting LI5 with LI11, 5 B-cun superior to the dorsal wrist crease. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Cleft point.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Facial paralysis, glossitis, parotitis(mumps), sore throat, stomatitis.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the posterolateral aspect of the forearm. When LI11 and LI5 are connected by 12 cun, 4 cun inferior to LI11.

2. Xialian is on the posterolateral aspect of the forearm, on the line connecting LI5 with LI11, 4 B-cun inferior to the cubital crease.
Note: LI8 is located at the junction of the upper one third and lower two thirds of the line connecting LI5 with LI11, 1 B-cun inferior to LI9. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Abdominal pain, headache, mastitis, pain of elbow and arm, painful eyes, vertigo.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the posterolateral aspect of the forearm. When LI11 and LI5 are connected by 12 cun, 3 cun inferior to LI11.

2. Shanglian is on the posterolateral aspect of the forearm, on the line connecting LI5 with LI11, 3 B-cun inferior to the cubital crease. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Hemiplegia, intestinal noises, abdominal pain, numbness of arms and legs, sprain.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1.  Located on the lateral aspect of the great toe in the depression, 0.1 cun posterior(into the body) to the lateral corner of the great toenail. It is at the intersection of the vertical line of the medial border and the horizontal line of the base of the 1st toenail.

2. On the great toe, lateral to the distal phalanx, 0.1 F-cun proximal to the lateral corner of the toenail, at the intersection of the vertical line of the lateral side of the nail and the horizontal line of the base of the toenail. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Well point. Wood point. Ben point(five phases). Entry point.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Pain of hernia, incontinence of urine, hematuria, orchitis, abnormal uterine bleeding, irregular menstruation, prolapsed uterus, opens the sensory orifices, eliminates dampness.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the medial aspect of the thigh, 3 cun inferior to ST30 over the femoral artery.

2. On the medial aspect of the thigh, 3 B-cun distal to ST30, over the artery. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Retention of urine, incontinence, eczema of scrotum, relaxes the tendons and muscles, lassitude, pain on the medial side of thigh.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the medial aspect of the thigh, 2 cun inferior to ST30 at the lateral aspect of the adductor longus muscle.

2. On the medial aspect of the thigh, 2 B-cun distal to ST30.
Note: LR11 is located lateral to the adductor longus muscle. When the thigh is adducted against resistance with the hip slightly flexed and abducted, the knee flexed, the adductor longus muscle becomes more distinct. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Pain of hernia, tendons problem, disorders of the lumbar spine, pain of the thigh, benefits the uterus and regulates menstruation, irregular menstruation.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the groin region at the same level as the superior border of the pubic symphysis, 2.5 cun lateral to the anterior median line. ST30 is at the superior aspect of the inguinal ligament, LR12 is at the point 0.5 cun inferiorlateral to the inguinal ligament and inferior aspect of the inguinal ligament. Same horizontal position as CV2, KI11, ST30, LR12 and SP12.

2. In the groin region, at the same level as the superior border of the pubic symphysis, and 2.5 B-cun lateral to the anterior median line. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Pain of hernia, dispels cold from the liver channel, penis pain, prolapsed uterus.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the flank just inferior to the free extremity of the 11th rib. Same horizontal position as CV10, KI17, ST23 and LR13.

2. On the lateral abdomen, inferior to the free extremity of the 11th rib.
Note: LR13 can be located while the subject is lying on the side with the shoulder flexed. The free extremity of the 11th rib can be palpated below the inferior border of the costal arch. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Alarm point(spleen). Crossing point with Governor vessel, GB and LR meridian. Eight Meeting points(viscus).

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Pain in the chest and ribs, harmonises the liver and the spleen, vomiting, lumps and distension in the chest due to accumulation of qi, enlargement of the liver & spleen, abdominal distension, hepatitis, enteritis, jaundice becomes black jaundice, yellow skin and dark facial complexion, diarrhea due to cold, turbid and cloudy urine.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the chest between the 6th rib and 7th rib in the 6th intercostal space, 4 cun lateral to the anterior median line. Same horizontal position as CV14, KI21, ST19 and LR14.

2. In the anterior thoracic region, in the sixth intercostal space, 4 B-cun lateral to the anterior median line.
Note: LR14 is inferior to the centre of the nipple, 2 B-cun lateral to ST19. In females, LR14 is located at the intersection of the midclavicular line and the sixth intercostal space. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Alarm point(liver). Crossing point with Yin link vessel, SI and LR meridian. Exit point.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Tidal fevers, chest pain, distension around the ribs, intercostal neuralgia, pleurisy, hepatitis, disperses accumulations, failure to discharge the placenta, harmonises the liver and the stomach, vomiting, enlarged liver, enlargement of the spleen, cholecystitis, nervous dysfunction of the stomach.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the lateral aspect of the great toe in the depression distal to the 1st metatarsophalangeal joint at the web margin between the 1st and 2nd toe at the border between the red and white skin.

2. On the dorsum of the foot, between the first and second toes, proximal to the web margin, at the border between the red and white flesh. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Brook point. Fire point. Sedation point.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text:
Clears liver fire, night sweats, insomnia, headache, spreads liver qi, glaucomas, liver wind, seizures, infantile convulsions, vertigo, intercostal neuralgia, clears heat and blood heat, eyes red and swollen, colic, orchitis, stops bleeding, abnormal uterine bleeding, benefits the lower energizer, loss of urine, cloudy urine or urethral discharge, pain in the penis, pain of hernia.

vomiting

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the back of the foot in the depression between the 1st and the 2nd metatarsal bones, 2 cun superior(to the ankle) to LR2 over the dorsalis pedis artery.

2. On the dorsum of the foot, between the first and second metatarsal bones, in the depression distal to the junction of the bases of the two bones, over the dorsalis pedis artery.
Note: LR3 can be felt in the depression when moving proximally from LR2 in the gap between the first and second metatarsal bones towards the base of two metatarsal bones. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Source point. Stream point. Earth point. Four Gate points(blood). Ma Dan-Yang Twelve Heavenly Star points(later added by Xu Feng).

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Liver wind, hypertension, insomnia, spreads liver qi, vertigo, headache, nourishes liver blood and liver yin, continuous sweating after childbirth, thrombocytopenia, hepatitis, calms spasms, benefits the eyes, pain of the eyes, abscessed breast, mastitis, alleviates pain, sore throat, chest and rib pain, low back pain, arthritis, regulates menstruation and the lower energizer, irregular menstruation, retention of urine.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the anteromedial aspect of the foot in the depression medial to the tibialis anterior tendon, anterior to the medial malleolus.

2. On the anteromedial aspect of the ankle, in the depression medial to the tibialis anterior tendon, anterior to the medial malleolus.
Note: LR4 is located midway between SP5 and ST41. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: River point. Metal point.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Regulates the lower energizer, hepatitis, jaundice, low back pain, pain of the knee or ankle, diseases of the ankle and surrounding soft tissues, lower abdominal pain, pain of hernia, colic, genital pain, nocturnal emissions, dripping urine, retention of urine.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the anteromedial aspect of the lower leg, 5 cun superior to the prominence of the medial malleolus on the medial border of the the tibia. Same horizontal position as LR5 and KI9.

2. On the anteromedial aspect of the leg, at the centre of the medial border (surface) of the tibia, 5 B-cun proximal to the prominence of the medial malleolus.
Note: LR5 is located at the same level as the upper two thirds and lower one third of the line connecting the apex of the patella with the prominence of the medial malleolus, at the centre of the medial border (surface) of the tibia, at the same level as KI9. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Connecting point.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Low back pain, pain of hernia, retention of urine, difficult urination, benefits the genitals, sexual dysfunction, impotence, swollen and painful testicles, orchitis, vaginal discharge, prolapsed uterus, abnormal uterine bleeding, regulates menstruation, irregular menstruation, endometritis.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the anteromedial aspect of the lower leg, 7 cun superior to the prominence of the medial malleolus on the medial border of the the tibia. Same horizontal position as LR6, ST39, GB36, GB35 and BL58.

2. On the anteromedial aspect of the leg, at the centre of the medial border (surface) of the tibia, 7 B-cun proximal to the prominence of the medial malleolus.
Note: LR6 is located at 0.5 B-cun inferior to the midpoint of the line connecting the apex of the patella with the prominence of the medial malleolus, at the centre of the medial border (surface) of the tibia. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Cleft point.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Dampness, acute hepatitis, abnormal uterine bleeding, spreads liver qi, paralysis of lower limb.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the medial aspect of the lower leg, 1 cun posterior to SP9, which is inferior to the medial condyle of the tibia.

2. On the tibial aspect of the leg, inferior to the medial condyle of the tibia, 1 B-cun posterior to SP9. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Liver wind and dampness, strong recurrent headache, arthritis of the knee.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the medial aspect of the knee with the knee flexed, it is in the popliteal crease between the sartorius muscle and the gracilis muscle, medial to the semitendinosus tendon and the semimembranosus tendon.

2. On the medial aspect of the knee, in the depression medial to the tendons of the semitendinosus and the semimembranosus muscles, at the medial end of the popliteal crease.
Note: With the knee flexed, LR8 is located in the depression medial to the most prominent tendon on the medial end of the popliteal crease. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Sea point. Water point. Tonification point.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Diseases of the knee & surrounding soft tissues, knee pain, pain of hernia, benefits the genitals and the uterus, impotence, itching and distension on the genitals, pain in the penis, prostatitis, vaginitis, prolapsed uterus, clears and eliminates dampness and damp-heat from the lower energizer, nephritis, dysentery, painful and rough urination, nocturnal emissions.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the medial aspect of the thigh, 4 cun superior to the base of the patella between the sartorius muscle and the gracilis muscle.

2. On the medial aspect of the thigh, between the gracilis and the sartorius muscles, 4 B-cun proximal to the base of the patella.
Note: With the hip slightly flexed and abducted and with the muscle under tension, the sartorius muscle becomes more distinct. LR9 is located posterior to the sartorius muscle. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Low back pain, retention of urine, enuresis, irregular menstruation.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. It is located on the chest, lateral to infraclavicular fossa, 1 cun inferior to LU2. Between the 1st and 2nd intercostal bone, 6 cun lateral to the anterior midline. Same horizontal position as CV20, KI26, ST14 and LU1.
2. Zhongfu is on the anterior thoracic region, at the same level as the first intercostal space, lateral to the infraclavicular fossa, 6 B-cun lateral to the anterior median line.

Note 1: After locating LU2, LU1 is located 1 B-cun inferior to LU2.
Note 2: ST14, KI26, CV20 and LU1 are located on the transverse line along the first intercostal space. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Alarm point(lung). Crossing point with SP and LU meridian. Entry point.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Cough, asthma, clears heat in the upper energizer, transforms phlegm, pain in the chest shoulder and back, fullness of the chest.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. It is located on the palm in the red and white flesh of the inner side of the midpoint of the 1st metacarpal bone.

2. Yuji is on the palm, radial to the midpoint of the first metacarpal bone, at the border between the red and white flesh. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Brook(Spring) point. Fire point.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text:
Cough, asthma, emotional disturbances, fever, hemoptysis, hoarseness,
infantile malnutrition syndrome, laryngopharyngitis, loss of voice, pain in chest and back, spitting blood, throat blockage, tidal fevers, tonsillitis.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. It is located on the radial aspect of the thumb in the depression, 0.1 cun posterior(into the body) to the radial corner of the thumb nail. At the intersection of the vertical line of the radial border and the horizontal line of the base of the thumb nail.

2. Shaoshang is on the thumb, radial to the distal phalanx, 0.1 F-cun proximal-lateral to the radial corner of the thumb nail, at the intersection of the vertical line of the radial border and the horizontal line of the base of the thumb nail. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Well point. Wood point. Thirteen Ghost point. Exit point.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Cough, asthma, apoplectic delirium, cervical swelling with throat blockage, common cold, fainting, infantile digestion, mumps, parotitis, pneumonia, psychosis, stroke, tonsillitis. It is the depression of the point 0.1 cun into the body from the radial corner of the thumb nail.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. 6 cun lateral to the anterior midline, in the deltopectoral triangle, medial to the coracoid process, as the same level with the inferior border of the clavicle. Same level as CV21, KI27, ST13 and LU2.
2. Yunmen is on the anterior thoracic region, in the depression of the infraclavicular fossa, medial to the coracoid process of the scapula, 6 B-cun lateral to the anterior median line.
- Note 1: After identifying the deltopectoral triangle when the arm is flexed and slightly abducted against resistance, LU2 is in the centre of the deltopectoral triangle.
- Note 2: ST13, KI27, CV21 and LU2 are located on the transverse line along the inferior border of the clavicle. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Risk of pneumothorax.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Cough, asthma, pain in the chest, shoulder and arm, fullness in the chest.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. It is located on the anterolateral aspect of the upper arm, lateral border of biceps brachii muscle, 3 cun inferior to the anterior axillary fold. It is one third of the anterior axillary fold when connecting the anterior axillary fold to LU5 and dividing it into three.

2. Tianfu is on the anterolateral aspect of the arm, just lateral to the border of the biceps brachii muscle, 3 B-cun inferior to the anterior axillary fold.
Note: Longitudinally, LU3 is located at the same level as the junction of the upper one third and lower two thirds of the line connecting the level with anterior axillary fold to LU5. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Windows of Heaven points(celestial warehouse).

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Asthma, epistaxis, pain in the medial aspect of the upper arm. opens the channel and alleviates pain.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. It is located on the anterolateral aspect of the upper arm, lateral border of biceps brachii muscle, 4 cun inferior to the anterior axillary fold. When connecting the anterior axillary fold to LU5 and dividing it into three, it is 1cun inferior to the one third place from the anterior axillary fold.

2. Xiabai is on the anterolateral aspect of the arm, just lateral to the border of the biceps brachii muscle, 4 B-cun inferior to the anterior axillary fold. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Cough, bronchitis, nosebleed, fullness in the chest, pain in the medial aspect of the upper arm, regulates qi & blood, sedates pain.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. It is located on the anterior aspect of the elbow at the cubital crease on the radial(lateral) aspect of the biceps brachii tendon. Same horizontal position as SI8, HT3, PC3, LU5 and LI11.

2. Chize is on the anterior aspect of the elbow, at the cubital crease, in the depression lateral to the biceps brachii tendon.
Note: With the elbow flexed, LU5 is located at the cubital crease, between LI11 and PC3, separated from PC3 by the biceps brachii tendon. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Sea point. Water point. Sedation point.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Asthma(esp. acute), bronchitis, chest pain, cough, erysipelas, fullness in chest, pleurisy, pneumonia, spitting blood, swelling & pain in the throat, swelling and pain in elbow and arm, throat blockage, irritability, person who cries easily, axillary abscess, lymphatic swelling.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. It is located on the anterolateral aspect of the forearm, 5 cun inferior to the LU5(at the cubital crease),1 cun superior to the midpoint of the line connecting LU5 with LU9.

2. Kongzui is on the anterolateral aspect of the forearm, on the line connecting LU5 with LU9, 7 B-cun superior to the palmar wrist crease.
Note: LU6 is 5 B-cun inferior to LU5, 1 B-cun superior to the midpoint of the line connecting LU5 with LU9. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Cleft point.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Absence of sweating, asthma, belching, coughing, headache, hemoptysis, loss of voice, pain in elbow and arm, pneumonia, sore throat, tonsillitis.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. It is located on the anterolateral aspect of the forearm in between the tendons of the abductor pollicis longus tendon and extensor pollicis brevis tendon, 1.5 cun superior to the palmar wrist crease. When cross both hands with 1st and 2nd finger, it is the place where the tip of the 2nd finger touches.

2. Lieque is on the radial aspect of the forearm, between the tendons of the abductor pollicis longus and the extensor pollicis brevis muscles, in the groove for the abductor pollicis longus tendon, 1.5 B-cun superior to the palmar wrist crease. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Connecting point. Confluence points of the eight vessels(conception vessel). Ma Dan-Yang Twelve Heavenly Star points. Four Command points(head and occiput). Six Command points(head and occiput).

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Asthma, blood in the urine, coughing, diseases of the wrist joint, edema of the limbs, facial paralysis, headache, hemiplegia, stiff neck, swollen pharynx/sore throat, urticaria, wind rash.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. It is located on the anterolateral aspect of the forearm in between the radial styloid process and the radial artery, 1 cun superior to the palmar wrist crease. It is 0.5 cun inferior to the LU7, 0.5 cun superior to the LU9.

2. Jingqu is on the anterolateral aspect of the forearm, between the radial styloid process and the radial artery, 1 B-cun superior to the palmar wrist crease.
Note: 1 B-cun superior to LU9. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: River point. Metal point. Ben point(five phases). Horary point.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Asthma, bronchitis, chest pain.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. It is located on the anterolateral(radial) aspect of the wrist on the abductor pollicis longus tendon’s radial fossa in between the radial styloid process and the scaphoid bone, 0.5 cun superior to the palmar wrist crease. It is 1 cun inferior to the LU7, and 0.5 cun inferior to the LU8. In this area, radial artery is palpable. Same horizontal position as LU9, LI5, TE4, SI5, HT7 and PC7.
2. Taiyuan is on the anterolateral aspect of the wrist, between the radial styloid process and the scaphoid bone, in the depression ulnar to the abductor pollicis longus tendon.
Note: On the radial side of the palmar wrist crease, over the radial artery. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Source point. Stream point. Earth point. Tonification point. Eight Meeting points(vessel).

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Asthma, bronchitis, chest pain, coughing blood, diseases of the radial side wrist joint, headache, influenza, pain in the eyes/membrane on the eye, pertussis, pulmonary TB, toothache.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the chest between the 4th rib and 5th rib in the 4th intercostal space, 5 cun lateral to the anterior median line. Same horizontal position as CV17, KI23, ST17, PC1, SP18, GB23 and GB22.

2. In the anterior thoracic region, in the fourth intercostal space, 5 B-cun lateral to the anterior median line. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Crossing point with LR, TE, GB and PC meridian. Entry point. Windows of Heaven points(celestial pool).

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Descends counterflow qi, promotes lactation, eliminates local qi stagnation, intercostal neuralgia, angina pectoris, pain and swelling below the axilla, eliminates excess from the thorax.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the anterior aspect of the upper arm between the long head and short head of the biceps brachii muscle, 2 cun inferior to the anterior axillary fold.

2. On the anterior aspect of the arm, between the long head and short head of the biceps brachii muscle, 2 B-cun distal to the anterior axillary fold. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Unbinds the chest, pain in the chest and flank, angina pectoris, palpitations, nourishes and invigorates the blood, cough, calms the shen, pain along the medial aspect of the upper arm.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the anterior aspect of the elbow at the cubital crease in the depression ulnar(medial) aspect of the biceps brachii tendon. Same horizontal position as SI8, HT3, PC3, LU5 and LI11.
On the cubital crease, the medial side of the biceps brachii tendon. Same level as SI8, HT3, PC3, LU5 and LI11.

2. On the anterior aspect of the elbow, at the cubital crease, in the depression medial to the biceps brachii tendon.
Note: When the elbow is flexed at 45 degrees, PC3 is located medial to the biceps brachii tendon. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Sea point. Water point.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Clears heat, drains fire, fever, heat exhaustion, bronchitis, harmonises the stomach and intestines, acute gastroenteritis, enteritis, diarrhea with vomiting, opens the channel, alleviates pain, chest pain and easily frightened, myocarditis, rheumatic heart disease, pain in the elbow & arm, irritability and fullness.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the anterior aspect of the forearm, 5 cun superior to the palmar wrist crease, between the palmaris longus tendon and the palmaris longus tendon.

2. On the anterior aspect of the forearm, between the tendons of the palmaris longus and the flexor carpi radialis, 5 B-cun proximal to the palmar wrist crease. PC4 is located 1 B-cun distal to the midpoint of the line connecting PC3 with PC7.
Note 1: With the fist clenched, the wrist supinated, and the elbow slightly flexed, the two tendons become more prominent.
Note 2: If the palmaris longus tendon is not present, PC4 is medial to the flexor carpi radialis tendon. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Cleft point.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Tonifies the blood, dispels blood stasis, spasm of the diaphragm, irritability and pain in the chest, chest pain with vomiting, palpitations, angina pectoris, calms the shen, depression, fear of strangers, hysteria, cools the blood, pleurisy, rheumatic heart disease, myocarditis, mastitis.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the anterior aspect of the forearm, 3 cun superior to the palmar wrist crease, between the palmaris longus tendon and the palmaris longus tendon.

2. On the anterior aspect of the forearm, between the tendons of the palmaris longus and the flexor carpi radialis, 3 B-cun proximal to the palmar wrist crease. PC5 is located 3 B-cun proximal to PC7.
Note 1: With the fist clenched, the wrist supinated and the elbow slightly flexed, the two tendons become more prominent.
Note 2: If the palmaris longus tendon is not present, PC5 is medial to the flexor carpi radialis tendon. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: River point. Metal point.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Unbinds the chest, chest pain, clears heart fire, rheumatic heart disease, calms the shen and the heart, seizures, psychosis, insanity, hysteria, palpitations, harmonises the middle energizer, stomachache, vomiting, yellow eyes, transforms invisible phlegm, tidal fevers, malaria, generalized scabies, irregular menstruation.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the anterior aspect of the forearm, 2 cun superior to the palmar wrist crease, between the palmaris longus tendon and the palmaris longus tendon. Same horizontal position as TE5 and PC6.

2. On the anterior aspect of the forearm, between the tendons of the palmaris longus and the flexor carpi radialis, 2 B-cun proximal to the palmar wrist crease. PC6 is located 2 B-cun proximal to PC7. The posterial point corresponding to PC6 is TE5.
Note 1: With the fist clenched, the wrist supinated and the elbow slightly flexed, the two tendons become more prominent.
Note 2: If the palmaris longus tendon is not present, PC6 is medial to the flexor carpi radialis tendon. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Connecting point. Confluence points of the eight vessels(yin link vessel). Six Command points(hear and thorax).

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Apoplexy, migraine headache, tidal fever, calms the shen, shock, seizures, hysteria, unbinds the chest, chest pain, diseases of the chest, spasm of the diaphragm, rheumatic heart disease, palpitations, angina pectoris, harmonises the stomach, abdominal pain, stomachache, vomiting, jaundice, prolapsed rectum, opens the channel, asthma, swollen and painful throat pain, associated with surgery, hyperthyroidism.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the center of the palmar wrist crease in the palmar wrist crease between the palmaris longus tendon and the palmaris longus tendon. Same horizontal position as PC7, LU9, LI5, TE4, SI5 and HT7.

2. On the anterior aspect of the wrist, between the tendons of palmaris longus and the flexor carpi radialis, on the palmar wrist crease.
Note: With the fist clenched, the wrist slightly flexed, the two tendons become more prominent. PC7 is located at the midpoint of the palmar wrist crease, between the tendons of palmaris longus and the flexor carpi radialis, at the same level as HT7, at the proximal extremity of the pisiform bone. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Source point. Stream point. Earth point. Sedation point. Thirteen Ghost point.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Clears heat from the heart, calms the shen, mental illness, insomnia, seizures, palpitations, cools heart fire affecting the bladder, harmonises the stomach and intestines, gastritis, unbinds the chest, intercostal neuralgia, cools the blood, myocarditis, tonsillitis, spitting blood, opens the channel, alleviates pain, throat blockage, pain at root of the tongue, swelling of the axilla, diseases & pain of the wrist joint, damp skin diseases of upper extremities, scabies(calms itching).

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the palm in the depression between the 2nd and 3rd metacarpal bones. Same horizontal position as HT8 and PC8.

2. On the palm of the hand, in the depression between the second and third metacarpal bones, proximal to the metacarpophalangeal joints.
Remarks: Alternative location for PC8 - On the palm of the hand, in the depression, between the third and fourth metacarpal bones, proximal to the metacarpophalangeal joints. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Brook point. Fire point. Ben point(five phases). Thirteen Ghost point. Nine points for Recovery Yang.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Clears heart fire and calms the shen, chest pain, angina pectoris, coma from stroke, frightened fainting among infants, mental illness, hysteria, madness, excessive sweating of the palms, hands tremors, harmonises the middle energizer, ulcerated oral cavity, stomatitis, jaundice, clears the ying-nutritive level and cools the blood, heat exhaustion, inability to swallow food, numb fingers.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1-1. Located on the middle point of the 3rd finger's tip, 0.1 cun distal to 3rd finger nail.(When execute pricking therapy with a needle)
 1-2. Located on the radial aspect of the 3rd finger in the depression, 0.1 cun posterior(into the body) to the radial corner of the middle fingernail at the intersection of the vertical line of the radial border and the horizontal line of the base of the 3rd nail.(When the needle is inserted)

2. On the middle finger, at the centre of the tip of the middle finger. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Well point. Wood point. Tonification point. Exit point.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Expels internal wind, apoplectic coma, strengthens collapsed yang, shock, heat exhaustion, high fever, clears heat especially from the heart and pericardium, angina pectoris.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the ulnar aspect of the 5th finger in the depression, 0.1 cun posterior(into the body) to the ulnar corner of the little fingernail, at the intersection of the vertical line of the radial border and the horizontal line of the base of the 5th nail.

2. Shaoze is on the little finger, ulnar to the distal phalanx, 0.1 F-cun proximal-medial to the ulnar corner of the little fingernail, at the intersection of the vertical line of ulnar border of the nail and horizontal line of the base of the little fingernail. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Well point. Metal point. Entry point.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Fever and chills with no sweating, headache, revives consciousness, opens the orifices, pterygium, deafness, membrane on eye, chest pain, shortness of breath, pain in ribs, jaundice, insufficient lactation, swollen breast, mastitis.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the posterior aspect to the shoulder in the depression inferiorlateral end to the inferior border of the spine of the scapula, 1 cun superior to the SI9. It is under the acromion LI15, TE14, SI10 and SI9, and is in the same line as ordered.

2. Naoshu is on the shoulder girdle, superior to the posterior axillary fold, in the depression inferior to the spine of the scapula. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Crossing point with SI, Yang link vessel and Yang heel vessel.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Hypertension, excessive sweating, chills & fever, hemiplegia, opens the channel and relaxes the sinews, pain in shoulder, perifocal inflammation of shoulder joint, inability to raise the arm, soreness & lack of strength in the arm.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the scapula, one third of SI12 when connecting SI12(the midpoint of the superior border of the spine of the scapula) to the inferior angle of the scapula and dividing it into three. Another measurement is two thirds of SI12, same horizontal position as GV11.

2. Tianzong is in the scapular region, in the depression between the upper one third and lower two thirds of the line connecting the midpoint of the spine of the scapula with the inferior angle of the scapula. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Swelling in the cheek and jaw, severe painful hiccup, fullness in the chest and ribs, benefits the breasts.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the scapula at the midpoint of the superior border of the spine of the scapula. It is the  midpoint between LI16 and SI13.

2. Bingfeng is in the scapular region, in the supraspinatous fossa, superior to the midpoint of the spine of the scapula. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Eliminates wind, opens the channel and the luo vessels, soreness & pain of the scapula, inflammation of the supraspinatus tendon.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the scapula in the depression of the medial end of the supraspinous fossa in the spine of the scapula. It is midpoint in the line connecting SI10 and the spinous process of the 2nd thoracic vertebra.

2. Quyuan is in the scapular region, in the depression superior to the medial end of the spine of the scapula.
Note: SI13 is located at the midpoint of the line connecting SI10 with the spinous process of the second thoracic vertebra (T2). [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Opens the channel blockage conditions, pain in the shoulder and shoulder blade, diseases of the soft tissue of the shoulder joint, inflammation of the tendon of the supraspinatous muscle, muscle spasms.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the upper back at the same level as the spinous process of the 1st thoracic vertebra, 3 cun lateral to the posterior median line. Same horizontal position as GV13, BL11 and SI14.

2. Jianwaishu is in the upper back region, at the same level as the inferior border of the spinous process of the first thoracic vertebra (T1), 3 B-cun lateral to the posterior median line.
Note 1: SI14 is located at the intersection of two imaginary lines: the vertical line of the medial extremity of the spine of the scapula and the horizontal line inferior to the spinous process of the first thoracic vertebra (T1).
Note 2: SI14 is located at the same level as BL11, GV13, and the inferior border of the spinous process of the first thoracic vertebra (T1). [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Expels wind-cold, soreness and pain of the scapula.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the nape of the neck at the same level as the spinous process of the 7th cervical vertebra, 2 cun lateral to the posterior median line. It is at the midpoint between GV14 and GB21. Same horizontal position as GV14 and SI15.

2. Jianzhongshu is in the upper back region, at the same level as the inferior border of the spinous process of the seventh cervical vertebra (C7), 2 B-cun lateral to the posterior median line.
Note: SI15 is located at the intersection of two imaginary lines: the vertical line of the junction of the lateral one third and the medial two thirds of the line connecting the posterior median line with the medial border of the scapula and the horizontal line inferior to the spinous process of the seventh cervical vertebra (C7). [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Fever and chills, cough, stiff neck, pain in the back and shoulder, blurred vision, asthma, bronchitis, bronchiectasis, spitting blood, consumption from milk in infants.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the lateral aspect of the neck at the same level as superior border of the thyroid cartilage, 4.5 cun lateral to anterior median line. At the intersection of the vertical line of the angle of the mandibular and the posterior border of the sternocleidomastoid muscle. Same horizontal position as ST9, LI18 and SI16.

2.  Tianchuang is in the anterior region of the neck, posterior to the sternocleidomastoid muscle, at the same level as the superior border of the thyroid cartilage.
Note 1: The sternocleidomastoid muscle is more distinct when the head is turned to the opposite side against resistance.
Note 2: SI16 is located at the same level as ST9, LI18 and the superior border of the thyroid cartilage. ST9 is located anterior to the sternocleidomastoid muscle, SI16, posterior to the sternocleidomastoid muscle and LI18, midway between the anterior and posterior borders of the sternocleidomastoid muscle. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Windows of Heaven points(celestial window).

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Expels wind and heat, stiff neck, deafness, tinnitus, sore throat, goiter.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the lateral aspect of the neck, 1 cun inferior to the TE17, anterior to the sternocleidomastoid muscle. At the same level as the angle of the mandible, SI17 is anterior to the sternocleidomastoid muscle, TE16 is posterior to the sternocleidomastoid muscle.

2. Tianrong is in the anterior region of the neck, posterior to the angle of the mandible, in the depression anterior to the sternocleidomastoid muscle.
Note: The sternocleidomastoid muscle is more distinct when the head is turned to the opposite side against resistance. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Windows of Heaven points(celestial countenance).

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Expels wind, disperses accumulations, severe cough, deafness, tinnitus,  distension and soreness of the neck, pharyngitis, tonsillitis, throat constricted and difficulty in swallowing, asthma.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the cheek bone at the intersection of the vertical line of GB1 in the outer cantus and the inferior border of the zygomatic bone. It is in the depression inferior border angle of the zygomatic bone.

2. Quanliao is on the face, inferior to the zygomatic bone, in the depression directly inferior to the outer canthus of the eye. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Crossing point with TE and SI meridian.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Eliminates wind, clears heat, alleviates pain, spasm of the facial muscles, facial paralysis, trigeminal neuralgia, reduces swellings.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the ear at the midpoint of anterior to the tragus. It is in the depression between anterior to the tragus and posterior border of the condyloid process of the mandible with the mouth opened. TE21, SI19 and GB2 is placed in order on same vertical line.

2. Tinggong is on the face, in the depression between the anterior border of the centre of the tragus and the posterior border of the condylar process of the mandible.
Note: When the mouth is slightly opened, SI19 is located in the depression anterior to the centre of the tragus, between TE21 and GB2. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Crossing point with TE, GB and SI meridian. Exit point.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Calms the shen, seizures and insanity, inflammation of the external ear canal, otitis media, pus in the ear, deafness, deaf-mutism, tinnitus, toothache, pain in the chest and abdomen.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the ulnar aspect of the 5th finger in the depression distal to the 5th metacarpophalangeal joint at the border between the red and white skin. When the hand is balled into a fist, the two wrinkles mark the distal and proximal to the 5th metacarpophalangeal joint. Distal(finger) to the 5th metacarpophalangeal joint is SI2. Proximal(wrist) to the 5th metacarpophalangeal joint is SI3.

2. Qiangu is on the little finger, in the depression distal to the ulnar side of the fifth metacarpophalangeal joint, at the border between the red and white flesh.
Note: When the hand is slightly flexed, the point is located at the ulnar end of the palmar metacarpophalangeal crease of the little finger. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Brook point. Water point.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Drains heat & expels wind, congested throat, tinnitus, pannus(destruction of joint in rheumatoid arthritis), disperses accumulations, numb finger, mastitis.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the ulnar aspect of the back of the hand in the depression proximal to the 5th metacarpophalangeal joint at the border between the red and white skin. When the hand is balled into a fist, the two wrinkles mark the distal and proximal to the 5th metacarpophalangeal joint. Distal(finger) to the 5th metacarpophalangeal joint is SI2, Proximal(wrist) to the 5th metacarpophalangeal joint is SI3.

2. Houxi is on the dorsum of the hand, in the depression proximal to the ulnar side of the fifth metacarpophalangeal joint, at the border between the red and white flesh.
Note: When the hand is slightly flexed, the point is located at the ulnar end of the distal transverse skin crease of the palm, at the border between the red and white flesh. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Stream point. Wood point. Tonification point. Opening (master) point(governor vessel). Confluence points of the eight vessels(governor vessel).

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Regulates governor vessel(GV), calms the shen, seizures, psychosis, hysteria, madness, deafness, deaf-mutism, tidal fevers, malaria, opens the channel and collateral vessels, night sweats, membrane on the eye, eyes red and painful, jaundice, stiff neck, intercostal neuralgia(posterior), low back pain, finger spasm. tinnitus

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the back of the hand in the depression between the 5th metacarpal bone and the triquetrum bone at the border between the red and white skin.

2. Wangu is on the posteromedial aspect of the wrist, in the depression between the base of the fifth metacarpal bone and the triquetrum bone, at the border between the red and white flesh.
Note: With one finger placed on SI3, push and slide proximally along the fifth metacarpal bone to the bony projection, SI4 is located in the depression between these two bones. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Source point.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Hot condition without sweating, emaciation & thirst, headache, throat blockage, diabetes, cholecystitis, jaundice, gastritis, clears damp-heat in the small intestine, tinnitus, pain in ribs, arthritis of the wrist, elbow and fingers, inhibited movement of fingers.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the posterolateral(ulnar) aspect of the wrist of the back of the hand in the depression between the ulnar styloid process and the triquetrum bone. Same horizontal position as SI5, HT7, PC7, LU9, LI5 and TE4.
2. Yanggu is on the posteromedial aspect of the wrist, in the depression between the triquetrum bone and the ulnar styloid process. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: River point. Fire point. Ben point(five phases).

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Clears heat and reduces swellings, fever, insanity, deafness, innitus, parotitis, wrist pain.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the posterolateral(ulnar) aspect of the wrist on the back of the hand in the depression over the styloid process of the ulnar. When the hand is turned from a pronated position to a supinated position, it is 1 cun superior to the SI5.

2. Yanglao is on the posteromedial aspect of the forearm, in the depression radial to the head of the ulnar bone, 1 B-cun proximal to the dorsal wrist crease.
Note: With the palm facing downwards, press the highest point of the head of ulnar bone with a finger, and then turn the palm towards the chest; SI6 is located at the cleft between the bones where the finger slides. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Cleft point.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Hemiplegia, eye diseases, blurred vision, alleviates acute conditions, pain of hernia, stiff neck, restricted movement lumbar area, low back pain, pain in shoulder and back, arthritis of the upper limb.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the posteromedial aspect of the forearm. When the top of the elbow and SI5 are connected by 12 cun, 5 cun superior to SI5, it is on the line between SI5 and SI8, 1 cun inferior to the midpoint between SI5 and SI8.

2. Zhizheng is on the posteromedial aspect of the forearm, between the medial border of the ulnar bone and the flexor carpi ulnaris muscle, 5 B-cun proximal to the dorsal wrist crease.
Note: 1 B-cun distal to the midpoint of the line connecting SI5 with SI8. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Connecting point.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Calms the shen, neurasthenia, insanity, releases the exterior, stiff neck, pain of the elbow or arm.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the posteromedial to the elbow in the depression between the olecranon and the medial epicondyle of the humerus. When the elbow is slightly flexed, it is in the groove for the ulnar nerve for shooting pain in the elbow to finger. Same horizontal position as SI8, HT3, PC3, LU5 and LI11.

2. Xiaohai is on the posteromedial aspect of the elbow, in the depression between the olecranon and the medial epicondyle of the humerus bone.
Note: When the elbow is slightly flexed, SI 8 is located in the groove for the ulnar nerve. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Sea point. Earth point. Sedation point.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Huntington's chorea, seizures, psychosis, pain of the scapula, neuralgia or paralysis of the ulnar nerve.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the posterior aspect to the shoulder, 1 cun superior to the posterior axillary fold, and posterior aspect to the deltoid muscle.

2. Jianzhen is on the shoulder girdle, posteroinferior to the shoulder joint, 1 B-cun superior to the posterior axillary fold.
Note: When the arm is adducted, SI 9 is located 1 B-cun superior to the posterior axillary fold, posterior to the deltoid muscle. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Excessive perspiration in the armpits, deafness, tinnitus, toothache, swelling of the mandible, expels wind and benefits the shoulder, pain in scapula, pain in arm inhibiting movement, diseases of the shoulder and joint, paralysis of upper limb.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the medial aspect of the great toe in the depression, 0.1 cun posterior(into the body) to the medial corner of the great toenail. At the intersection of the vertical line of the medial border and the horizontal line of the base of the 1st toenail.

2. Yinbai is on the great toe, medial to the distal phalanx, 0.1 F-cun proximal-medial to the medial corner of the toenail, at the intersection of the vertical line of the medial border and horizontal line of the base of the toenail. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Well point. Wood point. Thirteen Ghost point. Entry point.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Abdominal pain or distension, bleeding of the digestive tract, blood in urine or stool, abnormal uterine bleeding, continuous nosebleed, spitting blood, chronic infantile convulsions, mental diseases(well point).

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the anteromedial aspect of the thigh at the vastus medialis muscle, 2 cun superior to the medial aspect of the base of the patella. Same horizontal position as ST34 and SP10.

2. Xuehai is on the anteromedial aspect of the thigh, on the bulge of the vastus medialis muscle, 2 B-cun superior to the medial end of the base of the patella. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Abnormal uterine bleeding, anemia, irregular menstruation, neurodermatitis, pruritis, urticaria.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the anteromedial aspect of the thigh between the adductor longus muscle and the sartorius muscle. It is 12 cun superior to the medial aspect of the base of the patella over the femoral artery. Another theory says 8 cun superior to the medial aspect of the base of the patella.

2.  Jimen is on the medial aspect of the thigh, at the junction of the upper one third and lower two thirds of the line connecting the medial end of the base of the patella with SP12, between the sartorius muscle and the adductor longus muscle, over the femoral artery. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Dysuria, enuresis, urethritis, pain and swelling in the inguinal region, muscular atrophy, motor impairment, pain and paralysis of the lower extremities.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the groin region. 4 cun(or 3.5 cun) lateral to CV2 on the inguinal crease. Inferior to inguinal ligament and lateral to the femoral artery. Same horizontal position as CV2, KI11, ST30, LR12 and SP12.

2. Chongmen is in the groin region, at the inguinal crease, lateral to the femoral artery.
Note: At the same level as CV2, medial and inferior to SP13. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Crossing point with LR, TE, SP and Yin link vessel.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Endometritis, orchitis, pain of hernia, retention of urine.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the groin region. 4.3 cun inferior to the umbilicus, and 4 cun lateral to the anterior median line.
 
2. Fushe is on the lower abdomen, 4.3 B-cun inferior to the centre of the umbilicus, 4 B-cun lateral to the anterior median line. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Crossing point with Yin link vessel, LR and SP meridian.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Adnexitis(PID), appendicitis, inguinal lymphadenitis, pain of lower abdomen, hernia.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the lower abdomen. 1.3 cun inferior to the umbilicus, and 4 cun lateral to the anterior median line.
	 
2.  Fujie is on the lower abdomen, 1.3 B-cun inferior to the centre of the umbilicus, 4 B-cun lateral to the anterior median line. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Diarrhea, constipation, pain in the region of the umbilicus, pain of hernia.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the lateral to the umbilicus. 4 cun lateral to the center of the umbilicus. Same horizontal position as CV8, KI16, ST25, SP15 and GB26.

2. Daheng is on the upper abdomen, 4 B-cun lateral to the centre of the umbilicus.
Note: At the same level and lateral to ST25, KI16 and CV8. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Crossing point with Yin link vessel and SP meridian.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Abdominal distension, cold pain in the lower abdomen, constipation, diarrhea, intestinal paralysis, parasitic worms in the intestines, diarrhea.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the upper abdomen. 3 cun superior to the umbilicus, and 4 cun lateral to the anterior median line. Same horizontal position as CV11, KI18, ST22 and SP16.

2. Fuai is on the upper abdomen, 3 B-cun superior to the centre of the umbilicus, 4 B-cun lateral to the anterior median line.
Note: 3 B-cun superior to SP15, at the same level as CV11. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Crossing point with Yin link vessel and SP meridian.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Constipation, dysentery, indigestion, pain in the region of the umbilicus.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the chest between the 5th rib and 6th rib in the 5th intercostal space. It is 6 cun lateral to the anterior median line. Same horizontal position as CV16, KI22, ST18 and SP17. 

2. Shidou is in the anterior thoracic region, in the fifth intercostal space, 6 B-cun lateral to the anterior median line.
Note: SP17, ST18 and KI22 are located along the curve of the fifth intercostal space. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Ascites, gastritis, intercostal neuralgia, retention of urine.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the chest between the 4th rib and 5th rib in the 4th intercostal space. It is 6 cun lateral to the anterior median line. Same horizontal position as CV17, KI23, ST17, PC1, SP18, GB23 and GB22. 

2. Tianxi is in the anterior thoracic region, in the fourth intercostal space, 6 B-cun lateral to the anterior median line.
Note: SP18, ST17 and KI23 are located along the curve of the fourth intercostal space. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Asthma, bronchitis, hiccup, cough, mastitis.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the chest between the 3rd rib and 4th rib in the 3rd intercostal space. It is 6 cun lateral to the anterior median line. Same horizontal position as CV18, KI24, ST16 and SP19.

2. Xiongxiang is in the anterior thoracic region, in the third intercostal space, 6 B-cun lateral to the anterior median line.
Note: SP19, ST6 and KI24 are located along the curve of the third intercostal space. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Fullness and pain in the chest and hypochondriac region, intercostal neuralgia.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the medial aspect of the great toe in the depression distal to the 1st metatarsophalangeal joint at the border between the red and white flesh.

2. Dadu is on the great toe, in the depression distal to the first metatarsophalangeal joint, at the border between the red and white flesh. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Brook point. Fire point. Tonification point.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Abdominal distension, gastric pain, constipation, febrile diseases with anhidrosis, apoplectic coma, edema of the limbs, fever.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the chest between the 2nd rib and 3rd rib in the 2nd intercostal space. It is 6 cun lateral to the anterior median line. Same horizontal position as CV19, KI25, ST15 and SP20. 

2. Zhourong is in the anterior thoracic region, in the second intercostal space, 6 B-cun lateral to the anterior median line.
Note: SP20, ST15 and KI25 are located along the curve of the second intercostal space. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Bronchiectasis, intercostal neuralgia, pleurisy, cough, hiccup, pulmonary emphysema.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the flank between the 6th rib and 7th rib in the 6th intercostal space. It is 8 cun lateral to the anterior median line. Also, it is lateral to the CV16 and inferior to the GB22 on the midaxillay line.

2. Dabao is in the lateral thoracic region, in the sixth intercostal space, on the midaxillary line.
Note: With the subject lying on the side and the arm abducted, SP21 is located at the intersection of the midaxillary line and the sixth intercostal space. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Great(major) Collateral vessel(spleen). Exit point. Three Jiao problems(upper jiao).

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Asthma, general body soreness, intercostal neuralgia.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the medial aspect of the foot in the depression proximal to the 1st metatarsophalangeal joint at the border between the red and white flesh.

2. Taibai is on the medial aspect of the foot, in the depression proximal to the first metatarsophalangeal joint, at the border between the red and white flesh. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Source point. Stream point. Earth point. Ben point(five phases).

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Gastric pain, abdominal distension, constipation, dysentery, vomiting, diarrhea, borborygmus, sluggishness, beriberi.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the medial aspect of the foot in the depression proximal to the inferior border of the 1st metatarsal bone at the border between the red and white flesh.
, in the depression proximal to the 1st metatarsal bone.

2. Gongsun is on the medial aspect of the foot, anteroinferior to the base of the first metatarsal bone, at the border between the red and white flesh.
Note: A depression can be felt when moving proximally from SP3. SP4 is located in the depression distal to the base of the first metatarsal bone. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Connecting point. Confluence points of the eight vessels(thoroughfare vessel).

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Gastric pain, vomiting, abdominal pain and distension, diarrhea, dysentery, borborygmus.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the medial aspect of the foot. It is anteroinferior to the medial malleoulus at the intersection of the vertical line of the anterior border of the medial malleolus and the horizontal line of the inferior border of the medial malleolus. 

2. Shangqiu is on the medial aspect of the foot, anteroinferior to the medial malleolus, in the depression midway between the tuberosity of the navicular bone and the prominence of the medial malleolus.
Note 1: SP5 is located at the intersection of two imaginary lines: the vertical line of the anterior border of the medial malleolus and the horizontal line of the inferior border of the medial malleolus.
Note 2: SP5 is located posterior to LR4 and anterior to KI6. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: River point. Metal point. Sedation point.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Abdominal distension, constipation, diarrhea, borborygmus, enteritis, gastritis, indigestion, intestinal noises, jaundice, hemorrhoid, pain and rigidity of the tongue, pain in the foot and ankle, diseases of the ankle and surrounding soft tissues, edema.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the medial aspect of the lower leg. 3 cun superior to the prominence of the medial malleolus on the posterior border of the medial border of the tibia. 1 cun superior to KI8. Same horizontal position as SP6 and GB39.

2. Sanyinjiao is on the tibial aspect of the leg, posterior to the medial border of the tibia, 3 B-cun superior to the prominence of the medial malleolus.
Note: 1 B-cun superior to KI8. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Crossing point with LR, KI and SP meridian. Nine points for Recovery Yang. Two command points.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Abdominal pain, colic, abdominal distension, diarrhea, borborygmus, hernia, cloudy urine, dysmenorrhea, irregular menstruation, uterine bleeding, morbid leukorrhea, impotence, failure to discharge placenta, fetal death in uterus, pain in the external genitalia, muscular atrophy, motor impairment, paralysis and pain of the lower extremities, headache, dizziness and vertigo, hemiplegia, incontinence, insomnia.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the medial aspect of the lower leg. 6 cun superior to the prominence of the medial malleolus on the posterior border of the medial border of the tibia. 3 cun superior to SP6.
  
2. Lougu is on the tibial aspect of the leg, posterior to the medial border of the tibia, 6 B-cun superior to the prominence of the medial malleolus.
Note: 3 B-cun superior to SP6. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Abdominal distension, intestinal noises, paralysis of lower limb, urinary tract infection.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the medial aspect of the lower leg. 3 cun inferior to SP9 on the posterior border of the medial border of the tibia.
	
2. Diji is on the tibial aspect of the leg, posterior to the medial border of the tibia, 3 B-cun inferior to SP9.
Note: SP8 is located at the junction of the upper one third and lower two thirds of the line connecting the apex of the patella with the prominence of the medial malleolus. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Cleft point. Three Jiao problems(lower jiao).

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Abnormal uterine bleeding, irregular menstruation, difficult urination, distension of the abdomen and flanks, colic, hemorrhoids, edema, nocturnal emissions.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the medial aspect of the lower leg in the depression between the medial condyle of the tibia and the gastrocnemius muscle. Same horizontal position as SP9 and GB34.

2. Yinlingquan is on the tibial aspect of the leg, in the depression between the inferior border of the medial condyle of the tibia and the medial border of the tibia.
Note: A depression can be felt inferior to the knee joint when moving proximally along the medial border of the tibia. SP9 is located in a depression at the angle formed by the inferior border of the medial condyle of the tibia and the posterior border of the tibia. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Sea point. Water point.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Abdominal pain, ascites, beriberi, diarrhea with undigested food, distension of the abdomen, dysentery, edema, enteritis, nephritis, nocturnal emissions, retention of urine, urinary tract infection, pain of lower back & leg, knee pain, impotence, irregular menstruation, pain of the genitals.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the inferior aspect of the eye in the depression between the eyeball and the infraorbital margin.
With the eyes looking straight forward, it is directly 0.7 cun inferior to the pupil.

2. Chengqi is on the face, between the eyeball and the infraorbital margin, directly inferior to the pupil. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Crossing point with Yang heel vessel, Conception vessel and ST meridian. Entry point.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Acute & chronic conjunctivitis, astigmatism, cataract, color blindness, glaucoma, hypermetropia, inflammation or atrophy of the optic nerve, keratitis, myopia, night blindness, pigmentosa retinitis.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the neck at the same level as the superior border of the cricoid cartilage on the anterior to the sternocleidomastoid muscle. It is midpoint between ST9 and ST11, and the same horizontal position as ST10 and LI17

2. Shuitu is in the anterior region of the neck, at the same level as the cricoid cartilage, just anterior to the border of the sternocleidomastoid muscle. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Sore throat, asthma, cough, diseases of the vocal cords, goiter.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the neck in the lesser supraclavicular fossa at the intersection of the sternal end of the clavicle and the sternocleidomastoid muscle. Same horizontal position as CV22, ST12 and ST11.

2. Qishe is in the anterior region of the neck, in the lesser supraclavicular fossa, superior to the sternal end of the clavicle, in the depression between the sternal and clavicular heads of the sternocleidomastoid muscle.
Note 1: The sternocleidomastoid muscle is more distinct when the head is turned to the opposite side against resistance.
Note 2: ST11 is located superior to the clavicle, inferior to ST9. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Sore throat, pharyngitis, scrofula pain, rigidity of the neck, asthma, hiccup, goiter.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the neck in the greater supraclavicular fossa, 4 cun lateral to the the anterior midline. Same horizontal position as CV22, ST11 and ST12.
 
2. Quepen is in the anterior region of the neck, in the greater supraclavicular fossa, 4 B-cun lateral to the anterior median line, in the depression superior to the clavicle.[WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Meeting point with LI, SI, GB, TE and ST meridian.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Cough, asthma, sore throat, hiccup, cough, intercostal neuralgia, pain in the supraclavicular fossa.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the chest between the clavicle and the 1st rib, 4 cun lateral to the anterior median line. Same horizontal as CV21, KI27, LU2 and ST13.

2. Qihu is in the anterior thoracic region, inferior to the clavicle, 4 B-cun lateral to the anterior median line. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Fullness in the chest, asthma, bronchitis, hiccup, cough, pain in the chest and hypochondrium.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the chest between the 1st and 2nd rib in the 1st intercostal space, 4 cun lateral to the anterior median line. Same horizontal position as CV20, KI26, LU1 and ST14. 

2. Kufang is in the anterior thoracic region, in the first intercostal space, 4 B-cun lateral to the anterior median line. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Bronchitis, intercostal neuralgia, cough.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the chest between the 2nd and 3rd rib in the 2nd intercostal space, 4 cun lateral to the anterior median line. Same horizontal position as CV19, KI25, SP20 and ST15.

2. Wuyi is in the anterior thoracic region, in the second intercostal space, 4 B-cun lateral to the anterior median line.
Note: The second intercostal space is inferior to the second rib which is located at the same level as the sternal angle. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Fullness and pain in the chest and the costal region, cough, asthma, bronchitis, intercostal neuralgia, mastitis.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the chest between the 3rd and 4th rib in the 3rd intercostal space, 4 cun lateral to the anterior median line. Same horizontal position as CV18, KI24, ST16 and SP19.
 
2. Yingchuang is in the anterior thoracic region, in the third intercostal space, 4 B-cun lateral to the anterior median line. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Asthma, bronchitis, diarrhea, intercostal neuralgia, intestinal noises, mastitis.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the chest between the 4th and 5th rib in the 4th intercostal space, 4 cun lateral to the anterior median line. In the center of the nipple (Man’s case). Same horizontal position as CV17, KI23, PC1, SP18, GB23, GB22 and ST17.

2. Ruzhong is in the anterior thoracic region, at the centre of the nipple. 
Note: In males, the centre of the nipple is located in the fourth intercostal space. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Do not insert the needle. Do not execute moxibustion.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Insufficient lactation.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the chest between the 5th and 6th rib in the 5th intercostal space, 4 cun lateral to the anterior median line. Same horizontal position as CV16, KI22, SP17 and ST18.

2. Rugen is in the anterior thoracic region, in the fifth intercostal space, 4 B-cun lateral to the anterior median line.
Note: In males, ST18 is located at the intersection of nipple line and the fifth intercostal space. In females, ST18 is located at the midpoint of the inferior crease of the breast. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Great Collateral vessel(stomach).

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Bronchitis, insufficient lactation, mastitis.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the upper abdomen, 6 cun superior to the umbilicus, and 2 cun lateral to the anterior median line. Same horizontal position as CV14, KI21, LR14 and ST19.

2. Burong is on the upper abdomen, 6 B-cun superior to the centre of the umbilicus, 2 B-cun lateral to the anterior median line.
Note 1: ST 19 is 2 B-cun lateral to CV14.
Note 2: If the infrasternal angle is too sharp and the rib is located inferior to ST19, ST19 can be reached by oblique needling. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Abdominal distension, gastrectasis, intercostal neuralgia, stomachache, vomiting, anorexia.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the inferior aspect of the eye in the infraorbital foramen, directly 1 cun inferior to the pupil.

2. Sibai is on the face, in the infraorbital foramen. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Redness, pain and itching of the eye, keratitis, myopia, facial paralysis, twitching of eyelids, pain in the face, allergic facial swelling, dizziness, headache,  mouth and eyes awry, round worms in the bile duct, sinusitis, trigeminal neuralgia.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the upper abdomen, 5 cun superior to the umbilicus, and 2 cun lateral to the anterior median line. Same horizontal position as CV13, KI20 and ST20.

2. Chengman is on the upper abdomen, 5 B-cun superior to the centre of the umbilicus, 2 B-cun lateral to the anterior median line.
Note: ST20 is 5 B-cun superior to ST25, 1 B-cun inferior to ST19, 2 B-cun lateral to CV13. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Gastric pain, abdominal distension, vomiting, anorexia, acute & chronic gastritis, colic, indigestion, intestinal noises.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the upper abdomen, 4 cun superior to the umbilicus, and 2 cun lateral to the anterior median line. Same horizontal position as CV12, KI19 and ST21.

2. Liangmen is on the upper abdomen, 4 B-cun superior to the centre of the umbilicus, 2 B-cun lateral to the anterior median line.
Note: ST21 is 4 B-cun superior to ST25, 1 B-cun inferior to ST20, 2 B-cun lateral to CV12. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Do not execute moxibustion to pregnancy.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Gastric pain, vomiting, anorexia, nervous dysfunction of the stomach, prolapsed anus, stomach ulcers, abdominal distension, diarrhea.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the upper abdomen, 3 cun superior to the umbilicus, and 2 cun lateral to the anterior median line. Same horizontal position as CV11, KI18, SP16 and ST22.

2. Guanmen is on the upper abdomen, 3 B-cun superior to the centre of the umbilicus, 2 B-cun lateral to the anterior median line.
Note: ST22 is located at the same level and lateral to KI18 and CV11. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Abdorninal distension and pain, anorexia, borborygrnus, diarrhea, intestinal noises, lack of appetite ederna.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the upper abdomen, 2 cun superior to the umbilicus, and 2 cun lateral to the anterior median line. Same horizontal position as CV10, KI17, LR13 and ST23.

2. Taiyi is on the upper abdomen, 2 B-cun superior to the centre of the umbilicus, 2 B-cun lateral to the anterior median line.
Note: ST23 is located at the same level and lateral to KI17 and CV10. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Gastric pain, irritability, indigestion, mania.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the upper abdomen, 1 cun superior to the umbilicus, and 2 cun lateral to the anterior median line. Same horizontal position as CV9 and ST24.

2. Huaroumen is on the upper abdomen, 1 B-cun superior to the centre of the umbilicus, 2 B-cun lateral to the anterior median line.
Note: ST24 is at the same level and lateral to CV9. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Gastric pain, vomiting, chronic and acute gastritis, mania, insanity.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the lateral to the umbilicus, 2 cun lateral to the umbilicus. Same horizontal position as CV8, KI16, SP15, GB26 and ST25.

2. Tianshu is on the upper abdomen, 2 B-cun lateral to the centre of the umbilicus. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Alarm point(large intestine). Three Jiao problems(mid jiao). Do not insert the needle to pregnancy

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Abdominal pain and distension, vomiting, intestinal paralysis, peritonitis, borborygmus, pain around the umbilicus, constipation, diarrhea, roundworm in the intestinal tract, edema, low back pain, dysentery, irregular menstruation, infertility, vaginal discharge with blood.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the lower abdomen, 1 cun inferior to the umbilicus, and 2 cun lateral to the anterior median line. Same horizontal position as CV7, KI15 and ST26.

2. Wailing is on the lower abdomen, 1 B-cun inferior to the centre of the umbilicus, 2 B-cun lateral to the anterior median line.
Note: ST26 is at the same level and lateral to KI15 and CV7. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Abdominal pain, hernia, dysmenorrhea.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the lower abdomen, 2 cun inferior to the umbilicus, and 2 cun lateral to the anterior median line. Same horizontal position as CV5, KI14 and ST27.

2.  Daju is on the lower abdomen, 2 B-cun inferior to the centre of the umbilicus, 2 B-cun lateral to the anterior median line.
Note: ST27 is at the same level and lateral to KI14 and CV5. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Lower abdominal distension, cystitis, intestinal obstruction, retention of urine, dysuria, hernia, seminal emission, premature ejaculation.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the lower abdomen, 3 cun inferior to the umbilicus, and 2 cun lateral to the anterior median line. Same horizontal position as CV4, KI13 and ST28.

2. Shuidao is on the lower abdomen, 3 B-cun inferior to the centre of the umbilicus, 2 B-cun lateral to the anterior median line.
Note: ST28 is 3 B-cun inferior to ST25, 1 B-cun inferior to ST27, 2 B-cun lateral to CV4. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Ascites, cystitis, distension and fullness in the lower abdomen, lack of urine, nephritis, orchitis, pain leading to the genitals, urinary retention.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the lower abdomen, 4 cun inferior to the umbilicus, and 2 cun lateral to the anterior median line. Same horizontal position as the CV3, KI12 and ST29.

2. Guilai is on the lower abdomen, 4 B-cun inferior to the centre of the umbilicus, 2 B-cun lateral to the anterior median line.
Note: ST29 is 4 B-cun inferior to ST25, 1 B-cun inferior to ST28, 2 B-cun lateral to CV3. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Abdominal pain, colic, hernia, dysmenorrhea, irregular menstruation, amenorrhea, leucorrhea, prolapse of the uterus, endometritis, impotence, inflammation of the adnexa(PID).

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the cheek bone. With the eyes looking straight forward, it is at the intersection of the vertical line of the center of the pupil and the horizontal line of the inferior border of the als nasi, on the lateral side of the nasolabial groove.

2. Juliao is on the face, directly inferior to the pupil, at the same level as the inferior border of the ala of the nose.
Note: When looking straight ahead, ST3 is located at the intersection of the vertical line of the pupil and the horizontal line of the inferior border of the ala of the nose. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Crossing point with LI, ST and Yang heel vessel.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Facial paralysis, twitching of eyelids, epistaxis, toothache, swelling of lips and cheek, rhinitis, trigeminal neuralgia.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the groin region at the same level as the superior border of the pubic symphysis, 2 cun lateral to the the anterior median line over the femoral artery. Same horizontal position as CV2, KI11, LR12, SP12 and ST30.

2. Qichong is in the groin region, at the same level as the superior border of the pubic symphysis, 2 B-cun lateral to the anterior median line, over the femoral artery.
Note: ST30 is 5 B-cun inferior to ST25, 2 B-cun lateral to CV2. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Crossing point with Thoroughfare vessel, GB and ST meridian. Points of the Four Seas(sea of water and grain(nourishment)). Do not insert needle.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Colic, diseases of the reproductive organs, disorders related to childbirth, excessive bleeding(digestive), hernia, infertility, pain in the penis or testicles.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the anterior aspect of the thigh in the depression between the rectus femoris muscle and the sartorius muscle and the tensor fasciae latae muscle. It is 15 cun superior to the lateral aspect of the base of the patella, on the line between the anterior superior iliac spine and the upper lateral patellar border. Same horizontal position as CV1.

2. Biguan is on the anterior aspect of the thigh, in the depression among three muscles: the proximal portion of the rectus femoris muscle, the sartorius muscle and the tensor fasciae latae muscle. 
Note 1: With the hip and the knee in slight flexion, and the thigh slightly abducted when resistance is placed against the anteromedial aspect of the thigh, a triangular depression appears. The proximal portion of the rectus femoris muscle is found in the depression between the sartorius muscle medially and the tensor fascia latae muscle laterally. ST31 is located at the deepest point in the depression inferior to the apex of this triangle.
Note 2: ST31 is located at the intersection of the line connecting the lateral end of the base of the patella with the anterior superior iliac spine, and the horizontal line of the inferior border of the pubic symphysis. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Arthritis of the knee, atrophy or blockage of muscles of thigh and buttock, low back pain, cold in the knees, lymphadenitis of the inguinal lymph glands, numbness of the leg, paralysis of lower limb, sinew tension.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the anterolateral aspect of the thigh, 6 cun superior to the lateral aspect of the base of the patella on the line between the anterior superior iliac spine and the upper lateral patellar border. 

2. Futu is on the anterolateral aspect of the thigh, on the line connecting the lateral end of the base of the patella with the anterior superior iliac spine, 6 B-cun superior to the base of the patella. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Eight points for Beriberi.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Pain in the lumbar and iliac region, coldness of the knee, paralysis or motor impairment of the lower extremities, beriberi, urticaria.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the anterolateral aspect of the thigh, 3 cun superior to the lateral aspect of the base of the patella on the line between the anterior superior iliac spine and the upper lateral patellar border. Between the rectus femoris muscle and the vastus lateralis muscle.
