2. Yinshi is on the anterolateral aspect of the thigh, lateral to the rectus femoris tendon, 3 B-cun superior to the base of the patella.
Note: ST33 is at the midpoint of the line connecting ST32 with the lateral end of the base of the patella. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Numbness, soreness, motor impairment of the lower extremities.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the anterolateral aspect of the thigh, 2 cun superior to the lateral aspect of the base of the patella on the line between the anterior superior iliac spine and the upper lateral patellar border. It is between the rectus femoris muscle and the vastus lateralis muscle. Same horizontal position as SP10 and ST34.

2. Liangqiu is on the anterolateral aspect of the thigh, between the vastus lateralis muscle and the lateral border of the rectus femoris tendon, 2 B-cun superior to the base of the patella.
Note: Putting the thigh muscle under tension, the rectus femoris tendon and the vastus lateralis muscle are more distinct. ST34 is located between the muscle and the tendon, 1 B-cun directly inferior to ST33. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Cleft point.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Diarrhea, diseases of the knee & surrounding soft tissues, gastritis, mastitis, stomachache.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the anterior aspect of the knee in the depression lateral to patella ligament between the patella and the lateral condyle of tibia.

2. Dubi is on the anterior aspect of the knee, in the depression lateral to the patellar ligament.
Note: When the knee is flexed, ST35 is located in the depression lateral and inferior to the patella. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Eight points for Beriberi.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Pain, numbness and motor impairment of the knee, leg edema, beriberi.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. On the line connecting the ST35 with ST41, 3 cun inferior to the ST35. 1 fingerbreadth lateral to the anterior crest of the tibia, on the tibialis anterior muscle.
2. Zusanli is on the anterior aspect of the leg, on the line connecting ST35 with ST41, 3 B-cun inferior to ST35.
 - Note: ST36 is located on the tibialis anterior muscle. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Sea point. Earth point. Ben point(five phases point). Lower Sea points of the Six Bowels(stomach). Four Command points(abdomen region). Six Command points(abdomen region). Seven points for CVA. Eight points for Beriberi. Nine points for Recovery Yang. Ma Dan-Yang Twelve Heavenly Star points. Points of the Four Seas(sea of water and grain(nourishment)).

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Gastric pain, vomiting, hiccup, abdominal distension, indigestion, enteritis, constipation, diarrhea, ulcers, asthma, cough, borborygmus, edema, enuresis, general weakness, anemia, beriberi, hemiplegia, hypertension, dysentery, mastitis, aching of the knee joint and leg, seizures, shock, apoplexy, dizziness, insomnia, mania.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the anterior aspect of the lower leg. When ST35 and ST41 are connected by 16 cun, it is 6 cun inferior to ST35 on the tibialis anterior muscle, 3 cun inferior to ST36, and 3 cun superior to ST39.

2. Shangjuxu is on the anterior aspect of the leg, on the line connecting ST35 with ST41, 6 B-cun inferior to ST35.
Note: ST37 is located on the tibialis anterior muscle. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Lower Sea points of the Six Bowels(large intestine). Points of the Four Seas(sea of blood). Eight points for Beriberi.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Abdominal pain or distension, appendicitis, beriberi, deficient, weak conditions of the spleen and stomach, diarrhea, dysentery, enteritis, gastritis, indigestion, sharp pain in the intestines, hemiplegia.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the anterior aspect of the lower leg. When ST35 and ST41 are connected by 16 cun, it is 8 cun inferior to ST35 on the tibialis anterior muscle. Midpoint between ST35 and ST41, it is 2 cun superior to ST37, 1 cun inferior to ST39,and 1 cun anterior to ST40.

On the line connecting the ST35 with ST41, 8 cun inferior to the ST35. 1 fingerbreadth lateral to the anterior crest of the tibia, on the tibialis anterior muscle. 2 cun inferior to the ST37. Same level with ST40.

2. Tiaokou is on the anterior aspect of the leg, on the line connecting ST35 with ST41, 8 B-cun inferior to ST35.
Note: ST38 is located on the tibialis anterior muscle, at the same level as ST40. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Do not execute moxibustion.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Numbness, soreness and pain of the knee and leg, weakness and motor impairment of the foot, pain and motor impairment of the shoulder, abdominal pain.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the anterior aspect of the lower leg. When ST35 and ST41 are connected by 16 cun, it is 9 cun inferior to ST35 on the tibialis anterior muscle, and 1 cun inferior to ST38. Same horizontal position as GB36, GB35, BL58, LR6 and ST39.

2. Xiajuxu is on the anterior aspect of the leg, on the line connecting ST35 with ST41, 9 B-cun inferior to ST35.
Note: ST39 is located on the tibialis anterior muscle, at the same level as GB35 and GB36. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Lower Sea points of the Six Bowels(small intestine). Points of the Four Seas(sea of blood). Eight points for Beriberi.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Acute or chronic enteritis, mastitis, hepatitis, paralysis of the lower limb.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the lateral aspect of the lip. 0.4 cun lateral to angle of the mouth. With the eyes looking straight forward, It is at the point directly inferior to the pupil at the lateral corner of the mouth.

2. Dicang is on the face, 0.4 F-cun lateral to the angle of the mouth.
Note: Lateral to the angle of the mouth, the point is located in the nasolabial sulcus or on the continuation of the nasolabial sulcus. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Crossing point with LI, ST and Yang heel vessel.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Deviation of the mouth, salivation, twitching of eyelids, drooling, eye tic, spasms of the eyelid, facial paralysis, mouth and eyes awry, muteness, trigeminal neuralgia.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the anterior aspect of the lower leg. When ST35 and ST41 are connected by 16 cun, it is 1 cun posterior to the midpoint between ST35 and ST41, 8 cun superior to the prominence of the lateral malleolus, and 1 cun posterior to ST38.

On the line connecting the ST35 with ST41, 8 cun inferior to the ST35, 1 fingerbreadth lateral to the ST38.

2. Fenglong is on the anterolateral aspect of the leg, lateral border of the tibialis anterior muscle, 8 B-cun superior to the prominence of the lateral malleolus.
Note: ST40 is one fingerbreadth (middle finger) lateral to ST38. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Connecting point.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Abundant mucous, amenorrhea, beriberi, cough, headache, swelling of the limbs, vertigo.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the anterior aspect of the ankle in the depression between the extensor hallucis longus tendon and the extensor digitorum longus tendon. It is midpoint of the line between the prominence of the medial malleolus and the prominence of the lateral malleolus.  

2. Jiexi is on the anterior aspect of the ankle, in the depression at the centre of the front surface of the ankle joint, between the tendons of extensor hallucis longus and extensor digitorum longus.
Note: ST41 is located between two tendons on the dorsum of the foot which are more distinct when the ankle is in dorsiflexion, and is at the midpoint of the line connecting the prominences of the lateral malleolus and the medial malleolus. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Fire point. Tonification point. River point.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Pain of the ankle joint, muscular atrophy, motor impairment, pain and paralysis of the lower extremities, epilepsy, headache, dizziness, vertigo, abdominal distension, constipation.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the dorsum of the foot at the joint of the 2nd metatarsal bone and the intermediate cuneiform bone on the highest point of the dorsum of the foot. It is over the dorsal pedis artery.

2. Chongyang is on the dorsum of the foot, at the joint of the base of the second metatarsal bone and the intermediate cuneiform bone, over the dorsalis pedis artery. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Source point.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Facial paralysis, fever, headache, insanity, malaria, no strength in arms or legs, pain on dorsum of foot, toothache.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the dorsum of the foot in the depression proximal to the 2nd metatarsophalangeal joint between the 2nd and 3rd metatarsal bones.

2. Xiangu is on the dorsum of the foot, between the second and third metatarsal bones, in the depression proximal to the second metatarsophalangeal joint. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Stream point. Wood point.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Abdominal pain, conjunctivitis, edema, facial edema, hysteria, intestinal noise.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the lateral aspect of the 2nd toe in the depression distal to the 2nd metatarsophalangeal joint at the web margin between the 2nd and 3rd toe.

2. Neiting is on the dorsum of the foot, between the second and third toes, posterior to the web margin, at the border between the red and white flesh. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Brook point. Water point. Ma Dan-Yang Twelve Heavenly Star points.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Abdominal distension, acute & chronic enteritis, beriberi, blood in the urine, diarrhea, eye pain, “locked” jaw, nosebleed, pain of intestinal hernia, paralysis of the mouth, red and white dysentery, ringing in the ears, stomachache, throat blockage, tonsillitis, toothache-upper, trigeminal neuralgia, wind rash.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the lateral aspect of the 2nd toe in the depression, 0.1 cun posterior(into the body) to the lateral corner of the 2nd toenail. At the intersection of the vertical line of the lateral border and the horizontal line of the base of the 2nd toenail.

2. Lidui is on the second toe, lateral to the distal phalanx, 0.1 F-cun proximal-lateral to the lateral corner of the second toenail, at the intersection of the vertical line of the lateral border and the horizontal line of the base of the second toenail. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Well point. Metal point. Sedation point. Exit point.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Facial swelling, hepatitis, hysteria, indigestion, ischemia of the brain, neurasthenia, tonsillitis.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the jaw at 1.3 cun anterior to the angle of the mandible. It is  in the depression anterior border of the masseter muscle.

2. Daying is on the face, anterior to the angle of the mandible, in the depression anterior to the masseter attachment, over the facial artery. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Crossing point with the LI and ST meridian.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Facial paralysis, trismus, swelling of the cheek, pain in the face, "locked" jaw, parotitis, toothache.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the jaw 1 cun anterosuoperior to the angle of the mandible. It is on the prominence of the masseter muscle when the mouth is closed and the teeth are clenched.

2. Jiache is on the face, one fingerbreadth (middle finger) anterosuperior to the angle of the mandible.
Note: On the bisector of the angle of the mandible. When the mouth is closed and the teeth are clenched, this point is located at the prominence of the masseter and in the depression felt when the clenched teeth are released. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Thirteen Ghost point.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Facial paralysis, toothache, swelling of the cheek and face, mumps, trismus, "locked" jaw, mouth and eyes awry, spasms of the masseter muscle, stiff neck, temporomandibular arthritis.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the lateral aspect of the face in the depression between the midpoint of inferior border of the zygomatic arch and mandibular notch. It is inferior to GB3 at the pivot point when the mouth opens and closes. 
2. Xiaguan is on the face, in the depression between the midpoint of the inferior border of the zygomatic arch and the mandibular notch.
Note: When the mouth is closed, ST7 is located at the depression inferior to the zygomatic arch, directly inferior to GB3. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Crossing point with GB and ST meridian.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Deafness, tinnitus, otorrhea, toothache, facial paralysis, pain of the face, motor impairment of the jaw.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the lateral aspect of the head. It is 0.5 cun superior to the anterior hairline at the corner of the forehead, 0.5 cun superior to the anterior hairline, and 4.5 cun lateral to the anterior median line. Same horizontal position as GV24, BL3, BL4, GB15, GB13 and ST8.

2. Touwei is on the head, 0.5 B-cun directly superior to the anterior hairline at the corner of the forehead, 4.5 B-cun lateral to the anterior median line. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Crossing point with GB and ST meridian.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Headache, blurring of vision, ophthalmalgia, lacrimation, migraine headache, psychosis, sore eyes with excessive tearing, spasms of the eyelid.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the neck at the same level as the superior border of the thyroid cartilage, 1.5 cun lateral to anterior median line. It is over the carotid artery, anterior to the sternocleidomastoid muscle. Same horizontal position as LI8, SI16 and ST9.

2. Renying is in the anterior region of the neck, at the same level as the superior border of the thyroid cartilage, anterior to the sternocleidomastoid muscle, over the common carotid artery.
Note 1: The sternocleidomastoid muscle is more distinct when the head is turned to the opposite side against resistance.
Note 2: ST9 is located at the same level as LI18, SI16 and the superior border of the thyroid cartilage. ST9 is located anterior to the sternocleidomastoid muscle, and SI16, posterior to the sternocleidomastoid muscle and LI18, between the anterior and posterior borders of the sternocleidomastoid muscle. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Windows of Heaven points(celestial five-fold confluence). Sea of Energy. Crossing point with GB and ST meridian. Points of the Four Seas(sea of qi).

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Sore throat, asthma, goiter, dizziness, flushing of the face, cough & wheezing, high or low blood pressure, scrofula, speech impediment, swellings on the neck.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the ulnar aspect of the 4th finger in the depression, 0.1 cun posterior(into the body) to the ulnar corner of the ring fingernail at the intersection of the vertical line of the radial border and the horizontal line of the base of the 4th nail.

2. On the ring finger, ulnar to the distal phalanx, 0.1 F-cun proximal to the ulnar corner of the fingernail, at the intersection of the vertical line of the ulnar side of the nail and the horizontal line of the base of the fingernail. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Well point. Metal point. Entry point.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Clears heat from the upper energizer, fever, headache, conjunctivitis, laryngitis, benefits the ears and tongue, opens the channel and alleviates pain.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the posterior aspect of the upper arm, 1 cun superior to the prominence of the olecranon in the line connecting the prominence of the olecranon with the acromial angle.

2. On the posterior aspect of the elbow, in the depression 1 B-cun proximal to the prominence of the olecranon.
Note: When the elbow is flexed, TE10 is located in the olecranon fossa. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Sea point. Earth point. Sedation point.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Regulates and descends the qi, migraine headache, headache, deafness, clears heat from the channel, tidal fevers, tonsillitis, calms the shen, insanity, transforms phlegm and disperses accumulations, alleviates pain, throat blockage, pain in the eyes, pain in neck, shoulder and back, diseases of the soft tissue of the elbow, scrofula, urticaria.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1.  Located on the posterior aspect of the upper arm, 2 cun superior to the prominence of the olecranon in the line connecting the prominence of the olecranon with the acromial angle.

2. On the posterior aspect of the arm, on the line connecting the prominence of olecranon with the acromial angle, 2 B-cun proximal to the prominence of the olecranon.
Note: With the elbow extended, 2 B-cun superior to the prominence of the olecranon. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Dispels wind-damp, clears damp-heat, headache, pain of the eyes, pain of the shoulder and arm.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the posterior aspect of the upper arm, 5 cun superior to the prominence of the olecranon in the line connecting the prominence of the olecranon with the acromial angle.

2. On the posterior aspect of the arm, on the line connecting the prominence of the olecranon with the acromial angle, 5 B-cun proximal to the prominence of the olecranon. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Headache, toothache, stiff neck, pain of the arm, seizures.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the posterior aspect of the upper arm, 3 cun inferior to the prominence of the olecranon in the line connecting the prominence of the olecranon with the acromial angle. It is at the intersection of the horizontal line of the posterior axillary fold and the inferior border of the deltoid muscle.

2. On the posterior aspect of the arm, posteroinferior to the border of the deltoid muscle, 3 B-cun inferior to the acromial angle. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Crossing point with Yang link vessel, GB and TE merdian.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Regulates the qi flow and transforms phlegm, goiter, alleviates pain, pain of the arm and shoulder.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the posterior aspect of the shoulder in the depression between the acromial angle and the greater tubercle of the humerus. When the arm is abducted, two depressions appear, anterior and posterior to the acromion, the anterior depression is LI15, while the posterior depression is TE14.

2. On the shoulder girdle, in the depression between the acromial angle and the greater tubercle of the humerus.
Note: When the elbow is flexed and the arm is abducted, two depressions appear respectively anterior and posterior to the acromion. LI15 is located in the anterior one, deeper than the posterior one, in which TE14 is located. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Benefits the shoulder joint, disperses wind and dampness, alleviates pain.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the scapula in the depression at the superior angle of the scapula. At the midpoint between GB21 and SI13.

2. In the scapular region, in the depression superior to the superior angle of the scapula.
Note: With the upper limb hanging by the side of trunk in a seated position, TE15 is located midway between GB21 and SI13. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Crossing point with Yang link vessel, GB and TE meridian.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Fever, opens the channel and alleviates pain, pain or soreness in the region of the scapula and back of the neck, inflammation of the supraspinatous tendon, dispels especially wind-damp, unbinds the chest.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the lateral aspect of the neck, 1 cun inferior to the TE17, posterior to the sternocleidomastoid muscle. Same level as the angle of the mandible, SI17 is anterior to the sternocleidomastoid muscle, TE16 is posterior to the sternocleidomastoid muscle.

2. In the anterior region of the neck, at the same level as the angle of the mandible, in the depression posterior to the sternocleidomastoid muscle. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Windows of Heaven points(celestial orbit).

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Descends the qi, expels wind, excessive dreaming, stiff neck, benefits the head and sensory organs, deafness, sudden deafness, tinnitus, opens the channel and alleviates pain, sore eyes, sore throat, constricted throat, scrofula.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the lateral aspect of the neck at the posterior to the ear lobe, it is in the depression between the mastoid process and the mandibular angle.

2. In the anterior region of the neck, posterior to the ear lobe, in the depression anterior to the inferior end of the mastoid process. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Crossing point with GB and TE meridian.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Expels wind, facial paralysis, alleviates pain, membrane over the eye, sore eyes, blurred vision, mouth and eyes awry, locked jaw, toothache, clears heat, temporomandibular arthritis, parotitis, swelling in the cheeks, benefits the ears, deafness, deaf-mutism, tinnitus.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the posterolatral aspect of the head when connecting TE17, TE18, TE19 and TE20 as arching shape and dividing it into three, it is two thirds of TE20 at the center of the mastoid process.

2. On the head, at the centre of the mastoid process, at the junction of the upper two thirds and lower one third of the curved line from TE17 to TE20. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Opens the channel, alleviates pain, headache, benefits the ears, deafness, tinnitus, dispels wind, infantile convulsions.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the posterolatral aspect of the head when connecting TE17, TE18, TE19 and TE20 in an arching shape and dividing it into three. It is one third of TE20.

2. On the head, at the junction of the upper one third and lower two thirds of the curved line from TE17 to TE20. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Dispels wind, benefits the ear, clears heat, tinnitus, ear ache, otitis media, opens the channel, headache, vomiting.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the ulnar aspect of the 4th finger in the depression distal to the 4th metacarpophalangeal joint at the border between the red and white skin on the web margin between 4th and 5th finger.

2. On the dorsum of the hand, in the depression superior to the web margin between the ring and little fingers, at the border between the red and white flesh. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Brook point. Water point.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Benefits the ears and calms the shen, deafness, clears heat from the upper energizer, headache, laryngopharyngitis, malaria, opens the channel and alleviates pain, pain of the hand & arm, pain & swelling of the fingers.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the temporal region of the head when folding the ear to anterior where the auricular apex touches the head. Same horizontal position as GV17, BL9, GB19 and TE20. When the mouth is opened, the temporal muscle moves, and at this time, the point is absent from the place where the gap is formed.

2. On the head, just superior to the auricular apex.
Note: With the auricle folded forward and pressed against the head, the point is located where the auricular apex touches the head. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Crossing point with GB, SI and TE meridian.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Benefits the ears and the eyes, red and swollen earlobe, pannus, clears heat, toothache, parotitis.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the ear at the anterior to the limb of helix in the depression between anterior to the tragus and posterior border of the condyloid process of the mandible when the mouth is opened. TE21, SI19 and GB2 are placed in order on the same vertical line.

2. On the face, in the depression between the supratragic notch and the condylar process of the mandible.
Note: When the mouth is slightly opened, TE21 is located in the depression anterior to the supratragic notch, directly superior to SI19. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Clears heat, temporomandibular arthritis, pain in the jaw and headache, toothache, benefits the ears, otitis media, pus in the ear, deafness, deaf-mutism, tinnitus.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Anterior and superior to the TE21, between the root of the auricle and the posterior border of the circum auricular temporal hairline. In the depression the superficial temporal artery passes.
2. On the head, posterior to the temple hairline, anterior to the auricular root, posterior to the superficial temporal artery. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Crossing point with SI, GB and TE meridian.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Dispels wind, facial paralysis, headache, tinnitus, “locked” jaw.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the eyebrow in the depression at the lateral end of the eyebrow.

2. Located on the head in the depression at the lateral end of the eyebrow.
Note: TE23 is superior to GB1. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Crossing point with GB and TE meridian. Exit point.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Alleviates pain, lateral and midline headaches, headache, benefits the eyes, eye diseases, blurred vision, reddened eyes, ingrown eyelash, eliminates wind, facial paralysis, seizures, insanity, vertigo.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1-1. Located on the back of the hand between the 4th and 5th metacarpal bones in the depression, 1 cun proximal to the 4th metacarpophalangeal joint.
1-2. Located on the back of the hand, 1 cun posterior(to wrist) to TE2.

2. On the dorsum of the hand, between the fourth and fifth metacarpal bones, in the depression proximal to the fourth metacarpophalangeal joint. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Stream point. Wood point. Tonification point.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Benefits the ears, deafness, deaf-mutism, tinnitus, clears heat, drains fire, clears the head and the eyes, headache, blurred vision, intercostal neuralgia, alleviates pain, pain in shoulder, back, elbow & arm, inability to bend fingers.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. On the transverse crease of the back region of the wrist, between the tendons of the extensor digitorum and the extensor digiti minimi muscles. Same level as TE4, SI5, HT7, PC7, LU9 and LI5.
2. On the posterior aspect of the wrist, in the depression ulnar to the extensor digitorum tendon, on the dorsal wrist crease.
 Note 1: TE4 can be palpated when moving proximally along the gap between the fifth and fourth metacarpal bones, at the same level as LI5 and SI5.
 Note 2: When the wrist is extended against resistance, the extensor digitorum tendon can be palpated more easily. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Source point.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Clears heat, common cold, tidal fevers, thirst and dryness in mouth, malaria, red eyes and swollen, opens the channel, throat blockage, tonsillitis, deafness, relaxes the tendons, pain and diseases of soft tissues of wrist.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the posterior aspect of the forearm between the ulna and the radius when the prominence of the olecranon and TE4 are connected by 12 cun, 2 cun superior to TE4. Same horizontal position as TE5 and PC6.

2. On the posterior aspect of the forearm, midpoint of the interosseous space between the radius and the ulna, 2 B-cun proximal to the dorsal wrist crease.
Note: 2 B-cun proximal to TE4, in the depression between the radius and the ulna. The anterior point corresponding to TE5 is PC6. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Connecting point. Confluence points of the eight vessels(yang link vessel).

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Expels wind, hemiplegia, paralysis, hand tremors, common cold, benefits the head and ears, migraine headache, deafness, tinnitus, opens the channel, pneumonia, swollen throat, alleviates pain, pain in the ribs, stiff neck, pain in joints of upper limb, pain in fingers inhibiting grasp, clears heat, high fever, febrile diseases, parotitis, opens and regulates yang link vessel, constipation(TE6 used more), enuresis.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the posterior aspect of the forearm between the ulna and the radius when the prominence of the olecranon and TE4 are connected by 12 cun, 3 cun superior to TE4. Same horizontal position as TE6 and TE7.

2. On the posterior aspect of the forearm, midpoint of the interosseous space between the radius and the ulna, 3 B-cun proximal to the dorsal wrist crease.
Note: 1 B-cun proximal to TE5, between the radius and the ulna, at the same level as TE7. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: River point. Fire point. Ben point(five phases). Six Command points(lips and axillary).

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Benefits the lateral costal region, acute pain in the ribs & axilla, intercostal neuralgia, chest pain, angina pectoris, pleurisy, clears heat in the triple energizer, soreness and heaviness in the shoulder and arm, pain in shoulder and arm, regulates the qi, belching, promotes bowel movements, vomiting and diarrhea, constipation, habitual constipation, benefits the voice, swollen throat, opens the channel, insufficient lactation.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the posterior aspect of the forearm when the prominence of the olecranon and TE4 are connected by 12 cun in the depression, 3 cun superior and lateral(ulnar) to TE4. Same horizontal position as TE6 and TE7.

2. On the posterior aspect of the forearm, just radial to the ulna, 3 B-cun proximal to the dorsal wrist crease.
Note: TE7 is ulnar to TE6. [WHO]

sections.name: Classification
sections.text: Cleft point.

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Benefits the ears, deafness, alleviates pain, pain of the arm, opens the channel, seizures.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the posterior aspect of the forearm between the ulna and the radius when the prominence of the olecranon and TE4 are connected by 12 cun, 4 cun superior to TE4. It is one third of TE4 when connecting the prominence of the olecranon to TE4 and dividing it into three.

2. On the posterior aspect of the forearm, midpoint of the interosseous space between the radius and the ulna, 4 B-cun proximal to the dorsal wrist crease.
Note: At the junction of the upper two thirds and lower one third of the line connecting TE4 with the tip of the elbow. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Benefits the ears and the voice, deafness, aphasia, sudden muteness, alleviates pain, post-operative pain associated with pneumonectomy, pain in forearm inhibiting movement, pain in the arm.

sections.name: Location
sections.text:
1. Located on the posterior aspect of the forearm between the ulna and the radius when the prominence of the olecranon and TE4 are connected by 12 cun, 7 cun superior to TE4. It is 1 cun superior to the midpoint of the line connecting the prominence of the olecranon with TE4.

2. On the posterior aspect of the forearm, midpoint of the interosseous space between the radius and the ulna, 5 B-cun distal to the prominence of the olecranon. [WHO]

sections.name: Indications
sections.text: Neurasthenia, headache, paralysis of upper limb, pain in forearm, benefits the ears and throat, vertigo, deafness, sudden deafness, obstructed pharynx, loss of voice, toothache in the lower jaw, nephritis.
